name: A. Lange & Söhne
tagline: Saxon haute horlogerie reborn in Glashütte after the fall of the Berlin Wall
summary: A. Lange & Söhne is Germany's most celebrated watchmaker, famous for its lavishly hand-finished German silver movements, outsize date and the Lange 1. Revived in 1990 and owned by Richemont since 2000, it is widely regarded as a peer of Patek Philippe in movement finishing.
history:
Ferdinand Adolph Lange, a Dresden-trained watchmaker, set up a workshop in the impoverished Saxon mining town of Glashütte in 1845 with government support, training local apprentices and effectively founding the German precision watch industry. His sons joined the business, and the firm became known for its pocket watches, the three-quarter plate and a distinctly Saxon approach to movement construction.

The company thrived into the 20th century, supplying pilots' observation watches during the Second World War. On the last day of the war in Europe, 8 May 1945, the main factory building was destroyed in a Soviet air raid. In 1948 the East German state expropriated the firm and folded it into the nationalised VEB Glashütter Uhrenbetriebe, and the Lange name disappeared for over four decades.

After German reunification, Walter Lange, great-grandson of the founder, teamed up with IWC and Jaeger-LeCoultre chief Günter Blümlein to re-register Lange Uhren GmbH on 7 December 1990. The first new collection of four watches, including the Lange 1 with its off-centre dial and patented outsize date, was unveiled in October 1994 and instantly established the revived brand at the top tier.

The manufacture passed to Richemont in 2000 when the group bought Les Manufactures Horlogères from Mannesmann. Since then Lange has produced landmark pieces such as the Datograph, the digital-display Zeitwerk (2009) and, in 2019, its first sports watch, the Odysseus. Every movement is assembled twice and finished to exceptionally high standards, including hand-engraved balance cocks.

name: Accutron
tagline: The humming tuning-fork watch of the Space Age, reborn with electrostatic power
summary: Accutron began in 1960 as Bulova's revolutionary tuning-fork watch, the first electronic wristwatch to go mainstream and a fixture of the US space programme. Relaunched in 2020 as a standalone brand under Citizen, it now makes the Spaceview 2020 and DNA with the world's first electrostatic-powered movement.
history:
Accutron was born from the work of Swiss engineer Max Hetzel, who joined Bulova in the 1950s and developed a watch regulated by a 360 Hz tuning fork instead of a balance wheel. Launched in 1960, the Accutron 214 was guaranteed accurate to within a minute a month, far better than mechanical watches, and it famously hummed rather than ticked. The see-through Spaceview version, originally a display model for jewelers, became an icon.

Accutron's precision made it valuable to NASA: Accutron movements were used in spacecraft instruments and timers, and the Accutron Astronaut GMT was issued to test pilots. Quartz technology, arriving from 1969, made the tuning fork obsolete by the late 1970s, and the Accutron name became a line within Bulova's catalogue.

In 2020 Bulova, by then owned by Citizen, relaunched Accutron as a separate luxury brand. Its flagship Spaceview 2020 used a new electrostatic movement developed with Citizen, in which the wearer's motion spins turbines that generate electrostatic energy. Since then the brand has added the angular DNA, the Spaceview Evolution, Legacy reissues of 1960s–70s designs, a new Astronaut GMT and, most recently, a limited Spaceview 314 powered by a tuning-fork movement.

2020: first watch movement powered by electrostatic energy

name: Akrivia (Rexhep Rexhepi)
tagline: A Kosovo-born prodigy's Geneva atelier, making modern chronometers by hand
summary: Atelier Akrivia, now presented under its founder's name Rexhep Rexhepi, was founded in Geneva in 2012. Its Chronomètre Contemporain won the GPHG Men's Watch prize in 2018, and its successor won again in 2022, making Rexhepi one of the most sought-after independents of his generation.
history:
Rexhep Rexhepi was born in Kosovo and moved to Switzerland at age 11. At 15 he began a five-year apprenticeship at Patek Philippe, then worked with several leading Geneva watchmakers before founding his own atelier in 2012, aged 25. He named it Akrivia, from the Greek word for precision.

The first watch, the AK-01 Tourbillon Monopusher Chronograph (2013), was followed by further tourbillon pieces including a chiming jump hour and regulator, and the AK-06, the first Akrivia without a tourbillon. The breakthrough came in 2018 with the Chronomètre Contemporain, a time-only watch with a white grand feu enamel dial, a hand-finished in-house movement and a case by Jean-Pierre Hagmann; it won the GPHG Men's Watch prize. The Chronomètre Contemporain II, with dead-beat seconds and twin barrels, won the same prize in 2022.

The atelier moved to Geneva's Old Town in 2017 and has gradually brought micromechanics (2019), leatherwork (2023) and grand feu enamelling (2024) in-house. A collaboration with Louis Vuitton produced the LVRR-01, and the brand now presents itself under Rexhep Rexhepi's own name. Production is tiny and demand vastly exceeds supply.

name: Alpina
tagline: Swiss sports watches born in the Alps, from pilot's watches to divers
summary: Alpina is a sports-watch brand with roots in the 1883 Swiss Watchmakers Corporation, known for the 1938 Alpina 4 and for pilot's and dive watches. Revived by Frederique Constant in 2002, it has been owned by Citizen since 2016.
history:
Alpina traces its origins to 1883, when watchmaker Gottlieb Hauser founded the Swiss Watchmakers Corporation, a cooperative of independent watchmakers and suppliers. The group grew into Alpina Union Horlogère, one of the larger Swiss watch associations of the early 20th century, with a presence in Switzerland and Germany, where its German branch had factories in Glashütte.

In 1938 Alpina introduced the Alpina 4, a sports watch built around four principles: an antimagnetic movement, shock resistance, water resistance and a stainless-steel case. It became the basis for Alpina's later sports and dive watches, including the Seastrong divers. Alpina also made pilot's watches, and its German branch produced aviation watches in the 1930s. After the Second World War the German operation was separated and later became the Dugena brand, and as the quartz crisis deepened Alpina largely disappeared from view.

The brand was revived in 2002 when Peter and Aletta Stas, founders of Frederique Constant, acquired it. They repositioned Alpina as a Swiss sports-watch brand focused on mountaineering, aviation and diving, with collections such as the Alpiner, Startimer and Seastrong, and introduced in-house calibres developed alongside Frederique Constant's manufacture in Plan-les-Ouates. In 2016 both brands were sold to Japan's Citizen.

Alpina drew attention with the AlpinerX outdoor smartwatch in 2018 and, in 2020, with the Alpiner Extreme, an integrated-bracelet sports watch inspired by its 1970s designs. Recent models include solar Solarmetre versions and the 39mm Seastrong Diver Extreme. Alpina's watches carry a red triangle logo that represents the Alps.

name: Andersen Genève
tagline: Geneva's world-time specialist, founded by an AHCI co-founder
summary: Andersen Genève was founded in 1980 by Danish watchmaker Svend Andersen, a co-founder of the AHCI. Making around 50 watches a year, it is best known for its ultra-thin world-time watches, jumping hours and Montre à Tact.
history:
Danish-born Svend Andersen trained in Denmark and moved to Switzerland, where he worked in the complications workshop of Patek Philippe in Geneva for several years. In 1980 he went independent, opening his own atelier in Geneva, and in 1985 he co-founded the Académie Horlogère des Créateurs Indépendants (AHCI) with Vincent Calabrese to support independent watchmakers.

Andersen became renowned for reviving the world-time complication pioneered by Louis Cottier, making ultra-thin world-time modules at a time when few houses offered the function. He also made unusual complications and one-off pieces, from secular calendars to discreet erotic automata, earning the nickname 'watchmaker of the impossible'.

Today Andersen Genève operates from a riverside atelier in Geneva and a case workshop in La Chaux-de-Fonds, producing about 50 watches a year across its World Timer collection (Tempus Terrae, Rattrapante Mondiale, Communication 45), Jumping Hours and Montre à Tact lines, with many pieces customised with enamel, stone and hand-engraved dials. The brand celebrated its 45th anniversary in 2025. Many Andersen pieces are one-offs or tiny series made to a client's wishes, with dials in materials ranging from jade to grand feu enamel, reflecting a lineage of pure artisanal watchmaking.

name: Angelus
tagline: Le Locle's chronograph-calendar pioneer, revived as a high-end manufacture
summary: Angelus was founded in Le Locle in 1891 by the Stolz brothers and became celebrated for complicated chronographs such as the 1942 Chronodato and the Datalarm alarm watch. Revived in 2015 by movement maker La Joux-Perret, part of the Citizen group, it now makes avant-garde tourbillons and vintage-inspired chronographs.
history:
Angelus was founded in 1891 in Le Locle by brothers Gustav and Albert Stolz, and developed into one of the most innovative movement-making manufactures of the first half of the 20th century. The firm specialised in complications, producing chronographs, alarm watches, travel clocks and repeaters, and supplied movements to other brands.

In 1942 Angelus launched the Chronodato, one of the first serially produced wristwatch chronographs with a full calendar, followed by chronographs with triple calendar and moon phase. In the 1950s it introduced the Datalarm, an alarm wristwatch with date, and the Tempomatic automatic. Angelus's small, beautifully made desk and travel clocks, including eight-day and alarm models, were also widely admired. Like many of its peers, the company was hit hard by the quartz crisis, and the brand fell dormant in the 1970s.

In 2011 the Angelus name was acquired by La Joux-Perret, the La Chaux-de-Fonds movement maker owned since 2012 by Japan's Citizen group. After several years of development, the brand was relaunched in 2015 with the U10 Tourbillon Lumière, followed by skeleton tourbillons, a tourbillon diver, rattrapante tourbillons and a modern Chronodate with a sapphire-framed movement. More recently Angelus has balanced its avant-garde L.A.B. line with the La Fabrique collection of vintage-inspired chronographs such as the Instrument de Vitesse and the Chronographe Télémètre, all powered by in-house calibres designed, produced, finished and tested in-house.

name: anOrdain
tagline: Glasgow's enamel-dial workshop reviving high craft in British watchmaking
summary: anOrdain is a Glasgow watchmaker founded in 2016 by Lewis Heath, celebrated for vitreous enamel dials made entirely in its own Scottish workshop, including the world's first fumé enamel dials. With long waiting lists and a team of about 30 craftspeople, it has become one of the most admired British microbrands.
history:
anOrdain was incorporated in Glasgow in 2016 by Lewis Heath, a designer who had previously co-founded the Scottish headphone company RHA, working with a small founding team. The brand's name and philosophy centre on the idea that the best results come when designing and making happen under the same roof. Rather than outsourcing dials to Swiss suppliers, anOrdain set out to master vitreous enamel, one of the most difficult decorative crafts in watchmaking and traditionally the preserve of ultra-luxury maisons.

The first Model 1 watches paired Swiss movements with vividly coloured grand-feu style enamel dials and bespoke numerals inspired by the typography of old Scottish Highland maps. In 2019 anOrdain introduced what it describes as the world's first fumé enamel dials, in which colour graduates from a bright centre to a darker edge, and the Model 1 fumé became the brand's signature. The Model 2, a more compact and sporty design, followed, as did the Model 3 'Method' with a textured, hand-stamped enamel-on-silver dial and a porcelain-dial Model 1 that took three years to develop.

Demand quickly outstripped capacity, and anOrdain moved to a reservation-and-waiting-list system with lead times of many months. The team grew from three founders to around 30 people, including six specialist enamellers, and brought hand engraving, champlevé, porcelain, thermal bluing of hands, dial printing, type design, cold forging and leatherwork in-house. In 2025 the company moved into a purpose-designed factory on Glasgow's southside to expand production and train new craftspeople. anOrdain is a member of the Heritage Crafts Association and remains independent.

name: Apple (Apple Watch)
tagline: The world's best-selling watch, which turned the wrist into a health computer
summary: Apple entered watches in 2015 with the Apple Watch, which quickly became the world's best-selling watch of any kind. Built around health and fitness sensing, it now spans the Series, the rugged Ultra and the affordable SE, plus Hermès editions.
history:
Apple, founded in 1976 by Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne in California, announced the Apple Watch in September 2014 and released it in April 2015. The first generation was pitched partly as a luxury object, with an 18-carat gold Edition priced at more than $10,000, and it introduced the Digital Crown as a way to navigate a tiny touchscreen. A partnership with Hermès brought leather straps and branded faces.

Apple soon refocused the watch on fitness and health. Series 2 added GPS and swim-proofing, Series 3 cellular connectivity, and Series 4 in 2018 an electrical heart sensor for ECG readings, cleared by the US FDA, along with fall detection. Later models added blood-oxygen sensing, temperature sensing and sleep-apnea notifications, and the watch has been credited with alerting users to heart problems.

The Apple Watch Ultra of 2022 added a 49 mm titanium case, an orange Action button and dive-computer features, and the lower-priced SE line broadened the audience. By the late 2010s Apple was shipping more watches each year than the entire Swiss watch industry. In 2026 the range comprises the Series 12 in aluminium, titanium and ceramic, the Ultra 4 with satellite messaging, and the SE 3.

name: Aquastar
tagline: 1960s dive-instrument pioneer behind the Deepstar and Benthos 500
summary: Aquastar was founded in 1962 by diver-watchmaker Frédéric Robert and built some of the most inventive dive and regatta watches of the 1960s and 1970s, sold through Scubapro and Aqualung. Revived in 2019–2020 under Rick Marei, it reissues the Deepstar chronograph, Benthos 500 and Model 60 from Biel.
history:
Aquastar was established in 1962 by Frédéric Robert, a watchmaker and passionate diver who had taken over the JeanRichard firm and refocused it on functional instruments for aquatic use. Robert filed numerous patents covering crowns, rotating bezels and decompression tables, and Aquastar watches were sold initially through professional diving outlets such as Scubapro and Aqualung rather than jewellers.

The brand's catalogue from the 1960s and 1970s reads like a list of dive-instrument experiments. The Model 60 skin diver of the late 1950s and early 1960s was followed by the Deepstar, a dive chronograph with a no-decompression bezel, and around 1970 by the Benthos 500, a hefty professional diver with a central 60-minute chronograph. Aquastar also became known for regatta timers such as the Regate, with coloured countdown discs for sailing starts, and for the Airstar pilot's chronograph of 1965.

After Robert retired, the Eren Group acquired Aquastar in 1975, and in 1982 the Seinet brothers took over and moved into quartz models. For decades the brand survived mainly as a maker of regatta timing watches while vintage pieces became collector favourites. In 2019 the Synchron Group, under dive-watch revivalist Rick Marei, who had previously been involved in Doxa's reissues, acquired Aquastar and moved it to Bienne. The 2020 Deepstar re-edition was followed by the Deepstar II, the Benthos 500 Founder's Edition with its original central chronograph, the Benthos Heritage and the Model 60 MKII.

name: Armin Strom
tagline: Biel manufacture pioneering twin-balance resonance in the wristwatch
summary: Armin Strom is a Biel-based manufacture that grew from a renowned skeletonising workshop into an independent maker of in-house movements. It is best known for its patented resonance clutch spring, which couples two balance wheels, and for its openly displayed, off-centre dials.
history:
Armin Strom, a watchmaker from Burgdorf, established his business in 1967 and became celebrated for hand-skeletonised watches, engraving and openworking movements from other makers into delicate lacework. In 2006 the brand was taken over by investors including Willy Michel and his son Serge Michel, with master watchmaker Claude Greisler joining as technical lead; the founder retired.

The new owners transformed Armin Strom into a manufacture in Biel, launching their first in-house calibre around 2009 and building a large proportion of components themselves. The brand's signature became visible mechanics: dials pushed off-centre so that barrels, wheels and balances are on display on the front of the watch.

In 2016 the Mirrored Force Resonance introduced a patented clutch spring that links two independent balance wheels so they synchronise through resonance, improving stability. The resonance platform expanded into a dual time GMT and, in 2020, a minute repeater. More recently the System78 line - including the Tribute, Orbit with on-demand date and the Gravity Equal Force with a patented equal-force barrel - aimed at more accessible haute horlogerie.

Today Armin Strom is owned and run by Serge Michel and Claude Greisler and produces a few hundred watches a year in Biel.
ownership: Owned by Serge Michel and Claude Greisler

name: Arnold & Son
tagline: Astronomy, chronometry and world time in homage to John Arnold
summary: Arnold & Son is a high-end manufacture in La Chaux-de-Fonds named after John Arnold, the 18th-century English chronometer pioneer who coined the modern use of the term 'chronometer'. Part of the Citizen group through movement maker La Joux-Perret, it is known for the giant-moon Luna Magna, Perpetual Moon, Globetrotter and Time Pyramid.
history:
John Arnold (1736–1799), born in Bodmin, Cornwall, was among the most important English watchmakers of the 18th century. Working in London from around 1762, he designed practical, accurate marine chronometers that could be made in quantity from about 1782, gave the word 'chronometer' its modern meaning and invented the overcoil balance spring still used in most mechanical watches. His chronometer 'Arnold 36' performed remarkably in trials at the Royal Observatory. In 1787 he founded Arnold & Son with his son John Roger Arnold, supplying chronometers to the Royal Navy and explorers, and he formed a close friendship with Abraham-Louis Breguet, who trained John Roger.

The name was revived in 1995 as a Swiss brand within The British Masters group, which also launched Graham. In 2010 it became part of the La Joux-Perret movement manufacture in La Chaux-de-Fonds, and in 2012 Japan's Citizen group acquired the holding company, giving Arnold & Son access to substantial in-house movement development.

Arnold & Son organises its work around three pillars: astronomy, chronometry and world time. Its astronomical watches include the Perpetual Moon, with a large hand-painted moon accurate for 122 years, and the Luna Magna, featuring a three-dimensional half-marble, half-aventurine moon. Chronometry is represented by the Time Pyramid with its vertically stacked skeleton movement, the Nebula, the Ultrathin Tourbillon and constant-force designs, while the Globetrotter displays world time with a sculpted Northern Hemisphere dome. All are powered by manufacture calibres.

name: Atelier Wen
tagline: A 'Chinese soul' in guilloché, enamel and tantalum, from a Sino-French duo
summary: Atelier Wen is a Sino-French brand creating high-end watches that celebrate Chinese craftsmanship, notably hand-turned guilloché dials by master Cheng Yucai and grand feu enamel. Its integrated-bracelet Perception has become one of the most acclaimed new watches to come out of China.
history:
Atelier Wen was founded in 2018 by two Frenchmen, Robin Tallendier and Wilfried Buiron, who met while studying in Beijing in 2016 and were frustrated by the dismissive way Chinese craftsmanship was often seen. Their aim was to make 'a high quality timepiece with a Chinese soul'. Their first Kickstarter campaign in October 2018, for the Porcelain Odyssey Hao and Ji models with porcelain dials, was funded in under 30 minutes.

After a pause to refine the concept, the brand relaunched in 2022 with the Perception, an integrated-bracelet steel sports watch with hand-turned guilloché dials by Cheng Yucai, described as China's first master of the craft, and a Chinese Dandong movement. It sold out in 16 hours. Collaborations with Wristcheck and a titanium Millésime followed.

The brand has since moved upmarket. In 2025 it launched the Ancestra dress watch with a grand feu enamel dial and the Inflection, a full-tantalum integrated watch with enamel dials by Kong Lingjun's workshop and a customised Girard-Perregaux movement. In 2026 the Perception V3 adopted a French Pequignet EPM03 chronometer-grade movement. Atelier Wen coordinates design and production from Beijing and has its office in Hong Kong.

name: Audemars Piguet
tagline: The Le Brassus family manufacture that invented the luxury steel sports watch
summary: Audemars Piguet is the oldest fine watch manufacture still in the hands of its founding families, based in Le Brassus in the Vallée de Joux. Its 1972 Royal Oak created the luxury steel sports-watch category, and the brand remains one of the 'Holy Trinity' of Swiss watchmaking alongside Patek Philippe and Vacheron Constantin.
history:
Audemars Piguet was founded in 1875 in Le Brassus, in the Vallée de Joux, by two young watchmakers, Jules Louis Audemars and Edward Auguste Piguet. Audemars handled the technical side while Piguet ran sales, and the firm was formally registered as Audemars Piguet & Cie in 1881. From the start it specialised in complicated movements, producing grand complication pocket watches and, in 1892, a minute repeater movement small enough for a wristwatch.

The Great Depression and the Second World War slashed production, but the company survived by focusing on ultra-thin and complicated pieces, including the 1946 ultra-thin calibre 2003, then the world's thinnest. By the early 1970s, with the quartz crisis threatening mechanical watchmaking, managing director Georges Golay commissioned Gérald Genta to design a radically new watch. The result, the 1972 Royal Oak ref. 5402ST, was an octagonal-bezelled steel sports watch with an integrated bracelet priced above many gold watches. It was controversial at first but ultimately defined an entire category.

The Royal Oak Offshore followed in 1993, an oversized and aggressive variant nicknamed 'the Beast', and in 1986 AP released the first automatic tourbillon wristwatch. Under CEO François-Henry Bennahmias (2012–2023) the company cut back its wholesale network, pushed into directly operated boutiques and 'AP Houses', and saw revenues soar. The Code 11.59 collection was launched in 2019, and the Musée Atelier Audemars Piguet, a spiralling glass building by BIG, opened in Le Brassus in 2020.

The company is still owned by descendants of the Audemars and Piguet families. Ilaria Resta became CEO in 2024, and for its 150th anniversary in 2025 AP unveiled the Universelle RD#4, its most complicated watch to date with more than 40 functions.

name: Autodromo
tagline: Vintage dashboard gauges and 1960s-80s racing cars, reimagined for the wrist
summary: Autodromo is a New York-based independent brand founded in 2011 by industrial designer and car enthusiast Bradley Price. Its watches translate the dashboards, gauges and design language of 1960s-1980s racing and road cars, from Group B rally to single-seat 'monoposto' racers, into compact, affordable timepieces.
history:
Bradley Price founded Autodromo in New York in 2011. A self-professed 'petrolhead' and owner of a Ferrari Dino 208 GT4, Price set out to capture the expression and passion of automobiles and timekeeping from the 1960s, 1970s and 1980s. Rather than borrowing generic racing cues, Autodromo's designs draw directly on vintage dashboard instruments, speedometers and rev counters, while cases echo the wedge-era styling of Italian design studios such as Bertone.

The brand grew slowly and deliberately, releasing only a few watches each year. Early collections included the Monoposto, whose 43mm case recalls the oversized gauges of 1950s single-seater racing cars, and the Prototipo chronograph. The Group B, named after the famously wild 1980s rally category, became its best-known model, pairing a titanium bezel with a steel case and automatic Miyota movement. The Intereuropa, a hand-wound time-only watch on a Saffiano leather rally strap, and a Monoposto chronograph with a rev-counter-style redline followed, alongside collaborations such as a 2025 Group B 'Pegasus' edition with Mobil 1.

Autodromo has remained a small, independent and design-led company. In 2025 it re-issued the Monoposto as the limited Series Two with new colourways and a Miyota 9039 automatic, and in 2026 it launched the Group C Turbo Sport, a premium digital watch inspired by 1980s and 1990s Group C endurance racers. Beyond watches, Autodromo sells driving gloves, leather goods and apparel, rounding out a lifestyle brand for 'rev-heads who drive tastefully'.

name: Ball Watch
tagline: Railroad-standard accuracy since 1891, lit by self-powered tritium tubes
summary: Ball Watch Company was founded in Cleveland in 1891 by Webb C. Ball, whose railroad timekeeping standards made American trains safer. Now Swiss-based in La Chaux-de-Fonds and owned by Hong Kong's Asia Commercial Holdings, it makes rugged mechanical watches lit by tritium gas tubes.
history:
Webb C. Ball was a Cleveland jeweler when, after a deadly train collision at Kipton, Ohio, in April 1891 was blamed on an unreliable watch, he was appointed chief time inspector for the Lake Shore railroad lines. He introduced the General Railroad Timepiece Standards, which required watches to meet strict accuracy and design rules, along with regular inspection by certified watchmakers. The system spread across roughly 125,000 miles of US railways, and 'Ball time' became a byword for accuracy.

Ball's company did not make movements itself: it bought them from makers such as Waltham, Hamilton and Elgin, and sold Ball-standard watches to railroad men. The business remained in the family for decades, supplying railroads until the mid-20th century.

In the 1990s the brand was reborn around rugged sports watches for demanding conditions. It was acquired from the Ball family around 2000 by private investors, moved its international headquarters to La Chaux-de-Fonds in Switzerland and adopted the motto 'Accuracy under adverse conditions'. Every modern Ball uses self-powered micro gas tubes (tritium) for constant illumination, and the brand developed shock-protection and anti-magnetic systems for lines such as the Engineer, Engineer Hydrocarbon, Roadmaster, Trainmaster and Fireman. Today the company is owned by Hong Kong-based Asia Commercial Holdings.

name: Baltic
tagline: Besançon microbrand making vintage-inspired watches at honest prices
summary: Baltic is a French microbrand founded by Etienne Malec in Besançon, selling vintage-inspired divers, chronographs and dress watches directly online. Its affordable micro-rotor MR01 and Aquascaphe diver made it one of the most successful microbrands of its generation.
history:
Etienne Malec founded Baltic in 2016, inspired by his father, a photographer and passionate collector who documented every watch he encountered in a diary. The name nods to the family's Polish roots and the Baltic Sea. Launched through crowdfunding, the brand's first model, the Bicompax 001 manual chronograph, quickly sold out and set the tone: 1950s and 1960s-inspired designs, faithful proportions and prices within reach of young enthusiasts.

Baltic followed with the HMS 001 dress watch and, in 2020, the Aquascaphe, a compact vintage-style diver that became its best-seller. In 2021 the MR01, a sub-€600 dress watch with a micro-rotor movement, a salmon dial and Breguet numerals, won widespread acclaim.

The company designs its watches in Besançon, the historic heart of French watchmaking, sourcing components from Hong Kong and elsewhere and assembling and adjusting watches in its Besançon atelier, with straps made in France. Sold primarily direct to consumers and through a small number of retailers and showrooms, Baltic has broadened its line-up with GMT divers, the Hermétique field watch, the Scalegraph chronograph with a Sellita manual chronograph movement and stone-dial Prismic models.

name: Baume & Mercier
tagline: Accessible Geneva elegance with roots stretching back to 1830
summary: Baume & Mercier is a Geneva watchmaker known for classic, accessible luxury watches such as the Riviera, Clifton and Hampton. Owned by Richemont from 1988, it was sold to Italy's Damiani Group in 2026.
history:
The Baume family set up a watchmaking business in Les Bioux, in the Swiss Jura, in 1830, and brothers Louis-Victor and Célestin Baume founded Frères Baume, later opening a London branch, Baume Brothers, in 1844. The firm built a reputation for precise pocket watches and complications, winning prizes at observatory trials and international exhibitions in the late 19th century.

In 1918 William Baume went into partnership with Paul Mercier, a watch dealer of Russian origin, and the Maison Baume & Mercier was registered in Geneva in 1919, earning the Geneva Hallmark for its watches. The company focused on elegant wristwatches and, in the 1920s and 30s, on watches for women. In 1964 it adopted the Greek letter phi, symbol of the golden ratio, as its emblem, and in 1965 Piaget took control.

The quartz era brought the 1973 Riviera, an integrated-bracelet sports watch with a twelve-sided bezel, followed by the rectangular Hampton in 1994 and the Classima, Capeland and Clifton lines. In 1988 the Vendôme group, later Richemont, acquired Baume & Mercier, positioning it as the group's entry point to Swiss luxury.

In 2018 the brand introduced the Baumatic, an automatic movement with a five-day power reserve and silicon components developed with Richemont's ValFleurier manufacture. Sales, however, lagged behind rivals. In January 2026 Richemont agreed to sell the brand to the Italian jeweller Damiani Group, and the transaction closed on 1 July 2026, with Richemont providing operational services for a transitional period. The Riviera, relaunched in 2021, remains its best-known design.

name: Bausele
tagline: Australian watches with a piece of Australia sealed inside the crown
summary: Bausele is a Sydney-based watch brand founded in 2011 by Swiss-born watchmaker Christophe Hoppé. Its name means 'Beyond Australian Elements', and its signature is a hollow crown holding real Australian materials such as Bondi or Manly Beach sand, red earth or opal, combined with Swiss movements.
history:
Bausele was founded in Sydney in 2011 by Christophe Hoppé, a Swiss-born watchmaker who had worked in the Swiss watch industry in Geneva and La Chaux-de-Fonds before moving to Australia. The name is derived from 'Beyond Australian Elements', and from the start Hoppé combined Australian design with Swiss movements and components. The brand's signature became a hollow crown containing small quantities of Australian materials, from Bondi Beach sand and outback red earth to coral, opal and sea glass.

The OceanMoon was one of Bausele's three founding watches in 2011; with a tide indicator, sea glass in the crown and a distinctive case it became the brand's most popular model and a favourite of surfers and ocean lovers. In 2015 Bausele became the first Australian watch brand to exhibit at Baselworld in Switzerland. The following year it formed a joint venture with Flinders University to develop 'Bauselite', a ceramic composite, used in the Terra Australis collection. Bausele also produced a Pilot Automatic with Australian aviation and military communities and collaborated with the Sydney Opera House and the Bathurst 12 Hour endurance race.

Military partnerships have become central to the brand. In 2021 Bausele made the official centenary watch of the Royal Australian Air Force, later followed by the Air Force 5th Generation, whose crown holds soil from RAAF Base Point Cook. In 2024 it launched the Elemental dive collection, developed with input from more than 400 contributors, and in 2026 released officially authorised 125th-anniversary watches for the Australian Army and the Royal Australian Engineers. Bausele remains privately held and headquartered in Sydney, and has shown at Geneva Watch Days.

name: Beijing Watch Factory
tagline: China's capital-city watchmaker, specialists in hand-finished tourbillons
summary: Beijing Watch Factory, founded in 1958, is one of China's historic watchmakers and today concentrates on high-end mechanical watches, especially tourbillons with traditional Chinese decoration. It produces movements, components and complete watches.
history:
Beijing Watch Factory (Beijing Shoubiao Chang) was established in 1958, during the period when China set up state watch factories to make the country self-sufficient in timepieces, and its early watches were sold under the 'Beijing' name. Over the following decades it produced mechanical watches for the domestic market, including the Shuangling (Double Rhombus) line, which became a well-known Chinese watch name.

As the market liberalised and cheap quartz arrived, the factory reoriented toward high-end mechanical watchmaking. It developed its own movements and became known for tourbillons and elaborate hand decoration such as engraving and skeletonisation drawing on Chinese artistic themes, positioning itself as a Chinese counterpart to Swiss haute horlogerie.

The company later became privately owned and employed around 600 people in 2013. According to published sources, the Shenzhen watch group FIYTA acquired it in 2016. Detailed current model and pricing information is limited outside China. Its product range spans complete watches, in-house movements and components, and the factory presents its top tourbillon pieces as showcases of Chinese high watchmaking.

tagline: Square cockpit-instrument watches from a Paris-Swiss house
summary: Bell & Ross was founded in Paris in 1992 by Bruno Belamich and Carlos Rosillo, and is famous for the BR 01 and BR 03 square watches modelled on aircraft cockpit instruments. With Chanel as a shareholder and production in La Chaux-de-Fonds, it has expanded into integrated-bracelet sports watches with the BR 05.
history:
Bell & Ross was founded in 1992 in Paris by two friends, designer Bruno Belamich and businessman Carlos Rosillo, whose nicknames 'Bell' and 'Ross' give the brand its name. The project began as a university idea to create professional instrument watches for pilots, divers and other specialists. In its early years the watches were produced by Sinn in Frankfurt, a respected maker of tool watches, and Bell & Ross gained credibility with professionals including bomb-disposal and military units.

Chanel acquired a minority stake in the company, and in 2002 production moved from Germany to Switzerland, with a manufacturing base in La Chaux-de-Fonds while design and headquarters remained in Paris. In 1998 the Hydromax 11100M set a Guinness World Record for water resistance, rated to 11,100 metres thanks to its oil-filled case.

The brand's breakthrough came in 2005 with the BR 01, a large square case with a round dial directly inspired by aircraft cockpit instruments. The design became one of the most recognisable of the 2000s and spawned the smaller BR 03, as well as the round Vintage and BR V2 lines. Bell & Ross has supplied watches to French Air Force squadrons and partnered in Formula 1 with Renault and later the Alpine F1 Team. In 2019 it launched the BR 05, an integrated-bracelet 'urban' sports watch, followed by the BR-X5 with a manufacture calibre developed with Kenissi, and in 2023 a redesigned 41 mm BR 03.

name: Benrus
tagline: Military-issue American watch brand worn by Steve McQueen, revived in New York
summary: Benrus was founded in New York in 1921 by the Lazrus brothers and became one of America's largest watch companies, known for military watches such as the DTU-2A/P and the Type I and Type II. Revived after a 2018 recapitalisation, it now makes Swiss-made reissues of its military and civilian classics from New York.
history:
Benjamin, Oscar and Ralph Lazrus, immigrants from Romania, founded Benrus in Manhattan in 1921, combining Benjamin's first name with the family surname. The company grew quickly by importing Swiss movements and casing them in the US, and by the mid-century it was among the country's largest watch brands, headquartered at the Hippodrome building on Sixth Avenue.

Benrus is best remembered for its military work. It supplied the US armed forces with the DTU-2A/P field watch from 1964 and, in the 1970s, the rugged Type I and Type II dive-style watches for special operations units. Its civilian #3061 version of a military design became famous when Steve McQueen wore it in the 1968 film Bullitt, and the Sky Chief chronograph was a popular pilot's watch.

The quartz era and financial trouble ended the original business in the late 1970s, and the name passed through several owners. In 2018 a private investment group led by lawyer Michael Sweeney acquired the brand, and it relaunched with a team of industry veterans, a facility in La Chaux-de-Fonds and a new headquarters back at the Hippodrome in New York. Today's Swiss-made collection revives the DTU, Type I, Type II, #3061 and Sky Chief alongside the carbon-and-titanium Type 3X.

name: Blancpain
tagline: Claimed oldest watch brand and creator of the Fifty Fathoms dive watch
summary: Blancpain traces its roots to 1735 in Villeret, making it one of the oldest watch brands in existence. Revived in the 1980s and owned by the Swatch Group since 1992, it is best known for the 1953 Fifty Fathoms, the archetype of the modern diver's watch, and for traditional complications such as the full calendar with moon phase.
history:
Blancpain dates its founding to 1735, when schoolteacher and watchmaker Jehan-Jacques Blancpain registered as a watchmaker in Villeret, in the Bernese Jura. For almost two centuries the business passed from father to son, industrialising under Frédéric-Louis Blancpain in the 19th century. When the family line ended in 1932, the company was taken over by Betty Fiechter and André Léal and renamed Rayville SA, although Blancpain remained the brand name. It supplied movements for the Harwood automatic wristwatch of 1926 and produced the Rolls automatic in 1930.

In 1953, CEO Jean-Jacques Fiechter, a keen diver, developed the Fifty Fathoms, a robust automatic watch with a locking rotating bezel, luminous markers and a sealed case. It was adopted by the French Navy's combat swimmers under Captain Robert Maloubier and later worn in Jacques-Yves Cousteau's documentary The Silent World. Blancpain joined the SSIH group (Omega and Tissot) in 1961, but the quartz crisis devastated the business and production effectively stopped by the early 1980s.

In 1983 Jean-Claude Biver and Jacques Piguet bought the dormant name and relaunched it in Le Brassus with the famous slogan that Blancpain had never made a quartz watch and never would. They focused on six 'masterpieces' of traditional watchmaking, culminating in the 1991 '1735' grand complication. The success attracted SMH, the future Swatch Group, which acquired the brand in 1992.

Under Marc A. Hayek, president from 2002, Blancpain relaunched the Fifty Fathoms in 2003, developed in-house calibres including the carrousel and the Villeret collection's complete calendars, and supported ocean exploration through its Ocean Commitment programme. The Fifty Fathoms celebrated its 70th anniversary in 2023.

name: BOSS (Hugo Boss)
tagline: German tailoring house whose sharp chronographs are built by Movado Group
summary: Hugo Boss is the Metzingen-based fashion house behind the BOSS and HUGO labels. Its watches, mostly sporty quartz chronographs and dress pieces sold in department stores worldwide, have been designed, made and distributed under licence by Movado Group since 2005.
history:
Hugo Ferdinand Boss founded a clothing company in Metzingen, Germany, in 1924, initially producing workwear and uniforms. During the 1930s and 1940s the firm manufactured uniforms for the Nazi Party and German armed forces, using forced labour during the war, a history the company formally acknowledged and apologised for in 2011. After Boss's death in 1948 the business was run by his son-in-law Eugen Holy, whose sons Uwe and Jochen transformed it in the 1970s into an international menswear label known for sharp, power-dressing suits.

Hugo Boss went public in 1985 and was later controlled by the Italian Marzotto group and then private-equity firm Permira. The company expanded into womenswear, fragrance and accessories, much of it through licences. Watches arrived in the 1990s: from 1996 BOSS timepieces were produced by the licensee Tempus Concept, and in 2005 Movado Group took over a long-term global licence to design, manufacture and market BOSS and HUGO watches.

Under Movado, BOSS watches became a department-store staple, built around bold stainless-steel chronographs with motorsport and nautical themes such as Hero, Grand Prix, Santiago and Candor, alongside minimalist dress watches and a separate, younger HUGO line. In 2022 the partners renewed their licence through the end of 2026 and introduced BOSS watches made with recycled ocean-bound plastic. Today Hugo Boss AG remains listed in Frankfurt and headquartered in Metzingen.

name: Bovet
tagline: Fleurier's enamel-and-engraving specialist, once the watch of imperial China
summary: Bovet was founded in 1822 by Édouard Bovet, whose ornate pocket watches became so popular in China that the name became a byword for 'watch'. Owned since 2001 by Pascal Raffy, the independent house is known for hand engraving, miniature painting, the convertible Amadeo case and complicated Récital pieces.
history:
In 1814 Édouard Bovet, a young watchmaker from Fleurier in the Val-de-Travers, travelled to London and from there to Canton, the only Chinese port open to foreign trade. He sold four watches for the then enormous sum of 10,000 dollars and, recognising the Chinese appetite for richly decorated timepieces, founded Bovet with his brothers in 1822, with a workshop in Fleurier and a sales office in Canton. Their pocket watches, typically made in pairs and decorated with enamel miniatures, pearls and hand engraving, with fine movements visible through the back, became so desirable that 'Bo Wei' came to mean 'watch' in Chinese.

The firm prospered for much of the 19th century but declined as the China trade waned, passing through several owners over the following century. In 2001 the Swiss entrepreneur and collector Pascal Raffy bought the company and set about restoring its standing as a fully fledged manufacture. In 2006 he acquired the Dimier 1738 manufacture, giving Bovet its own movement and component production, including hairsprings, and he established the brand's base in Fleurier with a workshop at the Château de Môtiers.

Under Raffy, Bovet developed the patented Amadeo convertible case, which lets a single watch be worn as a wristwatch, a pocket watch, a pendant or a table clock. The house became known for extremely decorated métiers d'art pieces and for complications such as the Récital 20 Astérium astronomical watch and the Récital 22 Grand Récital. Bovet remains fully independent and produces only a small number of watches each year, many as bespoke pieces through its Ateliers Bovet programme.

name: Breguet
tagline: Abraham-Louis Breguet's legacy: the tourbillon, Breguet hands and guilloché
summary: Founded in Paris in 1775 by Abraham-Louis Breguet, perhaps the most influential watchmaker in history, Breguet invented the tourbillon and the first wristwatch. Now owned by the Swatch Group and based in the Vallée de Joux, it is known for engine-turned guilloché dials, blued 'pomme' hands and classical complications.
history:
Abraham-Louis Breguet, born in Neuchâtel in 1747, trained in France and opened his workshop on the Quai de l'Horloge in Paris in 1775. His innovations reshaped horology: the 'perpétuelle' self-winding watch of around 1780, the Breguet overcoil hairspring, the pare-chute shock protection of 1790, the ruby-cylinder escapement, the gong-spring for repeaters and, most famously, the tourbillon, patented in 1801 to counter the effects of gravity on the balance. He also designed the distinctive hands, numerals and engine-turned dials that still bear his name.

His clients included Marie-Antoinette, whose commissioned grand complication, No. 160, took more than four decades to finish, as well as Napoleon Bonaparte, the Duke of Wellington and Tsar Alexander I. In 1810 he began what is regarded as the first wristwatch, made for Caroline Murat, Queen of Naples. After Breguet's death in 1823 his son and grandson ran the company until 1870, when it passed to the English Brown family, who kept it for a century.

The twentieth century brought military chronographs for the French Air Force, notably the Type 20 from the 1950s, and a succession of owners: the Chaumet brothers in 1970, the investment group Investcorp in 1987 and, in 1999, the Swatch Group under Nicolas G. Hayek, who revived the manufacture at L'Abbaye in the Vallée de Joux and commissioned a replica of the lost Marie-Antoinette watch, completed in 2008.

Today Breguet produces the Classique, Tradition, Marine, Type XX and Reine de Naples collections, combining in-house guilloché and complications. In 2025 the brand celebrated its 250th anniversary with a series of commemorative models and new technical developments.

name: Breitling
tagline: Instruments for professionals: the aviator's chronograph since 1884
summary: Breitling is an independent Swiss brand best known for pilot chronographs such as the slide-rule Navitimer. Once the chronograph specialist of the aviation world, it has been repositioned since 2017 as a 'modern retro' casual-luxury brand with in-house B01 movements.
history:
Léon Breitling opened a workshop in Saint-Imier in 1884 to make chronographs and timing instruments, moving to Grenchen in 1892. His son Gaston created one of the first wrist chronographs with a separate pusher at 2 o'clock in 1915, and grandson Willy added an independent return-to-zero pusher in 1934, establishing the modern two-pusher layout.

Breitling became a favourite of aviators. The Chronomat of 1942 added a circular slide rule, and the Navitimer of 1952, adopted by the Aircraft Owners and Pilots Association, turned it into a flight computer for the wrist. Astronaut Scott Carpenter wore a 24-hour Navitimer Cosmonaute on Mercury-Atlas 7 in 1962. In 1969 Breitling co-developed the automatic Calibre 11 with Heuer, Hamilton-Büren and Dubois Dépraz.

The quartz crisis forced Willy Breitling to close the firm in 1979. Pilot and electronics entrepreneur Ernest Schneider bought the name and relaunched it from Grenchen, bringing a revived Chronomat in 1984 and the Emergency, with a built-in distress beacon, in 1995. By 2002 every Breitling was COSMOC-certified as a chronometer, and in 2009 it introduced its in-house B01 chronograph calibre.

In 2017 the Schneider family sold a majority to private-equity firm CVC Capital Partners and Georges Kern became CEO, reshaping the catalogue around the Navitimer, Chronomat, Superocean and Premier and a retro-casual image. Partners Group took a significant stake in 2021 and majority control in 2022, with CVC retaining a minority. Breitling remains headquartered in Grenchen.

name: Bremont
tagline: Aviation-inspired British watchmaker known for the ejection-seat-tested MB
summary: Bremont was founded in 2002 by brothers Nick and Giles English with the aim of reviving mechanical watchmaking in Britain. Known for rugged pilot's watches such as the Martin-Baker MB series, it assembles and increasingly manufactures watches at its facility in Henley-on-Thames.
history:
Brothers Nick and Giles English grew up restoring vintage aircraft with their father. The name Bremont comes from a French farmer, Antoine Bremont, who sheltered them after they made an emergency landing in France in 1995. After their father died and Nick was badly injured in a 1996 plane crash, the brothers decided to pursue their dream of building mechanical watches in Britain, founding Bremont in 2002.

The brand quickly built an aviation identity. Its partnership with ejection-seat maker Martin-Baker produced the MB series, which is tested on live ejection rigs; the red-barrelled MBI is available only to those who have ejected from an aircraft using a Martin-Baker seat. Bremont also partnered with military units, explorers and motorsport teams, and developed Trip-Tick case construction and a rubber-mounted, shock-protected movement.

In 2021 the company opened The Wing, a manufacturing and technology centre in Henley-on-Thames, where it machines components and assembles watches, alongside its first in-house-designed calibre. In 2023 an investor group led by Bill Ackman took a major stake, and in 2024 Davide Cerrato was appointed CEO, launching a streamlined collection built around the Supermarine, Altitude, Terra Nova and Supernova families and a new logo.

name: Brew
tagline: New York microbrand of 1970s-style chronographs inspired by espresso
summary: Brew Watch Co. was founded in New York by industrial designer Jonathan Ferrer, who draws on 1970s design and coffee culture for compact, colourful watches. Its 36 mm Metric chronograph is one of the best-known microbrand designs of recent years.
history:
Jonathan Ferrer, an industrial designer in New York, started Brew around 2015 with a Kickstarter-funded first watch inspired by espresso machines and the rituals of coffee culture. His designs borrow the cushion cases and bold colours of 1970s watches, and they keep sizes small at a time when many brands were making larger watches.

The Retrograph chronograph was designed to time an espresso shot, with its scale highlighting the 25–35 second extraction window. The 36 mm Metric followed with a brushed-and-polished cushion case and many colourways, from the Retro dial to titanium, PVD and textured 'Bloom' versions, and it earned coverage from Hodinkee, Bloomberg and The New York Times.

Brew has since added the Super Metric in brighter colours, the 30 mm automatic Metric Lite and the Digital Blend, which pairs analog time with an LED espresso-shot timer, while continuing to release limited editions and collaborations. Brew watches are designed in New York and sold mostly online, with frequent small-batch colourways that sell quickly. The brand's playful approach, mixing industrial design with coffee culture, has helped it stand out among microbrands and attract buyers who are new to watches.

name: Bulgari
tagline: Roman jeweller turned ultra-thin record-breaker with the Octo Finissimo
summary: Bulgari (styled Bvlgari) is a Roman jeweller founded in 1884 and owned by LVMH since 2011. Its watchmaking arm in Neuchâtel and Le Sentier has set multiple ultra-thin world records with the Octo Finissimo, while the Serpenti and Bulgari Bulgari remain design icons.
history:
Sotirios Voulgaris, a Greek silversmith from Epirus, emigrated to Italy and opened his first shop in Rome in 1884. The flagship on Via dei Condotti opened in 1905, and under his sons Giorgio and Costantino the house moved from silver to bold, colourful high jewellery that, by the 1950s and 60s, adorned film stars such as Elizabeth Taylor during the 'Hollywood on the Tiber' era. The Latinised 'Bvlgari' logo, inspired by classical Roman inscriptions, became its signature.

Bulgari's first Serpenti bracelet watches appeared in the late 1940s, with coiled snake bodies made of flexible Tubogas gold. In 1977 the Bulgari Bulgari watch, with the brand name engraved twice on the bezel like an ancient Roman coin, became a global success, and in 1982 the company founded Bulgari Time in Neuchâtel to develop its watchmaking.

The brand went public in 1995 and in 2000 bought the Daniel Roth and Gérald Genta watch companies, gaining movement expertise and the rights to Genta designs. The Octo, launched in 2012 from a Genta-era case concept combining an octagon with a round bezel, became the platform for Bulgari's technical ambitions. In 2011 LVMH acquired the company.

From 2014 the Octo Finissimo series set a string of world records for thinness, including the thinnest tourbillon, minute repeater, automatic watch and chronograph, and the Octo Finissimo Ultra of 2022 measured just 1.80 mm. A later chronometer-certified Octo Finissimo Ultra COSC reclaimed the record at 1.70 mm. Serpenti remains central to its women's watches, and the Octo Finissimo has since been extended with a smaller 37 mm size.

name: Bulova
tagline: New York's watch pioneer: radio ads, tuning forks and a chronograph on the Moon
summary: Bulova is one of America's oldest and best-known watch brands, founded in New York in 1875 and owned by Japan's Citizen Group since 2008. It is famous for broadcasting firsts, the Accutron tuning-fork watch, the Apollo 15 lunar chronograph and its high-frequency Precisionist quartz movements.
history:
Bulova began in 1875 when Bohemian immigrant Joseph Bulova opened a small jewelry shop on Maiden Lane in Manhattan. Over the following decades the company moved into watchmaking, building a factory in Switzerland in 1912 to standardise parts, and became a pioneer of mass-market marketing: in 1926 it aired the first nationwide radio time announcement, and in 1941 it broadcast what is widely cited as the first television commercial in the United States.

After the Second World War Bulova founded the Joseph Bulova School of Watchmaking to train disabled veterans. In 1960 it launched the Accutron, the first electronic watch regulated by a 360 Hz tuning fork, which became part of the American space programme. On 2 August 1971, Apollo 15 commander David Scott wore a Bulova chronograph on the lunar surface after his NASA-issued Omega's crystal came off, a watch that later sold at auction for more than $1.6 million.

The quartz era and changing ownership (Loews Corporation acquired control in 1979) saw Bulova refocus on accessible quartz watches. In 2008 Citizen Watch Co. bought Bulova for about $250 million. Under Citizen, Bulova introduced the 262 kHz Precisionist movement in 2010 and built a strong Archive Series of reissues such as the Lunar Pilot, Oceanographer 'Devil Diver', Computron and Super Seville. Accutron was spun off as a separate brand in 2020, while Bulova remains headquartered in New York.

name: Carl F. Bucherer
tagline: Lucerne's watchmaker of the peripheral rotor, now under Rolex ownership
summary: Carl F. Bucherer is the watch brand of the Lucerne jeweller Bucherer, known for its peripheral-rotor Manero and Patravi watches. Rolex acquired it with the Bucherer retail group in 2023, and in 2025 reports said the brand would be phased out.
history:
Carl Friedrich Bucherer and his wife opened a watch and jewellery shop in Lucerne in 1888, laying the foundation of what became Bucherer, one of Europe's largest watch retailers. The family began selling watches under its own name in 1919 with a collection of Art Deco ladies' watches, and later produced chronographs and certified chronometers; by the 1950s and 60s it was a notable producer of COSC-certified watches, and in 1969 it joined the consortium that developed the Beta 21 quartz movement.

For decades the watches were sold chiefly through the family's own stores. In 2001, under third-generation owner Jörg G. Bucherer, the brand was relaunched internationally as Carl F. Bucherer, with the sporty Patravi collection. In 2007 it acquired movement maker Techniques Horlogères Appliquées (THA) in Sainte-Croix, and in 2008 it unveiled the CFB A1000, a manufacture calibre with a peripheral rotor running around the edge of the movement, allowing an unobstructed view and a slimmer construction. The Manero, Patravi, Heritage and Adamavi collections followed, with prices broadly between about CHF 5,000 and 30,000.

The brand, estimated to make tens of thousands of watches a year, never achieved profitability, surviving largely as Jörg Bucherer's passion. In August 2023 Rolex announced it would buy the Bucherer group, including the watch brand; Jörg Bucherer died shortly afterwards. In February 2025 Swiss media reported that Rolex had decided to shut Carl F. Bucherer down, with its roughly 250 points of sale to be phased out and staff offered roles within Rolex. Bucherer called the reports rumours, and the brand's website remained online into 2026, so its long-term status is uncertain.

name: Cartier
tagline: The jeweller of kings whose Santos and Tank defined the modern wristwatch
summary: Cartier, founded in Paris in 1847, is the world's second-largest Swiss-made watch brand by revenue and one of the most influential designers of wristwatch shapes. Owned by Richemont, it created the Santos in 1904 and the Tank in 1917, and today sells an estimated 700,000 watches a year.
history:
Louis-François Cartier took over the Paris jewellery workshop of his master, Adolphe Picard, in 1847. His son Alfred and grandsons Louis, Pierre and Jacques turned the firm into an international house with branches in Paris (13 rue de la Paix from 1899), London and New York, supplying royal courts across Europe and earning King Edward VII's description of Cartier as 'the jeweller of kings and the king of jewellers'.

Louis Cartier was the creative force behind the house's watches. In 1904 he designed a flat square wristwatch with exposed screws for his friend, the Brazilian aviator Alberto Santos-Dumont, who wanted to read the time without letting go of his controls. The Santos was sold commercially from 1911. The Tortue followed in 1912, and in 1917 Louis drew the Tank, inspired by the outline of Renault tanks on the Western Front, with the brancards forming the lugs. Cartier also patented a deployant buckle in 1910. Movements were supplied by partners such as Edmond Jaeger, and Cartier produced remarkable mystery clocks.

After the family generation passed, the firm was split and then reunited in the 1970s by an investor group led by Joseph Kanoui and backed by the Rupert family's Rembrandt Group. The affordable 'Les Must de Cartier' line of the 1970s broadened the audience, and the Crash, the Pasha and the Panthère became cult designs. Cartier became the cornerstone of the Vendôme group, later Richemont, formed in 1988.

Cartier opened its manufacture in La Chaux-de-Fonds in 2001 and developed in-house movements such as the 1904 MC. The Ballon Bleu (2007) became a bestseller, and relaunches of the Santos (2018), Tank Must (2021, including the solar-powered SolarBeat) and the Cartier Privé series fuelled a boom, making Cartier Morgan Stanley's number two Swiss watch brand by 2025.

innovations: 1904: Santos, one of the first wristwatches designed for men and aviation

name: Casio
tagline: The digital watch icon: cheap, indestructible and everywhere
summary: Casio turned electronics expertise into the world's most ubiquitous digital watches. Its inexpensive resin and steel classics such as the F-91W, A168 and CA-53W calculator watch have sold in enormous numbers and become design icons, alongside higher lines such as Edifice, Pro Trek and G-Shock.
history:
Casio was founded in Tokyo in 1946 by engineer Tadao Kashio as Kashio Seisakujo, initially making parts and a finger ring that held a cigarette. Tadao and his brothers Toshio, Kazuo and Yukio went on to build the 14-A in 1957, the world's first compact all-electric calculator, and the company was incorporated as Casio Computer Co. that year.

Casio's expertise in integrated circuits led to its first watch, the Casiotron, in 1974, one of the earliest digital watches with an automatic calendar. Mass-produced LCD watches followed, with ever more functions: calculators, databanks, games and alarms. The rugged G-Shock arrived in 1983, and in 1989 Casio launched the F-91W, a simple resin digital watch that remains in production and has sold in the tens of millions.

Through the 1990s and 2000s Casio added Tough Solar power, Multi-Band radio-controlled timekeeping, the Pro Trek outdoor line and the Edifice motorsport line. The Timepiece segment is now Casio's largest business, with sales of about ¥166 billion in the year to March 2025, and G-Shock makes up roughly half of it.

The company remains headquartered in Shibuya, Tokyo, and the Kashio family still plays a leading role in management.

name: Caveman Watches
tagline: Made by Ghanaian artisans: Accra's award-winning homegrown watch brand
summary: Caveman Watches is an Accra-based Ghanaian watch company founded in December 2018 by Anthony Dzamefe, who began by selling watches in Kantamanto Market. It designs, hand-assembles and personalises watches and handmade straps in Ghana, and its Blue Volta was named Ghana's Product of the Year in 2021.
history:
Anthony Mensah Dzamefe started out in 2015 selling second-hand and replica watches in Accra's Kantamanto Market, buying his first watch for GH₵50 and reselling it at a profit. He learned to make leather watch straps from a cobbler and began repairing broken watches, gradually building the skills and customer base that would let him create his own brand. On 12 December 2018 he launched Caveman Watches in Ghana, with the ambition of building a Ghanaian watch manufacturing company whose products are 'made by Ghanaian artisans, built to last generations'.

The brand's first and best-known watch, the Blue Volta, launched with the company in 2018. It pairs a blue Pantone sun-ray dial with luminous hands and a date window in a slim 6mm stainless-steel case, offered in 42mm and 36mm sizes on leather straps or chain bracelets. It became a fan favourite among corporate professionals, and in 2021 won Product of the Year at the Ghana Manufacturing Awards, where Caveman was also named watch manufacturing company of the year; the brand was also named Brand of the Year at the EMY Africa Awards.

Caveman has since expanded into collections such as Classics, Heritage, Aviator and higher-end automatic pieces such as the Liege, along with wall clocks, jewellery and accessories. A signature of the brand is personalisation, with engraved dials and case sides, and bespoke commissions for public figures, including a customised watch for Ghanaian footballer Asamoah Gyan. Profiled by The New York Times and Forbes, Caveman is one of Africa's most visible homegrown watch brands and runs its operations from Accra.

name: Certina
tagline: Double Security: Swatch Group sports watches built to last
summary: Certina is a Swatch Group brand founded in Grenchen in 1888 and known for its DS (Double Security) concept of shock- and water-resistant watches. Its DS Action and DS PH divers and turtle logo target sporty, value-minded buyers.
history:
Brothers Adolf and Alfred Kurth founded Kurth Frères in Grenchen in 1888, making watch movements in a small workshop. The company prospered and in 1906 began selling finished watches under the name Grana. In 1938 it introduced the name Certina, from the Latin 'certus', meaning certain or assured, and after the Second World War Certina became the main brand.

By the 1950s Certina employed several hundred people and produced around a thousand watches a day. Its defining innovation arrived in 1959 with the DS, for Double Security: a construction that combined a shock-absorbing suspended movement with reinforced case, crystal and gaskets, making the watches unusually resistant to impacts and water. The turtle emblem, symbol of longevity and protection, became the DS signature. The DS-2 and DS PH200M diver followed in the late 1960s, and in 1971 Certina launched the Biostar, a watch that displayed the wearer's biorhythms.

The quartz crisis pushed Certina into the General Watch Co. of ASUAG in 1971, and through the 1983 merger with SSIH it became part of what is now the Swatch Group. Within the group Certina focuses on sporty, robust watches at accessible prices, often with Powermatic 80 movements and silicon balance springs.

Certina has built a following through heritage reissues such as the DS PH200M and DS Super PH500M, and through the DS Action range of divers and chronographs. It has long been associated with motor sport and diving, and the brand is now based in Le Locle.

name: Chanel
tagline: Couture house turned serious watchmaker: the ceramic J12 and in-house calibres
summary: Chanel, the fashion house founded by Gabrielle 'Coco' Chanel in 1910, entered watchmaking in 1987 with the Première and revolutionised the market in 2000 with the high-tech ceramic J12. Privately owned by the Wertheimer family, it now produces in-house movements in La Chaux-de-Fonds and holds stakes in several independent watchmakers.
history:
Gabrielle 'Coco' Chanel opened a millinery shop at 21 rue Cambon in Paris in 1910 and went on to transform women's fashion with jersey dresses, the little black dress, Chanel No. 5 perfume and the tweed suit. Since the 1950s the company has been owned by the Wertheimer family, originally Chanel's business partners in perfume, and it remains privately held under Alain and Gérard Wertheimer.

Chanel's watchmaking began in 1987 with the Première, a women's watch whose octagonal case recalled the stopper of the No. 5 bottle and the shape of Place Vendôme, worn on a chain bracelet interlaced with leather. In 1993 the house acquired the Swiss case maker G&F Châtelain in La Chaux-de-Fonds, which became its watch manufacture. The real turning point came in 2000 with the J12, designed by artistic director Jacques Helleu and inspired by America's Cup racing yachts. Made of scratch-resistant high-tech black ceramic, followed by white in 2003, it became one of the defining watches of the decade.

Chanel then pursued watchmaking credibility. It took stakes in independent makers such as Romain Gauthier and, in 2018, F.P. Journe, and in 2019 bought into movement maker Kenissi, which supplies Tudor. The Monsieur de Chanel of 2016, its first men's watch with an in-house jumping-hour and retrograde-minute calibre, was followed by the Boy·Friend skeleton and the J12's 2019 redesign with the Kenissi-made Calibre 12.1.

Today Chanel's watch collections include the J12, Première, Boy·Friend, Code Coco and Monsieur, alongside high-jewellery watches, while the company's global headquarters are in London.

name: Chopard
tagline: Scheufele family jeweller-watchmaker behind Happy Diamonds and L.U.C
summary: Chopard is a family-owned Geneva maison that combines high jewellery with serious watchmaking through its Fleurier-based L.U.C manufacture. Owned by the Scheufele family since 1963, it is known for the floating diamonds of Happy Sport, the Alpine Eagle sports watch, and its long partnerships with the Cannes Film Festival and the Mille Miglia.
history:
Louis-Ulysse Chopard founded his workshop in 1860 in Sonvilier, in the Bernese Jura, making precise pocket watches and chronometers that found customers across Europe and Russia. His son Paul-Louis moved the company to Geneva in 1937, but by the early 1960s the family had no successor willing to take over.

In 1963 the business was bought by Karl Scheufele III, heir to a Pforzheim jewellery and watchmaking family. Under Karl and his wife Karin, Chopard grew into an international jeweller-watchmaker, building a manufacture in Meyrin-Geneva in 1974. Designer Ronald Kurowski's Happy Diamonds of 1976, with loose diamonds dancing between two sapphire crystals, became a signature, and in 1993 Happy Sport became one of the first watches to combine steel and diamonds. The 1980 St. Moritz, Karl-Friedrich Scheufele's first design, introduced a steel sports watch with integrated bracelet.

Karl-Friedrich Scheufele, a passionate car enthusiast, linked the brand to the Mille Miglia race in 1988 and in 1996 founded Chopard Manufacture in Fleurier to produce high-end movements. The first in-house calibre, the micro-rotor L.U.C 96.01-L, appeared in 1997 and was named after the founder. His sister Caroline Scheufele took charge of jewellery and, from 1998, the redesign of the Cannes Film Festival's Palme d'Or, which Chopard has crafted ever since.

Today Karl-Friedrich and Caroline are co-presidents. In 2019 the Alpine Eagle revived the St. Moritz with Lucent Steel, and since 2018 Chopard has committed to using 100% ethically sourced gold. L.U.C Fleurier Quality Foundation certification and in-house tourbillons, chiming watches and perpetual calendars have given the brand genuine haute horlogerie credibility.

name: Christophe Claret
tagline: Le Locle complications master behind gaming watches and chiming tourbillons
summary: Christophe Claret is a Le Locle manufacture that for two decades built complex movements - minute repeaters, tourbillons, chronographs - for major brands before launching its own watches in 2009. Its own-name pieces range from Westminster-chiming tourbillons to watches that play blackjack or roulette.
history:
Born in Lyon in 1962, Christophe Claret trained in watchmaking in Geneva and worked restoring antique pieces before founding his own company in 1989, initially specialising in minute repeaters and other complications for leading Swiss brands. The business grew into a sizeable complications manufacture and moved into the Château du Soleil d'Or in Le Locle, a 19th-century manor that houses its workshops.

In 2009, marking 20 years in business, Claret launched watches under his own name with the DualTow. A series of spectacular pieces followed: the 21 Blackjack and other gaming watches with playable mechanisms, the Soprano tourbillon minute repeater with a Westminster chime, the X-TREM-1 with hours and minutes shown by magnetically driven floating steel balls, the Kantharos chronograph, the Maestoso with a detent escapement, and the Margot, a women's watch that plays 'loves me, loves me not'.

The company continues to develop and produce complications for other houses alongside its own low-volume collections, and remains owned by its founder. Its own-brand watches are made in very small numbers and are among the most mechanically ambitious playful watches of the modern era.

name: Christopher Ward
tagline: English-designed, Swiss-made watches sold direct at honest prices
summary: Christopher Ward is a direct-to-consumer British brand founded in 2004 that designs in England and builds its watches in its own atelier in Biel, Switzerland. Famous for strong value, the C60 Trident diver and the GPHG-winning Bel Canto, it has become one of the best-known British watch brands.
history:
Christopher Ward was founded in 2004 by three friends with retail backgrounds: Mike France, Peter Ellis and Chris Ward. Their idea was simple: sell well-made Swiss watches directly online, cutting out the middlemen and pricing each watch at roughly three times its production cost rather than the much higher multiples typical of the industry.

The brand grew quickly through the late 2000s with dress watches, pilots and the C60 Trident dive watch, which became its best-seller. It built a close relationship with Swiss movement specialist Jörg Bader and watchmaker Johannes Jahnke, which led to Christopher Ward's own in-house calibre, the SH21 (later known as CW001), introduced in 2014 and billed as the first commercially viable mechanical movement from a British brand in over 50 years. Jahnke also created the JJ-series modules used for jumping hours and chiming complications.

All Christopher Ward watches are hand-built in its atelier in Biel, Switzerland, while design and the head office are in Maidenhead, England. In 2022 the brand launched The Twelve, its dodecagonal integrated-bracelet sports watch, and in 2023 the C1 Bel Canto, a chiming watch priced under $5,000, made Christopher Ward the first British brand to win a Petite Aiguille at the Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Genève. The company commits 2 percent of sales to charitable causes.

name: Chronoswiss
tagline: Born in a Munich garage during the quartz crisis, famed for the Régulateur and guilloché
summary: Chronoswiss was founded in Munich in 1983 by master watchmaker Gerd-Rüdiger Lang to champion mechanical watchmaking during the quartz crisis. Known for regulator dials, onion crowns, fluted bezels and hand-guilloché dials, it is now based in Lucerne, Switzerland.
history:
Master watchmaker Gerd-Rüdiger Lang founded Chronoswiss in Munich in 1983, shortly after losing his job when Heuer's German operation collapsed. At the height of the quartz crisis, he started building mechanical wristwatches from a garage full of parts, reviving rare calibres and emphasising transparent case backs that showed off the movement.

The brand found its signature in 1987 with the Régulateur, the world's first serially produced wristwatch with a regulator-style dial separating hours, minutes and seconds. It also established the design codes that still define Chronoswiss: the onion crown, straight lugs, finely fluted coin-edge bezel and a multi-part case. Further firsts followed, including the Kairos automatic chronograph with decentralised hours and minutes (1991), the reversible Cabrio (1992), the Opus skeletonised automatic chronograph (1995) and the Delphis (1996), which combined digital jumping hours, retrograde minutes and analogue seconds.

In 2012 Lang sold the company to the Ebstein family, who moved its headquarters and atelier to Lucerne, Switzerland. Under the new owners Chronoswiss has emphasised colourful hand-guilloché dials, bold regulators and new manufacture calibres such as the C.6000 family, developed with La Joux-Perret and introduced in 2023.

name: Ciga Design
tagline: The Chinese design studio whose rotating-Earth Blue Planet won at the GPHG
summary: CIGA Design is a Shenzhen watch brand founded by industrial designer Zhang Jianmin that focuses on bold, design-led mechanical watches at accessible prices. Its Blue Planet, which tells time with a rotating 3D Earth, won the GPHG Challenge Watch Prize in 2021.
history:
CIGA Design was founded in 2016 by Zhang Jianmin, an industrial designer who previously created wayfinding and guidance systems for public spaces such as airports and railway stations. Rather than a traditional watch factory, CIGA operates as a design studio with an international team, assembling its watches in China with movements sourced from China, Japan and Switzerland.

The brand made its name with the Series Z 'Edge' and other skeleton designs, winning numerous design awards including iF, Red Dot and a German Design Award 2020, and set crowdfunding records on Indiegogo. Its breakthrough came in 2021 when the Blue Planet, which replaces conventional hands with a CNC-engraved topographic Earth that rotates beneath a fixed pointer, won the Challenge Watch Prize at the Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Genève, reported as the first GPHG prize for a Chinese mechanical watch.

CIGA has since developed its own calibres, including the CD-04-E automatic for the Blue Planet and, from 2023, an in-house central tourbillon used in the Everest series. It says its watches are available in over 100 countries and have more than 500,000 users.

name: Citizen
tagline: Light-powered Eco-Drive pioneer and one of the world's largest watchmakers
summary: Citizen is one of the world's largest watch manufacturers and the name behind Eco-Drive, light-powered quartz that never needs a battery change. Vertically integrated and technically ambitious, it also owns Bulova, Frédérique Constant, Alpina, Arnold & Son and the movement maker Miyota.
history:
Citizen's story begins in 1918 with the Shokosha Watch Research Institute in Tokyo, founded by jeweller Kamekichi Yamazaki to build a domestic watch industry. In 1924 it produced a pocket watch named 'Citizen' by Tokyo mayor Shinpei Goto, who hoped it would be a watch loved by ordinary citizens. Citizen Watch Co. was established in 1930 with the help of Swiss-born investor Rodolphe Schmid.

After the war Citizen grew rapidly, pioneering shock resistance and water resistance for the domestic market and, in 1970, the X-8 Chronometer, the world's first watch with a titanium case. In 1976 it launched the Crystron Solar Cell, the first light-powered analog quartz watch, the technology that became Eco-Drive in 1995. It also made the world's first multi-band radio-controlled watch in 1993 and, in 2011, the first light-powered watch to set itself via GPS satellites.

Citizen expanded internationally by acquisition: Bulova in 2008, the Swiss movement maker La Joux-Perret in 2012, and Frédérique Constant, Alpina and Ateliers deMonaco in 2016. In 2019 it unveiled Caliber 0100, a light-powered quartz accurate to ±1 second per year.

Today Citizen Watch Co. is listed in Tokyo and headquartered in Nishitokyo. Watches are its largest business alongside machine tools and components, and core lines include Promaster, Tsuyosa, Series 8 and The Citizen.
