name: CLUSE
tagline: Amsterdam's affordable-luxury minimalist watches with swappable straps
summary: CLUSE is an Amsterdam fashion-accessories brand founded in 2013, best known for minimalist women's watches with interchangeable straps at around €100. Designed in-house in Amsterdam and sold online and through retailers worldwide, it has since expanded into jewellery, bags and men's watches.
history:
CLUSE was founded in Amsterdam in 2013. Its founders saw a gap in the market: luxury watches offered beautiful design at high prices, while affordable watches too often lacked style and craftsmanship. CLUSE set out to create 'affordable luxury' watches combining timeless design and functionality sold at accessible prices.

The brand's early success rested on clean, feminine designs: slim round and square cases in silver, gold and rose-gold tones, minimalist dials, mesh bracelets and leather straps that customers could change themselves using quick-release fittings in standard CLUSE widths. Collections such as Minuit, Triomphe, La Tétragone, Gracieuse, Féroce and Boho Chic became staples, and CLUSE built a network of retailers and stockists alongside its own webshop, with collections designed by an in-house team in Amsterdam through a process of moodboards, sketching, material selection and detail refinement.

Over time CLUSE broadened from watches into jewellery and bags, positioning its accessories as 'an extension of your personality' that can be mixed and matched. It has also added more ambitious timepieces, including the integrated-bracelet Vigoureux line for men with chronograph and automatic versions, and multifunction models such as the Quadrus. The business is operated by Europe Watch Group B.V. from Amsterdam and remains one of the best-known Dutch watch brands.

name: Corum
tagline: La Chaux-de-Fonds creatives behind the Golden Bridge, Admiral and Coin Watch
summary: Corum was founded in La Chaux-de-Fonds in 1955 and became known for daring designs: the nautical-flagged Admiral, the Coin Watch made from a gold coin and the Golden Bridge baguette movement. After more than a decade under Hong Kong's Citychamp group, it returned to Swiss ownership through a management buyout in 2025.
history:
Corum was founded in 1955 in La Chaux-de-Fonds by Gaston Ries and his nephew René Bannwart, a watch designer who had worked at Omega and Patek Philippe. From the start the brand cultivated unconventional designs. The Admiral's Cup, launched in 1960, took its name from the famous sailing regatta and later adopted a twelve-sided case with nautical pennant flags in place of hour markers. In 1964 Corum introduced the Coin Watch, whose case and dial were made from a genuine US 20-dollar gold coin sliced in two, and it became a favourite of American presidents and celebrities.

Other imaginative pieces followed, including the Buckingham with an unusual case and the Romulus with Roman numerals engraved in the bezel. In 1980 Corum launched the Golden Bridge, designed by Vincent Calabrese, whose baguette movement is aligned in a single line and suspended between sapphire crystals, creating a striking linear look.

In 2000 Severin Wunderman, the former Gucci watch licensee, acquired Corum and injected new energy with pieces like the oversized Bubble. After his death in 2008, the brand was sold in 2013 to the Hong Kong-based China Haidian group, later renamed Citychamp Watch & Jewellery, which also owned Eterna. The following years were difficult amid declining sales and frequent management changes.

In 2025, the year of its 70th anniversary, Corum returned to 100% Swiss ownership through a management buyout led by Haso Mehmedovic, a former watchmaker and sales director who became CEO and chairman, backed by Swiss investors. The brand continues to focus on the Admiral, Golden Bridge, Bubble and heritage-inspired pieces.

name: Credor
tagline: Seiko's hand-finished haute horlogerie in gold, platinum and porcelain
summary: Credor is Seiko's most exclusive brand, dedicated to precious-metal watches and artisanal finishing. Its Micro Artist Studio creates the cult Eichi II, while the Gérald Genta-designed Locomotive returned in 2024 as a titanium luxury sports watch.
history:
Credor began in 1974 as a high-end line of Seiko's precious-metal watches; the name combines the French 'crête d'or', or 'crest of gold'. It became a stand-alone brand in 1979. Through the 1970s and 80s Credor produced gold dress watches and, in 1979, the Locomotive, a sports watch designed by Gérald Genta with hexagonal screws and an integrated bracelet.

In 2000 Seiko established the Micro Artist Studio at its Shiojiri facility in Nagano, a small team of craftsmen led by Yoshifusa Nakazawa. It created some of Japan's most ambitious watches, including the Spring Drive Sonnerie (2006), the Spring Drive Minute Repeater (2011) and the Fugaku tourbillon (2016). Its best-known creation is the Eichi, a simple time-only watch with a porcelain dial, hand-painted indices and a hand-finished manually wound Spring Drive movement; the Eichi II followed in 2014 and is made in tiny numbers.

For its 50th anniversary in 2024, Credor revived the Locomotive in high-intensity titanium with a new in-house automatic, the CR01. Regular-production green and blue versions followed. Credor also makes the ultra-thin Goldfeather line, descended from Seiko's 1960 Goldfeather and the 1969 U.T.D.

name: Cyrus
tagline: Le Locle-made avant-garde complications, led by the Klepcys
summary: Cyrus is a Swiss independent with headquarters in Plan-les-Ouates and a manufacture in Le Locle, owned by Dr. Pablo Richard with master watchmaker Jean-François Mojon. It is known for the Klepcys family of bold, complicated watches featuring vertical tourbillons, retrograde GMTs and unusual hour displays.
history:
Cyrus positions itself as an avant-garde manufacture emphasising technical independence. Its watches are produced in Le Locle with the involvement of master watchmaker Jean-François Mojon, a well-known complications specialist, while the company's headquarters are in Plan-les-Ouates near Geneva. The business is owned and presided over by Dr. Pablo Richard.

The brand's signature collection is the Klepcys, whose name evokes the clepsydra, an ancient water clock. Klepcys models combine an architectural case with complicated displays: the Klepcys Vertical Tourbillon, limited to 38 pieces per version in rose gold and black DLC titanium; the Klepcys GMT Retrograde; the Klepcys Réveil alarm; and the Klepcys DICE, issued in titanium editions of 50 pieces. The Dominion GMT and the Etheral Twin Orbital Tourbillon broaden the range.

Cyrus produces small limited series and remains a niche name even among collectors of independent watchmaking. Its limited editions are distributed through a small network of retailers and directly by the company. The brand combines contemporary materials such as black DLC titanium with traditional complications, and its modular approach allows the Klepcys case to host very different mechanisms, from alarms to tourbillons. Its catalogue currently lists around seventeen references across its collections.

name: Czapek
tagline: A 19th-century Geneva name, revived with the backing of its collectors
summary: Czapek & Cie revives the house of François Czapek, the Polish-Czech watchmaker who was Antoni Patek's first partner in Geneva. Relaunched in 2015 with collector crowdfunding, it is known for the Quai des Bergues, the integrated-bracelet Antarctique and inventive dial work.
history:
François Czapek, a Czech-born watchmaker who had fought in the Polish uprising of 1830-31, settled in Geneva and in 1839 co-founded Patek, Czapek & Cie with fellow émigré Antoni Patek. The partnership ended in 1845, when Patek joined Adrien Philippe and Czapek founded his own firm, Czapek & Cie. He supplied watches to European nobility, including Emperor Napoleon III, opened a shop near the Place Vendôme in Paris and published a treatise on watchmaking in 1850. The firm faded after his era.

In 2012 entrepreneur Xavier de Roquemaurel, investor Harry Guhl and watchmaker Sébastien Follonier created a company to revive the name. Instead of a traditional launch, they sold shares to collectors, dubbed 'Fellow Investors', and presented the Quai des Bergues in 2015, inspired by an 1850 Czapek pocket watch. The Faubourg de Cracovie chronograph and Place Vendôme tourbillon followed, with the Place Vendôme Complicité winning a GPHG public prize.

The integrated-bracelet Antarctique (2020) became the brand's commercial breakthrough and spawned rattrapante, tourbillon and smaller 'S' versions. Still led by de Roquemaurel and based in Geneva, Czapek marked its tenth anniversary in 2025.

name: Damasko
tagline: Bavarian materials specialists making ice-hardened, near-indestructible tool watches
summary: Damasko is a small manufacture in Barbing near Regensburg, founded in 1994 by materials engineer Konrad Damasko. It is known for ice-hardened steel and submarine-steel cases, patented crown seals and silicon hairsprings, and increasingly in-house movements.
history:
Konrad Damasko founded the company in 1994, applying high-performance materials technology he had developed for industries including aerospace. Its first major business was supplying hardened watch cases to Frankfurt's Sinn, a partnership that lasted until 2002, after which Damasko concentrated on watches under its own name.

The company built its reputation on metallurgy and engineering: ice-hardened stainless steel cases and bracelets, German submarine steel, its own DAMEST coating, patented crown and pusher sealing systems, and a patented silicon hairspring that resists magnetism and temperature changes. Damasko claims more than 100 patents, designs and utility models and says it produces demonstrably only in Germany, with manufacturing depth of up to 90 percent.

Around 2010 Damasko introduced its first in-house movement, the A35, followed by further automatic calibres and the C51 chronograph movement. Test pilots at Airbus Defence & Space have worn its DC-series chronographs. Still a family business with a team of around two dozen people, working from Barbing near Regensburg, Damasko sells through dealers and directly online, offering field watches (DK), divers (DSub), and pilot chronographs (DC) with a distinctly utilitarian aesthetic. Its utilitarian designs and genuine technical substance have earned the brand a loyal following among tool-watch enthusiasts worldwide.

name: Dan Henry
tagline: A 1,500-watch collector's vintage icons, reissued at bargain prices
summary: Dan Henry is a direct-to-consumer brand created by Brazilian vintage collector Dan Henry, who amassed more than 1,500 watches over 30 years. Each model is named after a year and pays homage to a classic mid-century archetype, from racing chronographs to super-compressor divers, typically priced around US$300 and produced in numbered limited editions.
history:
Dan Henry's fascination with mechanical watches began when he received a Roskopf pocket watch for his tenth birthday. Over some 30 years of combing flea markets and local auctions he built a collection of more than 1,500 vintage watches, which he began sharing on Instagram and documented in Timeline.Watch, an online encyclopaedia of watch history. Many followers wanted watches like the ones he showed but could not afford or find the originals, and around 2016 he launched Dan Henry Watches to make comparable vintage-inspired designs accessible.

The brand's concept is simple: each watch is named after a year and distils the best elements of the era's classics. The 1970 Automatic Diver revisits the super-compressor divers of the late 1960s with twin crowns and an inner rotating bezel; the 1964 Gran Turismo recalls motorsport chronographs worn in the hills of California and the streets of Monaco; the 1962 Racing Chronograph channels racing drivers' watches of the Le Mans era; the 1963 is a pilot's GMT; and the 1975 is a slim skin diver. Other models reference 1937 dress chronographs, 1939 military chronographs and 1945 WWII chronographs. Most are issued as limited editions numbered to the model's year, such as 1,964 pieces for the 1964.

Dan Henry keeps prices low, mostly between US$250 and US$400, by selling direct with sapphire or sapphire-coated crystals and Japanese Seiko movements, including meca-quartz VK63 chronographs and NH35 and NH34 automatics. The brand ships from local warehouses in the US, EU and Brazil, and has become one of the most recommended entry points for collectors who love vintage design.

name: Daniel Wellington
tagline: The Instagram-era Scandinavian minimalist that redefined fashion-watch marketing
summary: Daniel Wellington is a Stockholm-based fashion watch brand founded in 2011 by Filip Tysander, famous for slim, minimalist quartz watches on interchangeable NATO, leather and mesh straps. Its pioneering influencer marketing turned it into one of Europe's fastest-growing companies, and in 2025 Timex Group acquired a 51% majority stake.
history:
Daniel Wellington was founded in Stockholm in 2011 by Swedish entrepreneur Filip Tysander. The brand's name and look came from a stylish British gentleman Tysander met while backpacking in Australia, who wore his vintage watches on faded NATO straps. Tysander launched with a small sum of savings, designing a clean, thin, eggshell-dial quartz watch with interchangeable straps, manufactured in China with Japanese Miyota movements.

Rather than traditional advertising, DW became one of the first consumer brands to scale almost entirely through Instagram, gifting watches to thousands of influencers and offering discount codes. The strategy was spectacularly successful: by 2016 the company reported roughly US$230 million in revenue with more than US$100 million in profit, and in 2017 it was named Europe's fastest-growing private company. Its Classic collection, with models named after British places such as Sheffield, Durham and St Mawes, became a defining accessory of the 2010s.

Growth stalled at the end of the decade as the fashion-watch category shrank, smartwatches surged and influencer marketing became crowded; DW posted several years of operating losses around 2019-2021. The brand responded by broadening into jewellery and new collections such as Iconic Link, Iconic Chronograph, GMT and automatic models. In 2022 Timex Group entered via a convertible loan and distribution partnership, and in November 2025 Timex acquired a 51% controlling stake. DW continues to operate from its Stockholm headquarters and remains one of the most recognisable fashion-watch names worldwide.

name: De Bethune
tagline: Blued titanium, floating lugs and research-driven watchmaking from the Jura
summary: De Bethune is a manufacture in L'Auberson founded in 2002 by David Zanetta and master watchmaker Denis Flageollet. It is known for its space-age design language - flame-blued titanium, starry skies and floating lugs - and for technical research into balances, shock protection and moonphases.
history:
Collector David Zanetta and watchmaker Denis Flageollet, a specialist in restoring antique timepieces, founded De Bethune in 2002 in the Jura village of L'Auberson near Sainte-Croix. The name honours the Chevalier de Béthune, an 18th-century figure credited with an escapement invention. From the start, Flageollet treated the brand as a research laboratory, developing a self-regulating twin barrel, silicon and titanium-platinum balance wheels, a triple 'parachute' shock absorber and a precise spherical moonphase.

The DB28, introduced in 2010 with its articulated floating lugs and open, blued-titanium architecture, became the house's defining silhouette and won the Aiguille d'Or at the 2011 Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Genève. Heat-blued titanium dials pierced with white-gold 'stars' - the Starry Varius and Starry Seas pieces - became another signature.

Zanetta sold his majority stake in 2017 after years of financial difficulty, and in 2021 WatchBox (now The 1916 Company) acquired a controlling stake, with Pierre Jacques leading the business for several years before becoming honorary president. Flageollet remains in charge of creative and technical direction.

De Bethune produces only a few hundred watches a year with a team of under a hundred people, making almost every component in-house, and remains one of the most distinctive voices in independent watchmaking.

name: Delma
tagline: Family-owned Lengnau diver specialist with the 5,000 m Blue Shark
summary: Delma is a family-owned Swiss watchmaker founded in 1924 in Lengnau near Biel, known for robust dive watches such as the Periscope, Shell Star, Quattro and the Blue Shark, rated to an extreme 5,000 metres. Owned by the Wüthrich family since 1966, it offers serious tool watches at mid-range prices.
history:
Delma's story began in 1924, when brothers Adolf and Albert Gilomen founded A. & A. Gilomen S.A. in Lengnau, near Biel. One of the company's original models was named Delma, and the name soon became the brand itself. In 1946 the firm introduced its first chronograph, the Midland, in 18k yellow gold.

In 1966 the company was taken over by Ulrich Wüthrich and partners and renamed Delma Watch Ltd. Under Wüthrich, Delma moved decisively into sports and dive watches: the Periscope arrived in 1969, followed in the 1970s by the Shell Star and Quattro professional divers, whose rugged designs found favour with divers and collectors alike. The distinctive Shark model, with its rectangular case, debuted in 1981, and Delma survived the quartz era by combining mechanical and quartz production and maintaining broad international distribution.

In the 21st century Delma has concentrated on its diving heritage. The Blue Shark line, introduced in 2011, evolved through several generations with ever-greater water resistance, culminating in the 47 mm Blue Shark IV rated to 5,000 metres, one of the most water-resistant production watches available. Alongside it, Delma offers reissues and modern versions of the Shell Star, Quattro, Periscope, Commodore, Cayman and Santiago. Now led by the second and third generations of the Wüthrich family, Delma remains fully independent after a century in business, celebrating its centenary in 2024.

name: Doxa
tagline: The orange-dial dive watch pioneer since 1967
summary: Doxa is a Swiss watchmaker founded in 1889 whose SUB 300 of 1967 was one of the first professional dive watches offered to the public. Famous for its orange dials, cushion cases and no-decompression bezel, it remains a cult favourite among divers and tool-watch fans at accessible prices.
history:
Doxa was founded in 1889 in Le Locle by 21-year-old Georges Ducommun. The name, Greek for 'glory', gained recognition when an anti-magnetic Doxa pocket watch won a gold medal at the 1906 Milan World's Fair, and in 1907 the brand patented an eight-day movement that later equipped dashboard clocks, including in Bugatti cars. By the mid-century Doxa was a respected producer of dress and everyday watches, including the Bauhaus-inspired Grafic line.

In 1967 Doxa launched the SUB 300, developed with input from professional divers and with ties to Jacques-Yves Cousteau's circle. Its orange dial, chosen after tests showed orange was the most legible colour underwater, and its patented unidirectional bezel with a US Navy no-decompression table made it a genuine professional tool. The 1968 SUB 300T Conquistador was among the first dive watches with a helium release valve, and from 1973 novelist Clive Cussler put an orange Doxa on the wrist of his hero Dirk Pitt.

The quartz crisis hit Doxa hard and the brand became part of the Synchron group alongside Cyma and Ernest Borel, with production dwindling through the late 1970s and 1980s. In 1997 the Jenny family, watchmakers for four generations, acquired Doxa and moved its headquarters to Biel/Bienne. Faithful reissues of the SUB 300, SUB 300T and SUB 600T fuelled a revival, and under CEO Jan Edöcs and the Walca Group the brand has expanded internationally with carbon, titanium and GMT variants while keeping prices in the tool-watch sweet spot.

name: Ebel
tagline: The 'architects of time' and their wave-link bracelets
summary: Ebel is a La Chaux-de-Fonds watchmaker founded in 1911 and owned by the Movado Group since 2004. It is best known for the 1977 Sport Classic with its wave-shaped bracelet links and five-screw bezel, and for the Beluga ladies' watches.
history:
Ebel was founded in 1911 in La Chaux-de-Fonds by husband and wife Eugène Blum and Alice Lévy, and its name is formed from their initials: Eugène Blum et Lévy. Alice Lévy was closely involved in design and the business, and the company quickly established itself as a maker of fine watches. Their son Charles Blum took over in 1929 and expanded international sales.

The third generation, Pierre-Alain Blum, took charge in 1970 and transformed the company. Ebel manufactured watches for Cartier and, in 1977, launched the Sport Classic, whose integrated bracelet of wave-shaped links and screwed bezel became the brand's signature. In the early 1980s Ebel bought a stock of El Primero chronograph components from Zenith, producing its Calibre 134 chronograph, and Pierre-Alain Blum marketed the brand with the slogan 'the architects of time'. For the company's 75th anniversary in 1986, Ebel bought and restored the Villa Turque, designed by Le Corbusier in La Chaux-de-Fonds. Don Johnson's Sonny Crockett wore an Ebel on Miami Vice, and the 1911 chronograph and Beluga became hits of the 1980s and 90s.

The boom did not last. Ebel was sold to the investment firm Investcorp in 1994 and to LVMH in 1999. In 2004 the Movado Group bought it, repositioning Ebel as an accessible luxury brand with a strong focus on women's watches.

Today Ebel's collections centre on the Sport Classic, the Wave and the Beluga, with most models quartz-powered and sold through the Movado Group's distribution network.

name: echo/neutra
tagline: Dolomites-inspired, Swiss-made watches from an Italian architect and aerospace engineer
summary: echo/neutra is an independent Italian brand created by architect-designer Nicola Callegaro and aerospace engineer Cristiano Quaglia. Its Swiss Made watches, powered by Sellita and ETA movements, range from the Dolomites-inspired Averau field watches and 500m Cristallo diver to 1950s-style 1956 chronographs and the ultra-thin titanium Rivanera, with a studio in Milan.
history:
echo/neutra was founded by two northern Italians with very different backgrounds. Nicola Callegaro is an architect and brand strategist who founded the design practice Zeppelin Studio in 2008 and has worked in object design for almost 20 years; Cristiano Quaglia is an aerospace engineer with a master's degree in propulsion systems and a passion for mountaineering in the Dolomites. Together they set out to create objects with 'a soul', balancing function and form, and to make watches that are 'not replicated, not repeated' and always unconventional.

The mountains became the brand's first muse. Its Averau collection, named after a Dolomite peak, is a contemporary field watch whose best-known version carries a 'Big Moon' moon phase in which a large convex moon rotates on itself, indicating the lunar phase both graphically and in text. The Cristallo, also named after a Dolomite massif, is a Swiss Made professional diver rated to 500m with a helium valve, ceramic no-decompression bezel, small seconds and power-reserve display from a Sellita SW279 movement.

echo/neutra then broadened its range with the 1956 collection, vintage-inspired chronographs and GMTs drawing on the 1950s and 1960s, including a hand-wound Sellita SW510 chronograph with ceramic telemeter bezel, and the Rivanera, an Art Deco-influenced dress-sports watch in Grade 5 titanium only 5.5mm thick and weighing 21 grams, powered by an ETA 7001. The company, ENCQ Srl, later opened Studio Milano, its first dedicated boutique space, in central Milan, and continues to release colourways and one-of-a-kind pieces in small numbers.

name: Edox
tagline: 'The Water Champion' since the 1961 Delfin
summary: Edox is an independent Swiss watchmaker founded in 1884 in Biel and now based in Les Genevez in the Jura. Known for water-resistance innovations like the Delfin and Hydro-Sub, record-thin movements and motorsport chronographs, it produces around 30,000–40,000 watches a year under the Strambini family.
history:
Edox was founded in 1884 in Biel/Bienne by Christian Rüefli-Flury, a watchmaker from Grenchen. The name derives from ancient Greek for the 'measuring of time', and the hourglass logo appeared around 1900. After the founder's death in 1921, Robert Kaufmann-Hug took over and steered production toward wristwatches.

In 1961 Edox launched the Delfin, whose double caseback, special gaskets and double O-ring system gave it outstanding water resistance, earning Edox its 'Water Champion' slogan. The 1965 Hydro-Sub introduced a crown system with tension ring and shock-absorbing gasket rated to 500 metres, and in 1970 the Geoscope offered a world-time display. The brand also built the Chronorally and other racing-inspired chronographs.

The quartz crisis forced Edox to sell its shares to ASUAG, a forerunner of the Swatch Group, in 1973. In 1983 company president Victor Strambini bought back all the shares, making Edox independent again, and relocated it to Les Genevez in the Jura mountains. There it built a reputation for technical feats, notably the Les Bémonts Ultra Slim of 1998 with a 1.4 mm movement, a record thickness the brand still claims. From 2010 Edox became official timekeeper of the World Rally Championship and later the Dakar Rally, and it has partnered with motorsport and powerboat racing. Now led by CEO Alexandre Strambini, the family-owned company makes 30,000–40,000 watches a year, split between Ronda quartz and Sellita-based automatics, sold in more than 60 markets.

name: Elgin
tagline: Illinois giant that built half of America's pocket watches
summary: The Elgin National Watch Company, founded in 1864, ran the world's largest watchmaking complex in Elgin, Illinois, and made about half of all pocket watches produced in the United States. US manufacturing ended in 1968; the Elgin name has since been sold several times and is now used by MZ Berger on inexpensive fashion watches with no link to the original company.
history:
The National Watch Company was founded in Chicago in 1864 by a group of businessmen led by former Chicago mayor Benjamin W. Raymond, and it built its factory in the town of Elgin, Illinois. Its first watch, the B.W. Raymond, appeared in 1867. The company was renamed the Elgin National Watch Company in 1874, adopting the name its customers already used.

Elgin grew into a giant. By the 1920s its Elgin plant covered more than 21 acres and employed over 4,000 people, and the company eventually produced roughly half of all pocket watches made in the US. It supplied railroad-grade models, built the Elgin Observatory in 1910 to set time precisely, and turned to military production during the Second World War, making watches and precision instruments for US forces. Its Lord Elgin line became a well-known American wristwatch brand in the mid-20th century.

Foreign competition and changing tastes hit hard after the war. The original Plant No. 1 closed in 1964, and all US watch manufacturing ended in 1968. The Elgin name was sold and resold, and the current owner, MZ Berger & Co., uses it on affordable imported watches. Collectors, however, value original Elgin pocket watches and wristwatches, and many surviving movements are now rebuilt into wristwatches by companies such as Vortic.

name: Emporio Armani
tagline: Milanese minimalism for the wrist, made by Fossil since 1997
summary: Emporio Armani is the younger, more accessible line of Giorgio Armani's Milan fashion house. Its watches, designed and distributed by Fossil Group under licence since 1997, range from sleek quartz chronographs to open-heart automatics, solar World Explorers and a Swiss Made line.
history:
Giorgio Armani founded his fashion company in Milan in 1975 with his partner Sergio Galeotti, and in 1981 launched Emporio Armani, a younger, more affordable diffusion line identified by its eagle logo. The label became a pillar of the Armani empire, extending into denim, fragrance, eyewear and accessories through a network of licences.

Watches arrived in 1997, when the Armani Group signed Fossil to design, develop and distribute timepieces under the Emporio Armani name. The partnership grew steadily: jewellery was added in the early 2000s, Armani Exchange watches in 2008, and in 2014 the companies extended their global licence for ten years and launched Emporio Armani Swiss Made, a higher-priced collection produced in Switzerland. Emporio Armani watches became best-sellers in department stores and duty-free shops worldwide, known for clean dials, black-and-steel chronographs and, later, black ceramic cases.

In the smartwatch era Fossil produced Emporio Armani Connected touchscreen and hybrid smartwatches, while the core range shifted toward value mechanicals such as the open-heart Meccanico automatics and, more recently, solar-powered World Explorer and Sea Explorer models. Giorgio Armani led the company as sole shareholder and designer until his death in September 2025, after which ownership passed under the arrangements of his will and the Giorgio Armani Foundation. Emporio Armani watches continue to be made and sold by Fossil Group.

name: Enicar
tagline: 'Racine' reversed: the Sherpa tool watches that went to Everest
summary: Enicar was a major Swiss watch manufacturer founded in 1913 by the Racine family, best known for its Sherpa line of compressor-cased divers, chronographs and GMTs. The Swiss company collapsed in the quartz crisis; the name has been owned since 1988 by Hong Kong's Wah Ming Hong and is sold mainly in Asia.
history:
Enicar was founded in 1913 by Ariste Racine, whose family had been watchmakers since the 19th century; the brand name is simply 'Racine' spelled backwards. The company grew into a sizable manufacture based in Lengnau near Biel, producing its own movements and building a strong export network, notably in China where it was distributed from the 1930s by Hong Kong's Wah Ming Hong.

Enicar's golden era came in the 1950s and 1960s. In 1956 a Swiss expedition wore Enicar watches on the first ascent of Lhotse and the second ascent of Everest, and the brand promptly launched the Sherpa line. Sherpa models used EPSA 'Super Compressor' cases with twin crowns and internal rotating bezels, and included the Sherpa Super-Dive, the Sherpa Graph and Super Graph chronographs, the Sherpa Jet and Super Jet GMTs and the Sherpa Date. Enicar promoted its 'Ultrasonic' movement cleaning process and Seapearl waterproof cases, and its chronographs were worn in motorsport, while tennis champion Ken Rosewall wore a Sherpa Date.

The quartz crisis devastated Enicar. After years of losses the Swiss company ceased operations in the late 1980s, and in 1988 Wah Ming Hong acquired the trademark. Under Hong Kong ownership Enicar became one of the best-known imported watch brands in China, selling mainly quartz and Sellita-powered mechanical watches through Asian distribution while advertising itself as 'Enicar of Switzerland'. Outside Asia the brand is known almost entirely through vintage Sherpas, which have become sought-after collector pieces.

name: Ernest Borel
tagline: The 'dancing couple' brand and its kaleidoscope Cocktail watch
summary: Ernest Borel is a Swiss watchmaker founded in Neuchâtel in 1856 by Jules Borel, known for its dancing-couple logo and the kaleidoscopic Cocktail watch of the 1950s. Owned by Chinese investors since the late 1990s, it is a major Swiss brand in China and other Asian markets.
history:
Ernest Borel was founded in 1856 in Neuchâtel by Jules Borel, working with his brother-in-law Paul Courvoisier. The young company built a reputation for precision: it won first place at the Neuchâtel observatory chronometry competition in 1866 and took awards at the 1876 Philadelphia and 1878 Paris exhibitions. The business passed to Jules's son Ernest Borel, whose name it carries.

In the 1950s the brand created one of its most distinctive designs, the Cocktail watch, whose dial pattern appears to shift like a kaleidoscope as the wearer moves the wrist. It became an emblem of the brand in Asia, alongside the logo of a dancing couple that signifies romance and togetherness. Ernest Borel had been distributed in China and Hong Kong since the early 20th century and became a well-known Swiss name there.

The Borel family ran the company until 1975, when, during the quartz crisis, it joined the Synchron group with Doxa and Cyma. In 1997 Chinese investors bought the brand, which was later listed in Hong Kong as Ernest Borel Holdings, and in 2018 Hong Kong-based Citychamp Watch & Jewellery Group acquired a controlling interest. Now based in Le Noirmont in the Jura, Ernest Borel focuses on traditionally styled automatic and quartz watches for men and women, including the Cocktail, Retro, Heartful and Sage collections, with most of its sales in Greater China and Southeast Asia.

name: Eterna
tagline: The Grenchen innovator that gave birth to ETA
summary: Eterna is a Grenchen watchmaker founded in 1856 whose movement division became ETA, today the backbone of the Swatch Group. Famous for the ball-bearing Eterna-Matic rotor and the KonTiki divers, it has been owned by Hong Kong's Citychamp group since 2011.
history:
Eterna was founded on 7 November 1856 in Grenchen by physician Dr Josef Girard and teacher Urs Schild as the ébauche workshop Dr. Girard & Schild. The company became Schild Frères & Co. and, after launching its own finished watches, adopted the Eterna name in 1905. It was an early innovator: in 1908 it patented one of the first wristwatch alarms, and it made some of the earliest wristwatches for women.

In 1932, amid restructuring of the Swiss watch industry, Eterna's movement production was separated into a distinct company, ETA. ETA went on to become the dominant supplier of Swiss movements and, through ASUAG and the 1983 merger with SSIH, the industrial core of the Swatch Group, while Eterna continued as a watch brand.

In 1948 Eterna introduced the Eterna-Matic, whose rotor ran on five tiny ball bearings to reduce friction; the five balls became the brand's logo. When Thor Heyerdahl's 1947 Kon-Tiki raft expedition crossed the Pacific, Eterna watches were aboard, and in 1958 the brand launched the KonTiki sports watch, followed by divers such as the Super KonTiki. The Eterna-Matic 3000 Dato of 1962 was billed as the thinnest automatic men's watch with a date.

After the quartz crisis Eterna changed hands several times. In 1995 it was bought by the Porsche family, and it manufactured Porsche Design watches until the partnership ended in 2014. In 2011 it was acquired by China Haidian, later renamed Citychamp Watch & Jewellery Group. Eterna remains based in Grenchen, focusing on KonTiki, Heritage and Eternity collections; unlike stablemate Corum, it stayed with Citychamp after 2025.

name: F.P. Journe
tagline: Invenit et Fecit: one man's inventions, built in 18k gold movements in Geneva
summary: F.P. Journe is the Geneva manufacture of French-born watchmaker François-Paul Journe, famed for resonance chronometers, remontoir tourbillons and solid rose-gold movements. With under a thousand watches a year and huge collector demand, it is widely regarded as the most successful independent of its generation.
history:
François-Paul Journe was born in Marseille in 1957 and trained at the Paris watchmaking school before working in his uncle's restoration workshop. There he built his first tourbillon pocket watch by hand, and through the 1980s and early 1990s he made unique pocket watches and developed movements for other houses from his own workshop, later based in Geneva.

In 1999 he launched watches under his own name with the Tourbillon Souverain, a wristwatch tourbillon with a constant-force remontoir. It was followed in 2000 by the Chronomètre à Résonance, the first serially produced wristwatch using two balances that fall into acoustic resonance. The Octa automatic platform, with a 120-hour reserve, spawned a family of complications. From 2004 the brand switched to movements made entirely in 18k rose gold, a signature that remains unique among manufactures. Journe signs his dials 'Invenit et Fecit' - invented and made.

The company is still controlled by Journe, but in 2018 Chanel acquired a 20% minority stake in Montres Journe SA, pledging to preserve its independence. Collections now span the Classique line (Chronomètre Bleu, Résonance, Tourbillon Souverain, Astronomic Souveraine), the sporty LineSport, the Octa family, and the quartz-powered Élégante with its motion-sensing standby mode.

The brand makes under a thousand watches a year from its Geneva manufacture and its own case and dial suppliers, sells primarily through its own boutiques, and its pieces regularly trade well above retail at auction, where unique and early pieces have fetched millions.

name: Farer
tagline: British design, Swiss-made movements and a riot of colour
summary: Farer is an independent British watch company launched in 2015 and based in Berkshire, combining bold colours, textured dials and vintage-inspired cases with Swiss-made movements. Its direct-to-consumer range spans GMTs, compressor-style divers, racing chronographs, pilots and dress three-handers.
history:
Farer was incorporated in November 2014 by Paul Sweetenham, a designer and watch enthusiast, and launched its first collection in 2015. The founding idea was to revive the spirit of the 'halcyon era' of mid-century watchmaking, when bold colours and contrasting textures met serious craftsmanship, but to deliver it through a modern, direct-to-consumer model with no discounting. The brand's name evokes wayfaring and exploration, and many of its watches are named after explorers, ships and expeditions.

From the start Farer paired British design with Swiss manufacturing, working with Swiss partners on prototyping and production and fitting movements from Sellita and La Joux-Perret. Its signature became unexpected colour combinations: sea-green sunray dials with pillar-box red GMT hands, burnt-orange seconds hands, bronze crown caps and multi-level dials. The range grew to more than 40 models across a dozen collections, including the Lander GMT, the titanium Aqua Compressor divers with internal rotating bezels, hand-wound racing chronographs, pilot watches, world timers and a 35mm cushion-case line.

Farer has remained independent and founder-led, operating from an appointment-only showroom in the Berkshire countryside between Ascot and Bracknell. It offers a five-year movement guarantee, free worldwide shipping and complimentary engraving, and has become one of the best-known names in the wave of British independent brands that emerged in the 2010s.

name: Favre-Leuba
tagline: One of Switzerland's oldest watch names, now revived in Le Locle
summary: Favre-Leuba traces its roots to 1737 in Le Locle, making it one of the oldest Swiss watch brands. Known for pioneering mechanical altimeter and depth-gauge watches (the Bivouac and Bathy), it has been relaunched since 2024 under CEO Patrik Hoffmann with backing from Indian retailer Ethos.
history:
Favre-Leuba's story begins in 1737, when Abraham Favre registered as a watchmaker in Le Locle. His descendants built the business over generations, and in 1815 Frédéric Favre partnered with Auguste Leuba, giving the company its lasting name. Favre-Leuba became an early exporter, and from the 19th century it built a strong presence in India, where it remained a household name for generations.

In the 1960s the firm produced a remarkable run of tool watches. The 1962 Bivouac was the first mechanical wristwatch with an aneroid barometer-altimeter, measuring altitude up to 3,000 metres, and the 1968 Bathy included a mechanical depth gauge for divers. The Twin-Power calibre of the same era used two mainspring barrels to extend power reserve, and the Sea King and Sea Chief became popular export models.

The quartz crisis brought decline, and the family sold the brand in the 1980s; it passed through Benedom (LVMH) before Indian conglomerate Tata acquired it in 2011. Tata's 2016–2017 relaunch produced the Raider Harpoon and a modern Bivouac 9000 altimeter watch but was halted after a few years. In 2023–2024 the brand passed to new owners linked to Indian luxury watch retailer Ethos, which put industry veteran Patrik Hoffmann, formerly of Ulysse Nardin, in charge. Relaunched at Geneva Watch Days 2024, Favre-Leuba quickly rolled out Chief, Harpoon Revival and Sky Raider collections, presented its first tourbillon in 2025 and joined Watches and Wonders in 2026. India remains its largest market.

name: Fears
tagline: Bristol watchmaker from 1846, revived by the founder's great-great-grandson
summary: Fears was founded in Bristol in 1846 by Edwin Fear and made watches for 130 years before closing in 1976. Revived in 2016 by Nicholas Bowman-Scargill, it is known for the curvaceous cushion-cased Brunswick and small-batch watches hand-built in Britain.
history:
Edwin Fear founded the company in Bristol in 1846, on Redcliff Street, and it grew into a respected watch and jewellery business supplying pocket and then wrist watches under the Fears name. By the 1920s and 1930s the company was producing elegant cushion and rectangular wristwatches, several of which inspire today's designs, including a 1924 gentleman's cushion-case watch and a 1930 art deco rectangular piece.

Like much of the British watch trade, Fears was hit by changing markets in the post-war decades, and the business closed in 1976.

In 2016 Nicholas Bowman-Scargill, the great-great-grandson of Edwin Fear, relaunched the brand in Bristol. The first new models were the modestly priced Redcliff, named after the street where the company was founded, followed by the Brunswick, whose cushion case has no flat surfaces and a signature onion crown. In 2021 the brand celebrated its 175th anniversary with the Archival 1930, a proportional recreation of a 1930 rectangular watch using original vintage movements.

Fears now hand-builds its watches in small batches in Bristol and has expanded with the Brunswick 38, 40 and 40.5 Jump Hour (the latter using a Christopher Ward JJ01 module) and the Redcliff 39.5 with La Joux-Perret movements, winning a following among collectors for its refined, understated style.

name: Fiyta
tagline: China's space watch, worn on Shenzhou missions since 2003
summary: FIYTA is a Shenzhen watchmaker controlled by the state aerospace group AVIC and best known for supplying the watches used on China's crewed Shenzhou space missions. It is one of China's largest watch brands and also runs a major watch retail network.
history:
FIYTA was established in Shenzhen in 1987, growing out of the aviation industry's move into precision consumer products. It became one of the leading domestic watch brands during China's economic opening, and its parent company, FIYTA Precision Technology, is listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange with the Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC) as its controlling shareholder.

The brand's defining moment came on 15 October 2003, when a FIYTA space watch accompanied Yang Liwei, China's first astronaut, on Shenzhou 5; the watch was used to time spacesuit leak checks. FIYTA has since supplied watches for subsequent crewed missions, developing a manual-wound mechanical space movement with AM/PM display and timing functions, and markets its record of zero functional failures in space.

In 2011 FIYTA became the first Chinese watch brand invited to exhibit in Hall 1 at Baselworld. It pioneered titanium and carbon-fibre cases in China from 2007, and in 2016 it reportedly took control of the historic Beijing Watch Factory. Today its range covers the Space collection (Mars-500, Space Shuttle, Spacewalk), elegant women's watches, and classic and diver lines, alongside its Harmony watch retail business.

name: Formex
tagline: Biel independent with a patented shock-absorbing case suspension
summary: Formex is a family-owned independent watchmaker founded in Biel in 1999, known for its patented Case Suspension System that cushions the movement from shocks. Its Essence, Reef and Field models offer COSC-certified Swiss automatics at aggressive prices, and it now makes its own micro-rotor calibre.
history:
Formex was founded in 1999 in Biel/Bienne, initially building a reputation for sporty, design-led watches, including chronographs with motorsport themes, and for manufacturing expertise it also offered to other brands. The company is family-owned and has always emphasised in-house design and engineering over heritage storytelling.

Formex's signature innovation is its patented Case Suspension System, in which the inner case holding the movement is mounted on a shock-absorbing suspension within an outer structure. The system protects the movement from impacts while letting the watch sit comfortably and flex slightly with wrist movement. Formex also developed quick-release straps and bracelets, micro-adjustable carbon-fibre clasps and tool-free interchangeable bezels.

The brand's modern breakthrough came in 2019 with the Essence, launched with a strong direct-to-consumer approach and offering a COSC-certified chronometer, sapphire crystal, ceramic or carbon options and the suspension case at a price rarely seen for Swiss chronometers. It was followed by the Reef dive watch with 300 m water resistance and swappable bezels, the lightweight Essence Leggera, the titanium Field Automatic, the Stratos UTC and the Essence ThirtyNine. In 2024 Formex presented the Aria, powered by its first manufacture calibre, the FX01 micro-rotor. Today Formex is one of the most closely watched independent brands in the accessible-luxury segment.

name: Fortis
tagline: Grenchen tool watches tested in space since 1994
summary: Fortis is a Grenchen watchmaker founded in 1912 that made the first mass-produced automatic wristwatch with John Harwood in 1926 and supplied Russia's cosmonauts from 1994. Since 2018 owner-CEO Jupp Philipp has rebuilt it around bold Flieger, Marinemaster and Stratoliner tool watches.
history:
Fortis was founded in 1912 by Walter Vogt in Grenchen, in the canton of Solothurn. In 1926 the company worked with British inventor John Harwood to produce the first serially manufactured automatic wristwatch, using Harwood's hammer-style self-winding system, an achievement shown at the Basel fair that year. Fortis introduced chronographs in 1937 and water-resistant models in 1943, and built a line of robust pilot and sport watches through the post-war decades.

Fortis became closely associated with spaceflight. After tests connected with early space programmes, it became from 1994 the supplier of watches for crewed missions authorised by the Russian space agency, and the Official Cosmonauts Chronograph, powered by the Lemania 5100, became standard issue on the Mir and later the International Space Station. Fortis also won the 2004 European Aviation Watch Award and produced notable art editions with painters and designers.

The brand struggled financially in the 2010s and underwent a debt restructuring around 2017. German investor and watch enthusiast Jupp Philipp acquired Fortis, renaming the company Fortis Watches AG and becoming CEO. He reorganised the range into 'Space, Sky and Sea' pillars with in-house-developed WERK calibres built on Swiss ébauches, launching the Flieger F-39/F-41/F-43, the colourful Marinemaster M-40 and M-44 divers, the dust-textured Stratoliner chronographs and the stratospheric-flight-tested Novonaut. The relaunch, featuring the chunky 'Block' bracelet, has made Fortis a favourite among modern tool-watch enthusiasts.

name: Fossil
tagline: Texas-born fashion-watch giant behind Fossil, Skagen and dozens of licensed labels
summary: Fossil was founded in 1984 by Tom Kartsotis in Texas and grew into Fossil Group, one of the world's largest makers of fashion watches, both its own brands and licences such as Michael Kors, Armani Exchange and Diesel. After a costly move into smartwatches, it left that market in 2024 and has been restructuring its business.
history:
Tom Kartsotis founded Overseas Products International in Dallas in 1984, importing inexpensive watches from Asia; the Fossil brand's name came from a nickname for his father. With retro-styled designs, strong branding and distinctive tin packaging, Fossil became a hit in American department stores, and brother Kosta Kartsotis joined to lead its growth. The company went public in 1993 and later renamed itself Fossil Group.

Fossil expanded by buying brands such as Zodiac, Michele and Skagen, and by manufacturing licensed watches for fashion houses including Emporio Armani, Diesel, DKNY and Michael Kors, whose watch boom in the early 2010s drove revenue to record highs. Headquartered in Richardson, Texas, it became one of the largest watch companies outside Switzerland and Japan.

As smartphones cut into fashion-watch demand, Fossil bought wearables start-up Misfit for $260 million in 2015 and produced Wear OS smartwatches and hybrid watches for many of its brands; in 2019 it sold some smartwatch technology to Google. Sales kept falling, and in January 2024 the company said it would leave the smartwatch business. Franco Fogliato became CEO in September 2024, 2024 revenue was about $1.14 billion, and in 2025 the group went through a debt restructuring that included UK proceedings recognised in the US under Chapter 15.

name: Franck Muller
tagline: Genthod's 'Master of Complications' and the curved Cintrée Curvex case
summary: Franck Muller was founded in 1991 by watchmaker Franck Muller and entrepreneur Vartan Sirmakes, and grew rapidly on the strength of complicated movements and the curvaceous Cintrée Curvex tonneau case. Based at its Watchland campus in Genthod near Geneva, it is known for the Crazy Hours, Vanguard and Casablanca.
history:
Franck Muller, born in 1958 to a Swiss father and Italian mother, studied at the Geneva watchmaking school and worked restoring antique pieces for collectors and auction houses. In the late 1980s he built a series of highly complicated wristwatches under his own name, including tourbillons and a perpetual calendar with minute repeater, earning a reputation as a prodigy.

In 1991 he joined forces with Vartan Sirmakes, a case maker of Armenian origin, to found the Franck Muller company. The brand quickly defined its identity with the Cintrée Curvex, a tonneau case curved in three dimensions, and exuberant dials with stylised Arabic numerals. The company built its headquarters, Watchland, a château-style campus at Genthod on the shores of Lake Geneva, and rapidly expanded into a group that included several smaller brands and component suppliers.

Throughout the 1990s and 2000s Franck Muller was among the fastest-growing Swiss brands, famous for the Master Banker with three time zones, the Long Island rectangular watch, the Conquistador sports line and, in 2003, the Crazy Hours, whose hour hand jumps between numerals placed out of order. In 2009 the Aeternitas Mega 4 was presented as the most complicated wristwatch in the world, with 36 complications.

The founders fell out publicly in the 2000s, and Sirmakes has since run the group. The Vanguard, a sportier Curvex design introduced in the 2010s, became a bestseller, and the brand remains privately owned, with a strong following in the Middle East and Asia.

name: Frederique Constant
tagline: Accessible Geneva manufacture watches, from Heart Beat to perpetual calendars
summary: Frederique Constant is a Geneva brand founded in 1988 by a Dutch couple with the aim of making 'accessible luxury'. It is known for in-house movements at unusually low prices, including moonphases and perpetual calendars, and has been owned by Citizen since 2016.
history:
Frederique Constant was founded in Geneva in 1988 by Peter Stas and Aletta Bax, a Dutch couple who wanted to offer traditionally crafted Swiss watches at accessible prices. They named the brand after two ancestors: Frédérique Schreiner, Aletta's great-grandmother, and Ferdinand Constant Stas, Peter's great-grandfather, who had run a clock-dial business. The first watches were assembled in small numbers and sold mainly in Europe and Asia.

The brand's breakthrough came in 1994 with the Heart Beat, whose dial aperture revealed the beating balance wheel, a feature that became a signature. Frederique Constant then set out to make its own movements, presenting the in-house Heart Beat Manufacture calibre FC-910 in 2004 and gradually developing a family of manufacture calibres, including chronographs, moonphases, a worldtimer and a tourbillon. In 2002 the company also bought the historic sports-watch brand Alpina, and it later moved into a larger manufacture in Plan-les-Ouates, Geneva.

Frederique Constant earned a reputation for value: its Slimline Perpetual Calendar Manufacture, launched in 2016, was one of the most affordable Swiss in-house perpetual calendars. It also experimented with technology, launching a Horological Smartwatch in 2015 that kept an analogue display while tracking activity and sleep.

In 2016 the Stas family sold Frederique Constant, together with Alpina and Ateliers deMonaco, to Japan's Citizen Watch Co., with Peter Stas staying on for a period. In 2021 the brand unveiled the Slimline Monolithic Manufacture with a high-frequency flexure-based silicon oscillator. The Classics, Slimline, Highlife and Manufacture lines remain its core.

name: G-Shock
tagline: The toughest watch ever made, born from a dropped watch in 1983
summary: G-Shock is Casio's shock-resistant watch brand and a global cultural phenomenon, spanning $100 resin squares to titanium MR-G pieces. Engineered around a floating module inside a hollow resin case, it has sold well over 100 million units and dominates street, military and outdoor culture.
history:
G-Shock began in 1981 when Casio engineer Kikuo Ibe dropped and broke a watch his father had given him. He proposed a watch that would survive a 10-metre drop, offer 10-bar water resistance and a 10-year battery, the 'Triple 10' concept. His small 'Project Team Tough' tested around 200 prototypes, famously dropping them from a third-floor bathroom window, before hitting on a module 'floating' inside a hollow, shock-absorbing structure.

The first G-Shock, the square DW-5000C, launched in April 1983. Sales were slow until an American TV ad showing a G-Shock being used as a hockey puck caught attention, and the brand was adopted by skaters, surfers, police and soldiers. Keanu Reeves wore a DW-5600 in the 1994 film Speed, and the 1990s brought the Frogman diver, the Mudman and collaborations with street and fashion labels.

Tough Solar and Multi-Band 6 radio timekeeping arrived in the 2000s, followed by Bluetooth. Casio reached 100 million cumulative G-Shock shipments in 2017. The octagonal GA-2100, nicknamed the 'CasiOak', became a 2019 sensation, and the full-metal GMW-B5000 and titanium MR-G lines took the square design upmarket.

G-Shock accounts for roughly half of Casio's timepiece sales and ships over a million and a half watches per quarter.

name: Gallet
tagline: The 1826 chronograph pioneer reborn by Breitling for its bicentenary
summary: Gallet is a historic Swiss chronograph and timer maker founded in La Chaux-de-Fonds in 1826, famous for the 1939 Flying Officer with its world-time bezel and the MultiChron chronographs. Acquired by Breitling, it was relaunched in 2026 as an accessible sister brand with travel- and aviation-themed collections.
history:
Gallet & Co. was established in 1826 by Julien Gallet in La Chaux-de-Fonds, though the Gallet family traces watchmaking roots in Geneva back to the 15th century. Julien's son Léon expanded the business into the United States from the 1850s, and in 1890 his grandson Jules Racine founded Jules Racine & Co. in New York as the exclusive US distributor. After acquiring the Electa watch company in 1907, Gallet grew into one of the leading producers of stopwatches and professional timers; by the 1930s it supplied a large share of the timers used in America, and its timers are associated with timing pioneering aviation, including the Wright Brothers' era.

In 1939 Gallet introduced the Flying Officer, described as the first chronograph wristwatch with a multiple time zone calculator on a rotating bezel. An early example was presented to Senator, later President, Harry S. Truman. The MultiChron family followed, spanning pilot, racing, yachting and waterproof 'clamshell' chronographs, and Gallet was a favourite of military and motorsport users through the 1960s.

The quartz crisis and a shrinking market for mechanical timers reduced the company to a niche player, and it left family ownership in 1994, continuing at small scale under various owners. In 2025 Breitling acquired the name, adding it to a 'house of brands' alongside Universal Genève. Gallet relaunched in 2026, exactly 200 years after its founding, with four collections: the Flying Officer, Multichron Pilot, Multichron Sport and the Gallet Classics, the last powered by Breitling's manufacture B09 calibre. Positioned below Breitling in price, the new Gallet leans on a 'wanderlust' identity rooted in aviation and travel.

name: Garmin
tagline: GPS pioneer turned king of sports and adventure smartwatches
summary: Garmin was founded in Kansas in 1989 by Gary Burrell and Min Kao and made its name in GPS navigation before becoming a leader in GPS sports watches. Its fēnix, Forerunner, Instinct and Venu lines lead the premium outdoor and fitness smartwatch market.
history:
Gary Burrell and Min Kao founded the company in 1989 in Lenexa, Kansas, as ProNav, later renaming it Garmin from their first names. Its early GPS receivers were used by aviators, sailors and the US military, and in the 2000s its car satnavs became a mass-market hit.

In 2003 Garmin launched the Forerunner 201, the first wrist-worn GPS training device for runners, creating a new category. As smartphones undercut car navigation, fitness and outdoor watches became central to Garmin's growth: the Forerunner for runners, the fēnix multisport adventure watch, the rugged Instinct and the lifestyle-focused Venu, plus the MARQ luxury line and specialist aviation, diving and marine watches.

Garmin bought DeLorme in 2016, adding the satellite messaging now built into some watches, and fitness-analytics firm Firstbeat in 2020. It became the leader in premium smartwatches costing over $500, known for long battery life, solar charging and detailed training metrics. Legally domiciled in Schaffhausen, Switzerland, since 2010 but operated from Olathe, Kansas, Garmin reported revenue of about $7.25 billion in 2025 with around 23,000 employees. Garmin designs its own watch software and sensors, and much of its manufacturing is done in its own facilities in Taiwan.

name: Garrick
tagline: Norwich workshop hand-making dials, hands and movement parts for British fine watches
summary: Garrick is a small British watchmaker founded by David Brailsford and Simon Michlmayr, based in Norwich, Norfolk. It makes dials, hands and many movement parts in-house, using rose engines for guilloché and producing watches in very small numbers to order.
history:
Garrick was founded by David Brailsford and Simon Michlmayr with the ambition of building genuinely British fine watches, shunning mass production in favour of limited numbers of hand-finished pieces. The company set up its own workshop in Norfolk, where dials, hands and a multitude of movement components are made in-house, and its guilloché dials are engine-turned on historic rose and straight-line engines.

In 2016 Garrick released the Portsmouth, its first watch with an exclusive movement, the Calibre UT-G01, developed with a Swiss movement specialist. Further calibres followed, including the UT-G02 used in the Regulator with its visible free-sprung 'Trinity' balance.

The brand has since moved further into high horology with the S2 Deadbeat Seconds, powered by the Calibre DB-G06, and the S3, whose MK2 version has an openworked dial and the UT-G04 calibre with screwed chatons and black polishing. The more accessible S7 uses a modified vintage manual movement with a fully customisable engine-turned dial.

Garrick works from a clean-room workshop with positive air pressure in Norwich, building every watch to order, and has become one of the leading names in the small revival of British watchmaking.

tagline: Home of the Three Gold Bridges tourbillon and the octagonal Laureato
summary: Girard-Perregaux is a La Chaux-de-Fonds manufacture tracing its lineage to 1791, celebrated for the Tourbillon with Three Gold Bridges and the 1975 Laureato. After years under Kering, it was bought by its management in 2022 and is run alongside Ulysse Nardin within the Sowind Group.
history:
Girard-Perregaux dates its origins to 1791, when Jean-François Bautte, a Geneva watchmaker and jeweller, began signing his own timepieces. The modern name was born in 1856 after watchmaker Constant Girard married Marie Perregaux, daughter of a Le Locle watchmaking family, and set up Girard-Perregaux in La Chaux-de-Fonds. In 1906 the firm absorbed the Bautte business, uniting the two lineages.

Constant Girard's masterpiece was the Tourbillon with Three Gold Bridges, a pocket watch whose movement architecture reduced the bridges to three parallel gold arrows; it won a gold medal at the 1889 Paris Universal Exhibition and remains the house's emblem. Around 1880 the company produced early series wristwatches for officers of the German Imperial Navy, among the first wristwatches made in quantity.

In the 20th century the brand was an innovator in precision: the Gyromatic HF of 1966 was an early high-frequency automatic, and in 1970 Girard-Perregaux introduced a quartz movement running at 32,768 Hz, the frequency still used by almost all quartz watches. The Laureato, an octagonal-bezelled steel sports watch with integrated bracelet, followed in 1975.

The quartz crisis and changing ownership brought difficult years until Italian architect and racing driver Luigi Macaluso took control in 1992, restoring in-house manufacturing and launching the Sowind Group. The French group PPR, later Kering, acquired a majority stake from 2008 and full control in 2011, but in 2022 Kering sold Sowind, including Ulysse Nardin, to a management team led by Patrick Pruniaux. The Laureato was relaunched in 2016 and remains the brand's bestseller, alongside Bridges and the dressy 1966 collection.

name: Glashütte Original
tagline: Heir to Glashütte's state watch factory, now the Swatch Group's German manufacture
summary: Glashütte Original is the direct descendant of East Germany's nationalised watch combine GUB, privatised in 1994 and owned by the Swatch Group since 2000. It makes nearly everything in-house in Glashütte and is best known for its asymmetric Pano dials and Panorama Date big-date complication.
history:
Glashütte Original traces its roots to the Saxon watchmaking tradition that began in Glashütte in 1845. After the Second World War, the town's surviving firms, including Lange, were expropriated and in 1951 merged into the state-owned VEB Glashütter Uhrenbetriebe (GUB), which produced mass-market mechanical and later quartz watches for the Eastern Bloc for four decades.

With German reunification, GUB was converted into a limited company in 1990 and, in 1994, sold by the Treuhand privatisation agency to entrepreneur Heinz W. Pfeifer. The business was relaunched under the name Glashütte Original and repositioned as a maker of high-end mechanical watches, reviving historic calibres and developing new ones.

In 2000 the Swatch Group acquired the company, providing capital for a major expansion. Glashütte Original now produces its movements, dials (in its Pforzheim dial factory) and most components itself. Its signature designs include the PanoMatic family with its off-centre, asymmetrical dial layout, the Senator line of classic dress watches, and the retro-styled Sixties and Seventies collections.

The brand also supports local heritage: the Nicolas G. Hayek foundation established the German Watch Museum Glashütte in the company's former watchmaking school building in 2008. Glashütte Original continues to expand its line-up with dive watches such as the SeaQ and high complications including tourbillons and perpetual calendars.

name: Glycine
tagline: Makers of the 1953 Airman, the original pilot's GMT
summary: Glycine is a Swiss brand founded in Biel in 1914, celebrated for the 1953 Airman, a 24-hour pilot's watch that predated the Rolex GMT-Master and was used by US pilots in Vietnam and by astronaut Pete Conrad. Owned by Invicta Watch Group since 2016, it now sells Airman, Combat and Sea Kraken models at accessible prices.
history:
Glycine was founded in 1914 in Biel/Bienne by Eugène Meylan, who named the company after the wisteria flower (glycine in French). Early production focused on small, jewellery-like ladies' watches and innovative miniature movements, and in the 1930s Glycine developed one of the early automatic movements for wristwatches.

The brand's defining moment came in 1953 with the Airman, designed for airline pilots crossing multiple time zones. Its 24-hour dial, rotating 24-hour bezel locked by a crown at 4 o'clock and hacking seconds let pilots read a second time zone, and it reached the market a year before Rolex's GMT-Master. The Airman became standard kit for many US Air Force pilots during the Vietnam War, and in 1965 astronaut Pete Conrad wore one on the Gemini 5 mission.

The quartz crisis weakened Glycine, but it survived as an independent under Hans Hollenstein, who took over in 1984 and kept the Airman alive with new variants such as the Airman 7 and the Airman Base 22, along with Combat military-style watches and the Incursore. In 2016 the company was sold to Invicta Watch Group of Florida, which retained Swiss production while broadening distribution, especially through online retail. Today Glycine's collections include the Airman, the Combat Sub dive watches, the Combat field watches, the Airpilot and the Sea Kraken, sold mostly online at prices well below their official list prices.

name: Google (Pixel Watch / Fitbit)
tagline: Google's round Wear OS smartwatch, powered by Fitbit health tracking
summary: Google makes the Pixel Watch and owns Fitbit, the fitness-tracker pioneer it acquired in 2021. The domed, round Pixel Watch launched in 2022 and combines Wear OS with Fitbit's health and sleep tracking.
history:
Fitbit was founded in 2007 by James Park and Eric Friedman in San Francisco and popularised the clip-on and wrist-worn step counter. It went public in 2015, bought smartwatch start-up Pebble's software assets in 2016 and launched smartwatches such as the Ionic, Versa and Sense.

Google, founded in 1998 by Larry Page and Sergey Brin, had developed the Android Wear (later Wear OS) platform in 2014 for other manufacturers' watches. It announced a $2.1 billion deal for Fitbit in 2019, which closed in January 2021 after regulatory review, and in 2021 merged its smartwatch platform efforts with Samsung.

The first Google Pixel Watch launched in October 2022 with a round, domed design and Fitbit health features built in. Later generations added a larger 45 mm size, better battery life and satellite SOS, and in 2025 the Pixel Watch 4 was followed in 2026 by the Pixel Watch 5. Google continues to sell Fitbit trackers such as the Charge 6 alongside the Pixel Watch from its headquarters in Mountain View, California. The Pixel Watch is designed to work with Android phones and Google services, and many health features rely on a Fitbit subscription.

name: Graham
tagline: Left-handed Chronofighter trigger chronographs honouring George Graham
summary: Graham is a La Chaux-de-Fonds-based chronograph specialist founded in 1995 in homage to George Graham, the 18th-century London master who worked on early timing mechanisms. It is best known for the Chronofighter, with its oversized left-side trigger inspired by WWII RAF pilots' chronographs.
history:
The brand takes its name from George Graham (c.1673–1751), the English clock and instrument maker who apprenticed under Thomas Tompion, married his niece and succeeded him. Graham introduced the deadbeat escapement in precision regulators and invented the mercury pendulum, built early orreries and astronomical instruments for Greenwich, mentored Thomas Mudge and gave an interest-free loan to John Harrison. He is also credited by the brand with pioneering early timing devices that anticipate the chronograph. He is buried in Westminster Abbey alongside Tompion.

The modern Graham brand was established in 1995 in La Chaux-de-Fonds, adopting 1695, the year George Graham joined Tompion's workshop, as its heritage date. From the outset it focused on chronographs, and in 2001 it launched the Chronofighter, whose large lever-operated trigger on the left side of the case was inspired by devices used by British bomber pilots during World War II, allowing the chronograph to be started and stopped with a thumb even while wearing gloves.

The Chronofighter became the brand's identity, evolving into Oversize, Vintage, Superlight carbon and skeleton versions. Graham also created the Swordfish, with magnifying 'big eye' lenses over the subdials, the Silverstone motorsport chronographs, and the Geo.Graham Tourbillon Orrery, a haute horlogerie tribute to Graham's astronomical work. Graham sells largely direct and through selected retailers, with Chronofighter Vintage models forming its core range in 2026, the 25th anniversary of the Chronofighter.

name: Grand Seiko
tagline: Japanese nature, Zaratsu polish and the glide of Spring Drive
summary: Grand Seiko is Seiko's luxury marque, founded in 1960 to create the best watch possible. Known for razor-sharp Zaratsu polishing, nature-inspired dials and the unique Spring Drive movement, it has become the most credible Japanese challenger to Swiss luxury watchmaking.
history:
Grand Seiko was born in 1960 at Seiko's Suwa Seikosha factory with a simple aim: to make a watch as accurate, durable and beautiful as any in the world. The first Grand Seiko, a manually wound watch with a Chronometer-grade movement, was followed by landmark references such as the 44GS of 1967, whose design codified the 'Grand Seiko Style' of flat, mirror-polished surfaces and distortion-free reflections.

The brand thrived until the quartz revolution shifted Seiko's priorities; mechanical Grand Seiko production paused in the mid-1970s. It returned in 1988 with ultra-precise 9F quartz, and in 1998 the mechanical 9S caliber revived the line. In 2004 Spring Drive, a movement combining a mainspring with an electronic regulator and a gliding seconds hand, joined the range.

For decades Grand Seiko was largely sold in Japan. It began international distribution in 2010 and in 2017 became an independent brand, dropping the 'Seiko' name from the dial. Signature pieces like the 'Snowflake' SBGA211 and the 'White Birch' SLGH005 have won global acclaim, the latter taking a prize at the Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Genève in 2021.

Watches are made at the Shizukuishi Watch Studio in Iwate (mechanical) and the Shinshu Watch Studio in Nagano (Spring Drive and quartz). The 2022 Kodo constant-force tourbillon signalled its move into haute horlogerie.

name: Greubel Forsey
tagline: Inclined tourbillons and obsessive hand-finishing from La Chaux-de-Fonds
summary: Greubel Forsey was founded in 2004 by Robert Greubel and Stephen Forsey to push the tourbillon and chronometry further, starting with the Double Tourbillon 30°. Its watches, made in roughly 100-200 pieces a year, are benchmarks for hand finishing and among the most expensive regular-production watches in the world.
history:
Alsatian Robert Greubel and Englishman Stephen Forsey met at Renaud et Papi, the complication specialist, and in 2001 set up a development company to explore improving the tourbillon. Their first watch, the Double Tourbillon 30°, debuted at Baselworld 2004 with one tourbillon cage inclined at 30° spinning inside another, averaging out positional errors.

From a small workshop in La Chaux-de-Fonds the pair created the EWT (Experimental Watch Technology) research platform and developed the Tourbillon 24 Secondes, the Quadruple Tourbillon with differential, and from 2012 balance-wheel models such as the Double Balancier 35°. The Richemont group took a 20% minority stake in 2006 that the company later bought back. In 2019 its Hand Made 1 - a tourbillon made almost entirely by hand - redefined its artisanal ambitions.

The 2020s brought the Convexe line (Balancier Convexe S², GMT Balancier Convexe) and a change in leadership. CEO Antonio Calce departed in 2024, succeeded by long-time marketing head Michel Nydegger, and in February 2025 ownership was consolidated between the two founders, with Robert Greubel as chairman. Stephen Forsey was later removed from any operational role, while remaining a shareholder.

The company now makes around 200 watches a year from its La Chaux-de-Fonds atelier, with prices ranging from roughly $180,000 to around a million dollars.

name: Grönefeld
tagline: Dutch brothers building Swiss-grade constant-force watches in Oldenzaal
summary: Grönefeld is a Dutch independent run by brothers Bart and Tim Grönefeld in Oldenzaal, where their family has worked in horology since 1912. Their 1941 Remontoire and 1941 Grönograaf both won GPHG awards.
history:
The Grönefeld family's horological roots go back to 1912, when the brothers' grandfather established a watch and clock business in Oldenzaal in the east of the Netherlands. Bart and Tim Grönefeld trained at WOSTEP in Switzerland and then worked for years at Renaud et Papi (later Audemars Piguet Renaud & Papi), specialising in grand complications and tourbillons.

In 2008 the brothers launched watches under the Grönefeld name, producing complex pieces such as the Parallax Tourbillon and the dead-beat-seconds One Hertz, all assembled and finished in Oldenzaal. The 1941 Remontoire, introduced in 2016 with an eight-second constant-force remontoir, won the Men's Watch prize at the 2016 GPHG. The automatic 1941 Principia followed, and in 2022 the 1941 Grönograaf chronograph won another GPHG prize.

The brothers are AHCI members and produce very small numbers of watches; demand has at times been so high that the workshop has stopped accepting new orders. Recent designs include the 1969 DeltaWorks and the women's 1944 Tanfana. Everything from design to final hand-finishing is done in the family workshop, in the same town where the family business began more than a century ago.

name: Gucci
tagline: The first fashion house to make watches, now crafting Swiss high horology
summary: Gucci, the Florentine luxury house owned by Kering, entered watchmaking in 1972 and was the first high-fashion label to do so. Its Swiss-made watches range from logo-rich quartz pieces like the G-Timeless and skate-inspired Grip to the 25H sports-luxe line and high-watchmaking tourbillons.
history:
Guccio Gucci founded his leather-goods house in Florence in 1921, and by the 1950s-60s Gucci had become a global symbol of Italian luxury. In 1972, under Aldo Gucci, the house struck a licensing deal with Severin Wunderman, whose Severin Montres began producing Gucci watches in Switzerland. Gucci is widely described as the first high-fashion house to expand into watchmaking.

The partnership was an immediate hit. The Gucci Model 2000 quartz watch reportedly sold more than a million units in two years, earning a Guinness World Record in the mid-1970s. Through the 1980s and 1990s Gucci watches, including bangle watches and interchangeable-bezel designs, became department-store and duty-free staples. In 1997 Gucci bought Severin Montres outright, bringing watch design and production in-house in Switzerland. Soon afterwards Gucci itself came under the control of PPR, later renamed Kering.

In the 2000s the G-Timeless became the brand's core collection, while the Gucci Dive, first a limited edition in 2013, became a permanent line in 2015. Under creative director Alessandro Michele, Gucci's watches embraced maximalist symbols such as bees, snakes and stars, and the unisex, skateboard-inspired Grip of 2019 became a cult hit. In 2021 Gucci launched its first High Watchmaking collection, anchored by the slim, integrated-bracelet 25H, followed by tourbillons and planetarium complications for the house's 50th anniversary of watchmaking in 2022. Watches are designed in Neuchâtel and assembled at Kering's manufacture in La Chaux-de-Fonds, with dials made at Fabbrica Quadranti in Ticino.

name: GUESS
tagline: Los Angeles glamour in glitzy, bold fashion watches since 1983
summary: GUESS is the Los Angeles denim and lifestyle brand founded by the Marciano brothers in 1981. Its watches, introduced in 1983 and today designed, made and distributed by Timex Group, are known for bold, crystal-embellished and gold-tone designs such as the barrel-shaped Venix, with the pricier Gc line above them.
history:
GUESS was founded in Los Angeles in 1981 by brothers Georges, Maurice, Armand and Paul Marciano, who had emigrated from Morocco via France. Its first hit was a stonewashed, slim-fit denim with ankle zippers, and the brand's black-and-white advertising campaigns, which launched the careers of models such as Claudia Schiffer and Anna Nicole Smith, made GUESS a defining name in 1980s and 1990s fashion.

Watches were among the first licensed categories. GUESS watches were introduced in 1983, bringing the brand's sexy, glamorous aesthetic to the wrist with crystal-set bezels, gold-tone bracelets and bold, oversized cases. The watch business is managed by Timex Group, which designs, manufactures and distributes GUESS watches worldwide alongside its other fashion licences such as Versace and Ferragamo. A more premium, largely Swiss-made sister line, Gc (Guess Collection), sits above the core range.

GUESS itself went public on the New York Stock Exchange in 1996 and grew into a global retailer with around 1,600 stores and roughly US$3 billion in annual revenue. In 2025 Authentic Brands Group, together with Maurice and Paul Marciano and partner Alberini, agreed a take-private deal in which Authentic acquired a majority of the GUESS intellectual property; the company delisted in January 2026. The watches continue under Timex Group, with collections such as Modern Icons for women and the barrel-cased Venix for men, alongside a growing number of automatic models.
