name: H. Moser & Cie
tagline: Very rare Schaffhausen manufacture known for fumé dials and deadpan provocation
summary: H. Moser & Cie is a revived 19th-century house based in Neuhausen am Rheinfall, making in-house movements and hairsprings. Under the Meylan family it became famous for minimalist 'Concept' fumé dials, Vantablack pieces and satirical stunts.
history:
Heinrich Moser, a watchmaker's son from Schaffhausen, founded his firm in St Petersburg in 1828, selling high-quality pocket watches across the Russian Empire. He returned to Schaffhausen a wealthy industrialist, built hydraulic infrastructure on the Rhine and helped found the city's industrial base, while production for the Russian market continued from Le Locle.

After the 1917 revolution the Russian business was nationalised, and the Swiss operations passed through several hands before the name went dormant in the late 20th century. In 2005 the brand was revived in Schaffhausen by a group including Moser's great-grandson Roger Nicholas Balsiger and Dr. Jürgen Lange, launching with in-house calibres and an interchangeable escapement module. Sister company Precision Engineering AG gave Moser the rare ability to make its own hairsprings.

In 2012 the Meylan family's MELB Holding took over, and Edouard Meylan became CEO in 2013. Moser adopted the slogan 'Very Rare', stripped logos off many dials, and turned its signature gradient fumé dials into the brand's calling card. It also courted attention with provocative pieces - the Swiss Mad watch with a case partly made of Vacherin cheese, the Swiss Alp Watch mocking the Apple Watch, and the first Vantablack dials.

Today Moser produces a few thousand watches a year from Neuhausen am Rheinfall across the Endeavour, Pioneer, Streamliner and Heritage collections, and has become one of the best-known 'accessible' independents.

name: Habring²
tagline: Austrian husband-and-wife manufacture making honest complications by hand
summary: Habring² is a small Austrian manufacture founded in 2004 by Richard and Maria Kristina Habring in Carinthia. Known for affordable-by-independent-standards watches with in-house movements, it specialises in split-seconds chronographs, dead-beat (jumping) seconds and foudroyante complications.
history:
Richard Habring trained in Austria and spent years at IWC in Schaffhausen, where he worked on complications including the brand's split-seconds chronograph development. With his wife Maria Kristina he set up an independent workshop, and in 2004 the couple launched Habring² - the squared symbol representing the two of them - in Völkermarkt, Carinthia.

The Habrings built a reputation for mechanically serious watches at comparatively modest prices, often modifying and then replacing base calibres with their own construction. Their range includes the split-seconds chronograph Doppel, the jumping-seconds Erwin, the Foudroyante-Felix with a flying one-eighth-second display, and the time-only Felix, powered by their in-house A11 calibre.

The company remains a small family business with a handful of watchmakers, producing watches largely to order with extensive customisation. It marked its 20th anniversary in 2024 with the Oskar and Josef models, and continues to be one of the most respected value propositions in independent watchmaking. Customers can specify dial colours, numerals, hands and case details, and many watches are assembled only after an order is placed. The small team handles design, movement production, finishing and service under one roof.

name: Hajime Asaoka
tagline: Japan's first independent tourbillon maker, designing and machining every part himself
summary: Hajime Asaoka is a Tokyo-based AHCI independent watchmaker who, in 2009, completed the first tourbillon wristwatch made by an independent in Japan. His small output of tourbillons, chronographs and time-only watches, with movements made in his own workshop, is among the most coveted in Japanese watchmaking.
history:
Hajime Asaoka was born in Kanagawa in 1965 and graduated in design from Tokyo University of the Arts. In 1992 he founded his own design office, working as a product designer and becoming an early expert in 3D computer graphics for advertising and magazines. A commission to design a watch led him to teach himself watchmaking, and he began making watches in 2005.

Working largely alone with CNC machines and hand tools, in 2009 he presented a high-end mechanical wristwatch with a tourbillon, the first made by an independent watchmaker in Japan. His striking designs, combining Art Deco typography with engineering precision, drew global attention, and he became a full member of the Académie Horlogère des Créateurs Indépendants (AHCI).

Asaoka's watches include the Tsunami, a time-only watch with an unusually large 15 mm balance; a classical column-wheel Chronograph; the Tourbillon Pura with an A7075 duralumin carriage; and Project T, a tourbillon developed with aerospace machinist Yuki Precision and tool maker OSG, which uses tiny ball bearings in place of some jewels. He makes all the movement parts in his own workshop, run as Precision Watch Tokyo. In 2019 he launched Kurono Tokyo to offer his designs at accessible prices. In 2024 his company also revived the defunct Nagoya brand Takano with the Chateau Nouvelle, the first Japanese watch certified by the Besançon Observatory.

name: Halios
tagline: Vancouver's cult one-man microbrand of dive and sport watches
summary: Halios is a small Vancouver brand founded by Jason Lim that makes limited batches of dive and sport watches such as the Seaforth, Delfin, Fairwind and Universa. Its watches routinely sell out through pre-orders and are highly regarded for design and finishing at their price.
history:
Jason Lim founded Halios in Vancouver, British Columbia, as a passion project, releasing small batches of dive watches designed by himself and produced with Swiss and Asian suppliers. Early models such as the Holotype and Puck established a reputation for clean, tool-like design and careful detailing.

The brand's popularity grew with the Delfin, a 1960s-style skin diver, the Tropik, and above all the Seaforth, a compact diver offered with fixed or rotating bezels and many dial colours, including sunburst and pastel shades. Releases are made to order in limited runs, and demand has consistently exceeded supply, earning Halios a cult following among collectors.

More recent designs include the Fairwind, a slim sports watch with an integrated feel, and the Universa, a 38 mm sport-dress watch whose latest version uses galvanically treated or vitreous enamel dials. The fourth-generation Seaforth moved to titanium with a Sellita movement, continuing Halios's approach of small, carefully planned production. Lim handles the design work himself and deliberately keeps the brand small, which is part of its appeal to collectors. Halios watches are known for high-quality dials, crisp case finishing and well-judged proportions, and many enthusiasts consider the brand one of the pioneers of the modern microbrand movement.

name: Hamilton
tagline: American spirit, Swiss precision: the field watch and film-star brand
summary: Hamilton was founded in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, and made railroad and military watches before moving to Switzerland and joining the Swatch Group. Its Khaki Field watches, the triangular Ventura and frequent film appearances make it a favourite affordable brand.
history:
The Hamilton Watch Company was founded in 1892 in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, taking over the premises of earlier watch firms and taking its name from Andrew Hamilton, who had once owned the land. It became known for highly accurate pocket watches for the American railroads, where precise timekeeping was a matter of safety, and at its peak supplied a large share of railroad-grade watches.

Hamilton became the official watch supplier to the US armed forces. In the First World War it made wristwatches for American soldiers, and in the Second World War it halted civilian production to make watches and precision marine chronometers for the military. Those rugged, legible designs inspired today's Khaki Field line. In 1918 Hamilton watches were used on the first US airmail flights.

In 1957 Hamilton launched the Ventura, the world's first battery-powered electric wristwatch, in a triangular case designed by Richard Arbib; Elvis Presley wore one in the 1961 film Blue Hawaii. In 1966 Hamilton bought the Swiss firm Büren, which had pioneered the micro-rotor, and in 1969 it helped introduce the Calibre 11 automatic chronograph. In 1970 it unveiled the Pulsar, the first LED digital watch. American production wound down, and in 1974 the brand was sold to the Swiss SSIH group, which in 1983 merged into what became the Swatch Group.

Now headquartered in Biel/Bienne, Hamilton uses Swatch Group movements such as the H-10 with 80-hour power reserve. It has appeared in more than 500 films, including 2001: A Space Odyssey, Men in Black and Interstellar, whose Murph watch became a production model. The Khaki Field Mechanical, Khaki Navy Scuba, Jazzmaster and American Classic PSR are among its best-known models.

name: Hanhart
tagline: Black Forest chronograph specialist famous for its red pusher and Bundeswehr 417
summary: Hanhart was founded in 1882 in Diessenhofen, Switzerland, and has made watches and stopwatches in Germany's Black Forest since 1902. It is renowned for its 1930s pilot chronographs and the 417 issued to the West German military, whose red pusher became the brand's trademark.
history:
Johann A. Hanhart opened a watch shop and workshop in Diessenhofen, Switzerland, in 1882. In 1902 the business moved to Schwenningen in Germany's Black Forest, and it later settled in Gütenbach, where it still manufactures today. Hanhart made its first stopwatch in 1924 and became one of Germany's leading makers of affordable mechanical stopwatches.

In 1938 Hanhart introduced the Calibre 40 single-button chronograph, followed in 1939 by the two-pusher Calibre 41 with flyback function. These robust pilot's chronographs, including the TachyTele, were supplied to German aviators and are now highly collectible. Their red pusher, originally a safety measure to stop pilots accidentally resetting the chronograph, became Hanhart's visual signature.

In 1954 Hanhart created the 417 and the stainless-steel 417 ES for the newly formed West German Bundeswehr. Steve McQueen owned a 417 ES and wore it in the 1962 film The War Lover, helping make the model an icon. Like much of the industry, Hanhart struggled through the quartz era and went through several ownership changes in the 2000s and 2010s.

Today, led by co-CEOs Felix Wallner and Simon Hall, Hanhart produces reissues of the 417 ES and 415 ES, Pioneer and Primus pilot's chronographs and dive watches, assembled in Gütenbach with in-house tool-making and parts manufacture.

name: Harry Winston
tagline: The 'King of Diamonds' whose Opus series reinvented independent watchmaking
summary: Harry Winston is a New York high-jewellery house founded in 1932, famous for historic diamonds such as the Hope Diamond. Its watch division, based in Geneva and owned with the whole house by the Swatch Group since 2013, blends gem-setting with complications, and its Opus series gave a platform to leading independent watchmakers.
history:
Harry Winston, the son of a small New York jeweller, founded Harry Winston Inc. in 1932 and built his reputation by buying historic jewellery collections and famous stones, recutting and resetting them. Over his career he handled many of the world's great diamonds, including the Jonker, the Vargas and the Hope Diamond, which he donated to the Smithsonian Institution in 1958 by sending it through the US mail. He became known as the 'King of Diamonds' and the 'jeweller to the stars', lending jewels to Hollywood actresses for the Academy Awards.

After his death in 1978, his son Ronald Winston led the company and in 1989 launched its first watch collection, the Premier, a ladies' watch that combined fine jewellery with Swiss movements. A dedicated watch company was established in Geneva, and the house expanded into men's watches with the Ocean and Midnight collections.

In 2001 Maximilian Büsser, then head of the watch division, created the Opus series, inviting an independent watchmaker to create an annual limited-edition piece under both names. Opus 1 was made with François-Paul Journe, and later editions involved Vianney Halter, Felix Baumgartner of Urwerk, Andreas Strehler and others. The series helped bring independent watchmaking into the mainstream. The Histoire de Tourbillon series followed with multi-axis tourbillons.

In 2013 the Swatch Group bought Harry Winston's jewellery and watch business from the Canadian mining company then known as Harry Winston Diamond Corporation. Today the house's Geneva workshops produce the Premier, Midnight, Ocean and Emerald lines alongside high-complication and métiers d'art pieces.

name: Hermès
tagline: The Paris saddler whose watches play with time, leather and wit
summary: Hermès, the family-controlled Paris luxury house founded in 1837, makes watches through La Montre Hermès in Biel, established in 1978. It holds stakes in movement, case and dial makers, and its Arceau, Cape Cod, Slim d'Hermès and H08 collections blend equestrian heritage with playful complications.
history:
Thierry Hermès opened a harness workshop in Paris in 1837, making fine saddlery for the carriage trade. His son Charles-Émile moved the business to 24 rue du Faubourg Saint-Honoré in 1880, and as cars replaced horses, grandson Émile-Maurice Hermès diversified into leather goods, luggage and accessories. In 1912 the house made a leather strap with a pocket to hold a watch on the wrist, and it sold watches from partners such as Universal and Jaeger-LeCoultre in its Paris store.

Hermès established its own watch subsidiary, La Montre Hermès, in Biel/Bienne in 1978. That same year designer Henri d'Origny created the Arceau, with its round case and stirrup-shaped asymmetric lugs and slanting numerals that seem to gallop. D'Origny also designed the Cape Cod in 1991, a square within a rectangle inspired by the chaîne d'ancre link, later worn on the long double-tour strap created with Martin Margiela.

In the 2000s the house pursued vertical integration, acquiring a 25% stake in Vaucher Manufacture Fleurier in 2006, and later the case maker Joseph Erard and dial maker Natéber. This enabled the Slim d'Hermès of 2015, with numerals drawn by typographer Philippe Apeloig, and a series of 'poetic' complications such as the Arceau Le Temps Suspendu of 2011, whose hands can be made to stop time at the push of a button.

The cushion-shaped H08 sports watch followed in 2021, and Hermès has won prizes at the Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Genève for its métiers d'art dials. The house remains majority-controlled by descendants of Thierry Hermès.

name: HMT
tagline: 'Timekeepers to the Nation': India's state watchmaker behind the Janata
summary: HMT, the watch division of state-owned Hindustan Machine Tools, made India's first mass-produced wristwatches from 1961 and dominated the market for decades. Its hand-wound Janata and Pilot are nostalgic icons, and HMT Limited still sells watches online.
history:
HMT, Hindustan Machine Tools, set up a watch factory in Bangalore in 1961 in collaboration with Japan's Citizen Watch. Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru released the first wristwatches made there, and HMT quickly became the watch of a newly independent India, sold with the slogan 'Timekeepers to the Nation'.

Its hand-wound mechanical watches, above all the Janata ('people's') and the Pilot, were affordable, durable and ubiquitous; other lines included the Jhalak semi-skeleton, Sona, Sujata, Rajat and a Braille watch. Production expanded to new factories at Tumkur (1978) and Ranibagh (1985), HMT began making quartz analogue watches in 1981, and it also built floral, tower and solar clocks, including the famous floral clock at Lalbagh in Bangalore.

From the late 1980s, competition from Titan and liberalisation eroded HMT's position, and slow decision-making kept it from modernising. HMT Watches Ltd. was closed in 2016, triggering a rush for the remaining stock among collectors. The brand did not disappear: HMT Limited's auxiliary business division in Jalahalli, Bengaluru, continues to sell HMT-branded mechanical, automatic, quartz, skeleton and Braille watches, including Janata, Pilot and Jawan automatics, through its official online shop.

name: Huawei
tagline: Chinese tech giant making long-battery, elegantly styled smartwatches
summary: Huawei, the Shenzhen-based technology group founded in 1987, is one of the world's largest wearables makers. Its Watch GT line is known for classic round designs and battery life measured in weeks, and it also makes premium titanium and blood-pressure-measuring watches.
history:
Ren Zhengfei founded Huawei in Shenzhen in 1987 as a telecom-equipment reseller, and it grew into one of the world's largest makers of networking gear and smartphones. The company describes itself as employee-owned through a union shareholding scheme.

Huawei's first smartwatch, the round Huawei Watch, arrived in 2015 running Android Wear, and the Watch GT of 2018 switched to Huawei's own lightweight software to achieve battery life of up to two weeks, which became its hallmark. After US sanctions in 2019 cut off access to Google services, Huawei moved its watches to its own HarmonyOS and continued to grow, especially in China, Europe and the Middle East.

Huawei's range now spans the Watch GT series with traditional-looking cases, the premium Watch Ultimate in Liquidmetal and titanium, the Watch Fit fitness line, and the Watch D series, which uses a tiny built-in air pump to take cuff-style blood-pressure readings. Current models include the Watch GT 7 Pro, the Watch 6 Pro and the Watch D3. Huawei watches are not generally sold in the United States. In China, Huawei is among the leading sellers of wearables, and its watches are also popular in Europe and the Middle East.

name: Hublot
tagline: The 'Art of Fusion': gold meets rubber, ceramic meets sapphire
summary: Hublot, founded in 1980 by Carlo Crocco, shocked the industry by pairing a gold watch with a natural rubber strap. Reinvented by Jean-Claude Biver with the 2005 Big Bang and owned by LVMH since 2008, it is known for bold materials, sports sponsorships and the in-house Unico chronograph.
history:
Hublot was founded in 1980 by Carlo Crocco, an Italian from the Binda watch dynasty, under the company name MDM Genève. His first watch, with a porthole-shaped case (hublot means porthole in French) and a gold case on a natural rubber strap, was so unconventional that it was rejected by the Basel fair, yet it quickly found clients among European royalty. Developing a rubber strap that did not crack or smell took years of research.

By the early 2000s the brand had stagnated. In 2004 Jean-Claude Biver, who had revived Blancpain and led Omega's marketing, became CEO and shareholder. In 2005 he launched the Big Bang, a 44 mm chronograph combining steel, ceramic, rubber and Kevlar under the 'Art of Fusion' slogan. It won a design prize in Geneva and transformed Hublot's fortunes, with sales rising several-fold within a few years.

LVMH acquired Hublot in 2008. The brand built a manufacture in Nyon, launched the in-house Unico flyback chronograph in 2010 and developed proprietary materials such as Magic Gold, a scratch-resistant ceramic-gold alloy, and coloured sapphire cases. Sponsorships of football, including FIFA World Cup timekeeping, and ambassadors such as Usain Bolt and Pelé made it one of the most visible luxury brands. Ricardo Guadalupe succeeded Biver as CEO in 2012.

Today Hublot's collections include the Big Bang, Classic Fusion, Spirit of Big Bang, Square Bang and the high-end MP series, while the 2025 twentieth anniversary of the Big Bang celebrated its defining model.

name: Invicta
tagline: Swiss-born in 1837, reborn in Florida as the king of big, bold, budget watches
summary: Invicta was founded in La Chaux-de-Fonds in 1837 by Raphael Picard and is now run from Hollywood, Florida, by the Lalo family. It is known for huge catalogues of inexpensive, oversized watches sold largely through TV shopping and online, and above all for the Pro Diver.
history:
Raphael Picard founded Invicta in La Chaux-de-Fonds in 1837 with the aim of making good Swiss watches at prices a broad public could afford; the name is Latin for 'invincible'. The company won a gold medal at the 1914 Swiss National Exhibition in Bern and supplied watches to Allied forces during the Second World War.

Like much of the Swiss industry, Invicta nearly disappeared in the quartz crisis, and its parent company went bankrupt in 1982. In 1991 Eyal Lalo, whose family had been involved in distributing Invicta, acquired the brand and rebuilt it in the United States. Under the Lalo family, Invicta Watch Group moved its headquarters to Hollywood, Florida, and became famous for its sheer output, reportedly designing around 1,500 new models a year, mostly with Japanese movements, and selling them heavily through TV shopping channels and online at deep discounts from high list prices.

The Pro Diver, particularly the automatic 8926OB with a Seiko NH35 movement, became one of the best-selling watches on Amazon and a popular entry point for new collectors. Invicta bought the Swiss brand Glycine in 2016 and filed for Chapter 11 in June 2023 to restructure its retail operations, while continuing to sell watches worldwide.

name: IWC Schaffhausen
tagline: Engineering-led pilot's watches and Portugiesers from Switzerland's only Rhine-side maker
summary: IWC is a Richemont-owned manufacture in Schaffhausen, founded by an American, and best known for its Pilot's Watches, the Portugieser and the Ingenieur. It is prized for technical watchmaking, from the Pellaton winding system to perpetual calendars.
history:
The International Watch Company was founded in 1868 by Florentine Ariosto Jones, a watchmaker from Boston who planned to combine cheap Swiss labour with American industrial methods. Unusually, he chose German-speaking Schaffhausen in north-eastern Switzerland, where industrialist Heinrich Moser's Rhine hydropower plant could drive machinery. Jones's venture struggled, and in 1880 the Rauschenbach family took control; the family and their descendants, including Ernst Jakob Homberger, ran IWC for nearly a century.

IWC built a reputation for robust, precise movements. The Pallweber pocket watches of 1884 showed the time with jumping digital numerals. In 1936 it launched its first Special Pilot's Watch, followed in 1939 by the large-cased Portugieser ordered by two Portuguese merchants, and in 1940 by the 55mm Big Pilot's Watch for the German air force. The Mark 11 of 1948 served the Royal Air Force for decades. Technical director Albert Pellaton developed his efficient pawl winding system in 1950, used in the antimagnetic Ingenieur of 1955.

The quartz crisis led to IWC's sale to the German VDO Adolf Schindling group in 1978. Under Günter Blümlein, IWC made titanium watches for Porsche Design and in 1985 launched Kurt Klaus's Da Vinci perpetual calendar, which could be set entirely by the crown. IWC joined Jaeger-LeCoultre and A. Lange & Söhne in LMH, which was acquired by Richemont in 2000.

Under Richemont IWC expanded its in-house calibres, including the 7-day 5000 series and later the 52000 and 82000 families built around Pellaton winding. The Pilot's Watches, Portugieser and a Gérald Genta-inspired Ingenieur revived in 2023 anchor a catalogue that ranges from steel tool watches to grand complications such as the Portugieser Sidérale Scafusia.

name: Jacob & Co.
tagline: Jacob Arabo's diamond-drenched, kinetic-sculpture watches from New York and Geneva
summary: Jacob & Co. was founded in New York in 1986 by jeweller Jacob Arabo and became famous with hip-hop stars before moving into high watchmaking in Geneva. It is known for spectacular pieces such as the rotating Astronomia, the Bugatti Chiron Tourbillon and extravagant diamond watches.
history:
Jacob Arabo, born in Uzbekistan and raised in Queens after his family emigrated to the United States, trained as a jeweller and opened his own business in New York's Diamond District in 1986. His bold, colourful designs and personal relationships with musicians made 'Jacob the Jeweler' a household name in hip-hop culture during the 1990s, and his work was name-checked in numerous songs.

In 2002 he launched the Five Time Zone watch, a colourful quartz watch with four subdials that became a celebrity hit and moved the brand into watches. Arabo then pushed into high horology, setting up Jacob & Co. operations in Geneva and collaborating with specialist movement makers. The Astronomia, launched in 2014, features a vertical, multi-axis tourbillon, a rotating globe and a spherically cut diamond all orbiting the dial, and became the brand's signature.

The brand also created the Billionaire watch, set with hundreds of carats of emerald-cut diamonds, and a series of musical watches such as the Opera Godfather, which plays the film's theme. Partnerships with Bugatti produced the Bugatti Chiron Tourbillon, whose miniature W16 engine animates at the push of a button, and Cristiano Ronaldo became a partner with his own collections.

Jacob & Co. remains privately owned by Jacob Arabo and his family, with its jewellery business headquartered in New York and its high-watchmaking arm based in Geneva, positioning itself at the extreme, theatrical end of luxury watchmaking.

name: Jaeger-LeCoultre
tagline: The 'watchmaker's watchmaker' of the Vallée de Joux, home of the Reverso
summary: Jaeger-LeCoultre is a highly vertically integrated manufacture in Le Sentier that has created more than 1,200 calibres and historically supplied movements to Patek Philippe, Audemars Piguet and Vacheron Constantin. Owned by Richemont, it is famous for the swivelling Reverso, the Atmos clock and technically ambitious complications.
history:
In 1833 the self-taught watchmaker Antoine LeCoultre opened a small workshop in Le Sentier in the Vallée de Joux to make precision gear-wheel components. In 1844 he invented the Millionomètre, the first instrument able to measure to a micron, and in 1847 a keyless winding and time-setting system that did away with the key. By 1866 LeCoultre & Cie had become the valley's first manufacture to bring all watchmaking crafts under one roof, earning its reputation as the 'Grande Maison'.

Around 1903 the Paris-based naval chronometer maker Edmond Jaeger challenged Swiss manufacturers to produce his ultra-thin movements, and Jacques-David LeCoultre took up the challenge. The collaboration produced the record-thin calibre 145 pocket watch in 1907 and, in 1929, the Calibre 101, still the world's smallest mechanical movement. The Atmos clock, which draws its energy from small changes in temperature, followed in 1928, and in 1931 the Reverso, a rectangular watch whose case flips over to protect the crystal from polo mallets. The two families formally merged under the Jaeger-LeCoultre name in 1937.

Mid-century hits included the Memovox alarm watch and the anti-magnetic Geophysic chronometer of 1958. After difficult quartz-era years, the company came under VDO (1978) and Mannesmann before being acquired by Richemont in 2000. The Master Control line of 1992 introduced the '1000 Hours Control' test, and the Gyrotourbillon (2004), Duomètre dual-wing movements (2007) and the Hybris Mechanica grand complications reasserted its technical ambitions.

Today Jaeger-LeCoultre remains the largest employer in the Vallée de Joux, producing most components in-house across roughly 180 crafts, while the Reverso, Master and Polaris lines anchor its collection.

name: Junghans
tagline: Black Forest maker of the Max Bill icon and the first radio-controlled wristwatch
summary: Junghans, founded in Schramberg in 1861, was once the world's largest clock manufacturer. Today it is best known for the Bauhaus-inspired max bill watches and a pioneering role in radio-controlled and solar timekeeping.
history:
Erhard Junghans and his brother-in-law Jakob Zeller-Tobler founded the company in Schramberg in the Black Forest in 1861, initially making clock components before producing complete clocks. Adopting American-style industrial production methods, Junghans grew rapidly and by around 1903 was the largest clock factory in the world, employing some 3,000 people.

Wristwatch production began in earnest in the 1930s, and after the Second World War Junghans became one of Germany's biggest producers of chronometers. In 1956 the Diehl group took control of the company. Swiss architect and Bauhaus alumnus Max Bill designed a kitchen clock for Junghans in 1956 and a range of wristwatches in the early 1960s, whose minimalist dials remain the brand's best-known design.

Junghans was official timekeeper of the 1972 Munich Olympics and led the development of radio-controlled timekeeping: it launched radio-controlled table clocks in 1985 and, in 1990, the MEGA 1, the world's first radio-controlled wristwatch, followed by a solar-powered radio-controlled watch in 1993.

The company was sold to EganaGoldpfeil in 2000, but the new owner's collapse pushed Junghans into insolvency in 2008. In 2009 the Schramberg entrepreneur Hans-Jochem Steim and his son Hannes Steim acquired it, refocusing Junghans on design-led mechanical and quartz watches such as max bill, Meister and Form.

name: Kari Voutilainen
tagline: Finnish master of guilloché and hand-finishing in the Val-de-Travers
summary: Kari Voutilainen is a Finnish watchmaker working in Môtiers, Switzerland, whose tiny output of hand-finished watches features his own direct-impulse movements and hand-guilloché dials made in-house at Comblémine. He is considered one of the finest living artisan-watchmakers.
history:
Born in Finland in 1962, Kari Voutilainen trained at the Finnish watchmaking school and later at WOSTEP in Switzerland, where he also taught. He worked in the restoration department of Parmigiani Fleurier, specialising in complicated antique pieces, before going independent in 2002 in Môtiers, in the Val-de-Travers.

His first wristwatch series, the Observatoire, was built on vintage chronometer movements with exquisite guilloché dials. In 2011 he introduced the Vingt-8 calibre, featuring a double escape-wheel direct-impulse escapement developed for efficiency and accuracy; it underpinned most of his models, including GMT, moonphase and power-reserve variants, until its retirement at the end of 2025. Later calibres include the KV20 and the tonneau-shaped KV21 with its dual-wheel direct impulse escapement.

To control his supply chain he acquired the dial maker Comblémine in 2014 and co-founded the case maker Voutilainen & Cattin. In 2021 he led an investor group that acquired Urban Jürgensen, serving as co-CEO until stepping back into an advisory role. His workshop makes fewer than 60 watches a year, collaborates with artisans such as Japanese urushi lacquer masters, and has won several GPHG prizes, including in 2025.

name: King Seiko
tagline: Seiko's 1960s high-grade rival to Grand Seiko, revived for a new era
summary: King Seiko was the high-grade line of Seiko's Daini Seikosha factory, built to compete with Suwa's Grand Seiko in the 1960s. Revived in 2022, it now offers faceted, sharply finished mechanical watches between Seiko Presage and Grand Seiko.
history:
King Seiko was introduced in 1961 by Daini Seikosha, the Tokyo-area Seiko factory that competed internally with Suwa Seikosha, maker of Grand Seiko. The rivalry pushed both teams to improve accuracy and finishing, and King Seiko quickly earned a reputation for crisp, faceted cases and reliable movements.

The 1965 KSK introduced a hacking seconds function, protected crown and the distinctive shield logo, and its sharp lugs and flat surfaces became a design hallmark. Later models, including the 45KCM of 1969 and the 5626 and 56KS automatics, featured high-beat and chronometer-grade movements. The line was wound down in the mid-1970s as quartz transformed Seiko's business.

In 2021 Seiko released a limited recreation of the KSK, and in 2022 King Seiko returned as a full collection. The range has since grown to include the KSK series, the KS1969 series based on the curved 45KCM, and in 2024 the angular VANAC series inspired by a 1972 design, using the upgraded 6L35 and 8L45 movements.

Today King Seiko sits between Seiko Presage and Grand Seiko, with most models priced around $3,100 to $3,850. Its cases emphasise flat, sharply faceted surfaces and wide polished bevels, echoing the internal rivalry that once pushed Daini Seikosha and Suwa Seikosha to outdo each other.

name: Knot
tagline: Made-in-Japan watches you build yourself from thousands of case and strap combinations
summary: Maker's Watch Knot is a Tokyo brand, founded in 2014, that sells affordable made-in-Japan watches designed to be mixed and matched with a huge range of straps. Its gallery shops let customers choose from over 100,000 combinations, and its Takumi line features traditional Japanese crafts on the dial.
history:
Knot was founded in 2014 in Kichijoji, Tokyo, with the aim of offering well-made Japanese watches at accessible prices while letting customers personalise them. Rather than selling finished watches, it separates cases and straps: buyers pick a watch head and then choose from around 200 straps made with its network of partner artisans, allowing more than 100,000 combinations.

The brand grew quickly through direct-to-consumer sales and its own gallery shops, now numbering a dozen across Japan. Its range spans quartz and solar watches, Miyota and Epson-powered automatics with sapphire crystals and Zaratsu-polished cases, and a premium Takumi collection featuring crafts such as Kanazawa gold leaf, urushi lacquer and raden mother-of-pearl inlay.

Knot also produces custom and corporate watches, with collaborations including Uniqlo, Studio Ghibli, Kyocera and the Yokohama DeNA BayStars.

The company, Knot Co., Ltd., is led by founder Hiromitsu Endo and began in a small apartment room in Kichijoji. Its Takumi collection works with named artisans: raden and urushi dials by lacquer craftsman Nobuichi Ohtake, and Kanazawa gold-leaf dials made with Hakuichi, a gold-leaf company founded in 1975 in a craft tradition more than 400 years old. Strap partners include makers of Tochigi leather.

name: Konstantin Chaykin
tagline: Russia's inventor-watchmaker, from the Joker Wristmon to the world's thinnest watch
summary: Konstantin Chaykin is a Moscow-based watchmaker and inventor who founded his workshop in 2003 and became the first Russian member of the AHCI. He is known for playful 'Wristmon' faces like the Joker, astronomical complications, and the record-breaking 1.65mm ThinKing.
history:
Born in St Petersburg in 1975, Konstantin Chaykin came to watchmaking via antiques and restoration and set up his independent workshop in 2003. He completed his first clock in 2004 and specialised early in astronomical and calendar mechanisms, including clocks that compute the date of Orthodox Easter; his first patent, for an Easter date indicator, was granted in 2007.

In 2010 he became the first and only Russian member of the Académie Horlogère des Créateurs Indépendants, later serving as its president from 2016 to 2019. He moved production to Moscow in 2012. His watches include the Lunokhod with a spherical moonphase (2011), the Cinema with a mechanical cinematograph animation (2013), the single-hand Genius Temporis (2014) and the Mars Conqueror series telling Martian time.

In 2017 he created the Joker, the first of his 'Wristmons' - watches whose dials form faces, with hours and minutes as eyes and a moonphase as a grinning mouth - which became his best-known design. In 2020 he received the WIPO Medal for Inventors, and he holds over 100 patents. In 2024 he unveiled the ThinKing, a mechanical watch just 1.65mm thick, claiming the title of the world's thinnest.

name: Kudoke
tagline: Stefan Kudoke's hand-engraved independent watches from rural Saxony
summary: Kudoke is the independent atelier of master watchmaker Stefan Kudoke, known for hand-skeletonised and engraved art pieces and the HANDwerk line built on his in-house Kaliber 1. His KUDOKE 2 and KUDOKE 3 both won the GPHG Petite Aiguille prize.
history:
Stefan Kudoke trained under two experienced master watchmakers and finished his apprenticeship as Brandenburg's state champion, placing third in the national craft-youth competition. He then joined Glashütte Original, working in its atelier for complications and prototypes, and later serviced Breguet, Blancpain and Omega watches in New York. He earned his master watchmaker's certificate at just 22.

Combining this training with studies in economics and finance, Kudoke set out on his own to design and make watches under his name. His early KUNSTwerk pieces, based on hand-skeletonised and hand-engraved movements, established his reputation, with creations such as the octopus-themed KudOktopus and the literal 'Real Skeleton' with an engraved skull.

The HANDwerk collection began with Kaliber 1, his first in-house manual-wind movement, featuring a raised, hand-engraved balance cock with his infinity motif. The KUDOKE 2 added a hand-engraved rotating day/night sky disc for 24-hour indication and won the GPHG Petite Aiguille prize in 2019; the unconventional three-armed hour display of the KUDOKE 3 won the same prize in 2024 in salmon.

Kudoke works from a small workshop in Weifa in Saxony with a tiny team, making watches largely to individual customer specifications.

name: Kurono Tokyo
tagline: Hajime Asaoka's accessible Art Deco watches that sell out in minutes
summary: Kurono Tokyo is the accessible brand of AHCI independent watchmaker Hajime Asaoka. It pairs his meticulous dial and case designs with reliable Japanese movements, released in small batches that routinely sell out almost instantly.
history:
Kurono Tokyo was launched in 2019 by Hajime Asaoka, the Tokyo designer-turned-watchmaker whose hand-built tourbillons had earned him AHCI membership but cost far more than most collectors could pay. The idea was to share the design DNA of his atelier watches, including hand-drawn typefaces, multi-layer dials, hand-mixed colours and carefully proportioned cases, at a fraction of the price by using off-the-shelf Japanese movements.

Early models were small-batch, mostly online releases that sold out quickly, building a devoted international following. The range has grown into several series: the Bunkyo Tokyo Classic series of Art Deco three-handers, the Grand series with urushi lacquer dials made by a master craftsman, a Complications series including the Chronograph I and II with Seiko column-wheel calibres and the Calendrier full calendar, and Special Projects such as 34 mm Art Deco and meteorite-dial editions.

Kurono now operates salons in Aoyama, Tokyo and in Shanghai, and in 2026 released its first diver's watch.

Typical releases illustrate the formula: the 34 mm Art Deco models of 2022 used a Miyota 90S5 and were limited to 80 pieces per colour, the Calendrier Type I combined a Miyota 9122 with a domed khaki dial and full calendar, and the Chronograph II used Seiko's NE86 column-wheel movement with a multi-layered lacquered dial.

name: Laco
tagline: Pforzheim pilot-watch specialist and one of the original B-Uhr makers
summary: Laco was founded in Pforzheim in 1925 and was one of the five firms that built Luftwaffe B-Uhr observation watches in the 1940s. Today it offers affordable to mid-priced Flieger watches, from Miyota-powered basics to faithful 'Original' reconstructions.
history:
Frieda Lacher and Ludwig Hummel founded Lacher & Co. in Pforzheim in 1925, producing watch cases and complete watches. Hummel went on to found the movement maker Durowe (Deutsche Uhren-Rohwerke) in 1933, while Erich Lacher, Frieda's son, ran the Erich Lacher Uhrenfabrik. The companies grew to about 1,400 employees by the mid-1950s.

During the Second World War, Laco was one of five manufacturers of the Beobachtungsuhr (B-Uhr), the oversized observation watch used by Luftwaffe navigators, alongside A. Lange & Söhne, Stowa, Wempe and IWC. These 55 mm watches established the Type A and Type B dial layouts that define pilot's watches to this day.

In 1959 Laco-Durowe was sold to the US company Timex, and in 1965 it passed to the Swiss Ebauches SA. The Erich Lacher Uhrenfabrik continued as a smaller company, and in 1988 Horst Günther acquired the Laco name and logo, allowing modern Laco watches to be produced again.

The company filed for insolvency in 2009 but restarted in 2010 under new management with a small team. Laco has since focused on pilot's watches, from entry-level automatic Flieger models to aged 'Erbstück' pieces and DIN 8330-certified watches, alongside navy and squad lines, all assembled in Pforzheim.

name: Laurent Ferrier
tagline: Pebble-smooth cases and classical chronometry from a Patek Philippe veteran
summary: Laurent Ferrier is a Geneva brand founded by a former Patek Philippe watchmaker after 37 years at the firm. Its soft 'Galet' pebble cases, restrained dials and superbly finished micro-rotor and tourbillon calibres have won multiple GPHG prizes.
history:
Laurent Ferrier spent 37 years at Patek Philippe, rising to technical director, while racing cars in his spare time - he finished third overall at the 1979 24 Hours of Le Mans with his friend François Servanin. Servanin later became the financial backer of Ferrier's own brand, which was set up in Geneva with his son Christian Ferrier and launched its first watches in 2010.

The debut Galet Classic Tourbillon Double Spiral, with a discreet tourbillon hidden on the back and a twin-hairspring balance, won the Best Men's Watch prize at the 2010 Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Genève. It was followed by the Galet Micro-Rotor with a natural escapement in silicon, the cushion-shaped Galet Square, travel-time and annual calendar models, and the integrated-bracelet Grand Sport Tourbillon Pursuit and Sport Auto.

Servanin, the controlling shareholder, took a hands-on role in the late 2010s. In January 2025 long-serving board member Florent Perrichon was appointed CEO. The manufacture in Plan-les-Ouates produces a few hundred watches a year, and the Classic Moon won the brand's fifth GPHG award in 2024. The brand remains small and family-rooted, prized for restrained design and finishing of the highest order.

name: Lip
tagline: France's oldest watch brand, known for presidents' watches and the Mach 2000
summary: Lip was founded in Besançon in 1867 by Emmanuel Lipmann and became France's most famous watchmaker, supplying watches to heads of state and pioneering electric timekeeping. Today it offers affordable heritage designs such as the Himalaya, Général de Gaulle and Roger Tallon's Mach 2000.
history:
Emmanuel Lipmann founded a small watchmaking workshop in Besançon in 1867, and the family business, later branded Lip, grew into the largest watch manufacturer in France. Its T18 calibre watches of the 1930s and 1940s became symbols of French precision; after the Liberation, Lip watches were presented to Winston Churchill and General de Gaulle, earning the Général de Gaulle model the nickname 'the watch of presidents'. Mountaineer Maurice Herzog's Annapurna expedition of 1950 is linked to the Himalaya model.

Under Fred Lip, the founder's grandson, the company pursued technical innovation, including early electric wristwatches developed in the 1950s. In the 1970s it commissioned avant-garde designs from industrial designer Roger Tallon, whose asymmetric Mach 2000 of 1975 is now considered a design classic.

Financial troubles led to the famous 'Lip affair' of 1973, when workers at the Palente factory in Besançon occupied the plant and continued to produce and sell watches themselves, becoming a landmark of French labour history. The company was eventually liquidated, and the brand passed through several owners in the following decades.

In the mid-2010s the Lip brand returned to Besançon under new owners, who revived its heritage models and developed the R26, described as the first automatic movement made in Besançon since the Fred Lip era, with most components sourced in France.

name: Longines
tagline: Elegance since 1832, under the oldest registered watch logo
summary: Longines is the Swatch Group's classic mid-luxury brand from Saint-Imier, with a long history in aviation, sports timing and elegant dress watches. Its winged hourglass is one of the oldest registered trademarks still in use.
history:
Longines traces its origins to 1832, when Auguste Agassiz joined a watch trading business in Saint-Imier in the Jura. His nephew Ernest Francillon took over and in 1867 brought production under one roof in a factory on a meadow known as 'Les Longines' ('the long fields'). The first movement made there won an award at the Paris Universal Exhibition the same year. The winged hourglass logo was registered in 1889 and is recognised as the oldest unchanged registered trademark for a watch brand.

Longines built its name on precision and sports timing, timing equestrian events and early Olympic Games, and in the 1920s and 30s it became the aviator's brand. It made the Weems Second-Setting Watch for navigator Philip Van Horn Weems and in 1931 the Hour Angle Watch designed with Charles Lindbergh. Amelia Earhart and other pioneer aviators also used Longines. Albert Einstein owned a Longines pocket watch.

The quartz crisis weakened the independent firm, which was sold to General Watch Co. (ASUAG) in 1971. In 1983 ASUAG merged with SSIH to create what became the Swatch Group, and Longines was positioned as its elegant, accessible luxury brand.

Since the 1990s Longines has become one of the Swatch Group's largest brands by volume, with strong sales in China. Its catalogue blends classic lines such as the Master Collection and La Grande Classique with heritage reissues like the Legend Diver and sporty lines such as the Conquest, HydroConquest and the Spirit pilot's watches introduced in 2020. Movements are exclusive ETA-based calibres with silicon balance springs. Longines remains in Saint-Imier, where its museum holds the company's archives.

name: Lorier
tagline: Husband-and-wife microbrand making vintage-style watches at under $1,000
summary: Lorier is a New York-based microbrand founded by Lauren and Mike Tsai that makes 36–39 mm vintage-inspired dive, field, dress and GMT watches with Miyota movements. Its compact cases, domed crystals and fair pricing have made it an enthusiast favourite.
history:
Lorier was started by husband-and-wife team Lauren and Mike Tsai in New York, with the goal of making the kind of mid-century-inspired watches they loved at an accessible price. The brand launched with the Neptune dive watch and quickly became known for modest case sizes, vintage-style domed crystals and gilt details, a contrast to the oversized watches common among microbrands at the time.

The range grew to include the Falcon field watch, with a 3-6-9 dial and broad-arrow hands, the Astra dress-sport watch and the Hyperion GMT, powered by a Miyota 9075 with an independently adjustable local hour hand. Lorier sells directly online, in batches, keeping prices below $1,000.

Recent updates to the core collection added sapphire crystals and, on divers and GMTs, sapphire bezel inserts, improving durability while keeping the vintage look. The company trades as Studio Lorier with the slogan 'Legacy in Action'. Lorier's designs draw on dive, field and travel watches from the 1950s to the 1970s, reinterpreted with modern parts. Its watches are typically released in limited batches that sell directly to customers, and the brand has become a common recommendation for buyers seeking vintage character without vintage fragility.

name: Louis Erard
tagline: Regulator dials and cult collaborations from Le Noirmont
summary: Louis Erard is a Swiss watchmaker founded in 1929 and based in Le Noirmont in the Jura, known for regulator-dial watches. Under CEO Manuel Emch it has become a darling of collectors through limited collaborations with Alain Silberstein, Vianney Halter, Konstantin Chaykin and others at accessible prices.
history:
Louis Erard was founded in 1929 in La Chaux-de-Fonds by Louis Erard and André Perret, producing watches in the Jura watchmaking tradition. The company later settled in Le Noirmont in the Franches-Montagnes, where it remains. For decades it was a modest, family-run producer of classic mechanical watches.

The company changed hands in 1992 for family reasons, and in 2003 it was acquired by a group of investors led by Alain Spinedi, who repositioned Louis Erard as a mid-range Swiss brand offering traditional mechanical watches, notably its Excellence and Heritage lines, at competitive prices. The regulator layout, in which the hours, minutes and seconds are shown on separate axes, became a signature of the house.

In 2019 Manuel Emch, formerly of Jaquet Droz and Romain Jerome, took the helm and reinvented the brand around limited-edition collaborations. The Le Régulateur Louis Erard x Alain Silberstein of 2020, with its playful coloured hands and geometric shapes, sold out rapidly, and was followed by partnerships with independent watchmakers Vianney Halter and Konstantin Chaykin, artist Monica Bonvicini and pop-culture names such as Astro Boy, as well as Métiers d'art editions featuring grand feu enamel, marquetry and hand engraving. Grouped into the Noirmont X, Noirmont Métiers d'art, 2340 and Hall of Fame lines, Louis Erard now offers creative independent-style watches at a small fraction of typical independent prices.

name: Louis Moinet
tagline: Honouring the inventor of the chronograph with meteorites and tourbillons
summary: Ateliers Louis Moinet is a Saint-Blaise brand created in 2004 by Jean-Marie Schaller to honour Louis Moinet, the French horologist whose 1816 'compteur de tierces' is recognised as the first chronograph. It is known for limited, highly decorative pieces using meteorites and rare stones, and for the Memoris chronograph.
history:
Louis Moinet (1768-1853), born in Bourges, was a painter, sculptor and professor of fine arts at the Louvre as well as a gifted horologist and collaborator of Abraham-Louis Breguet. In 1815-1816 he built the 'compteur de tierces', an instrument measuring sixtieths of a second at 216,000 vibrations per hour for astronomical observation - now recognised as the first chronograph. He made clocks for Napoleon, Thomas Jefferson and James Monroe, and in 1848 published a celebrated two-volume Traité d'Horlogerie.

In 2004 Jean-Marie Schaller, a watch industry executive, founded Ateliers Louis Moinet in Saint-Blaise near Neuchâtel to revive the name. The brand became known for tiny limited series with exotic materials - meteorite, lunar and Martian rock, dinosaur bone, rare minerals - and for complex tourbillons. When the original compteur de tierces resurfaced, it was authenticated and presented by the brand, earning Guinness World Records recognition as the first chronograph.

For the bicentenary, the brand launched the Memoris (2015), billed as the first watch built around a chronograph displayed on the dial side. Later creations include the Space Revolution with twin satellite tourbillons and meteorite fragments, and space- and astronomy-themed 'Cosmic Art' pieces. Louis Moinet produces small quantities of limited editions and bespoke pieces from Saint-Blaise.
knownFor: Heritage of the first chronograph & meteorite dials

name: Louis Vuitton
tagline: The trunk maker's Geneva watchmaking, reborn with the 2023 Tambour
summary: Louis Vuitton, the Paris trunk maker founded in 1854 and the flagship of LVMH, has made watches since the 2002 Tambour. With its own La Fabrique du Temps manufacture in Geneva, it moved decisively upmarket with the redesigned integrated-bracelet Tambour of 2023 and collaborations with leading independent watchmakers.
history:
Louis Vuitton, a carpenter's son from the Jura, walked to Paris as a teenager and trained as a box-maker and packer. In 1854 he opened his own workshop, and his flat-topped, stackable trunks, the Damier canvas of 1888 and the Monogram canvas of 1896 created by his son Georges made the house synonymous with luxury travel. In 1987 it merged with Moët Hennessy to form LVMH, of which it is the largest brand.

Louis Vuitton entered watchmaking in 2002 with the Tambour, whose drum-shaped case with the brand's name engraved around the side became its signature. In 2011 the company acquired La Fabrique du Temps, a Geneva complications workshop, and later built a manufacture in Meyrin, adding case- and dial-making capability. Its high-end pieces included the Escale Worldtime of 2014 and the Tambour Moon series, and in 2017 the Tambour Horizon became its connected smartwatch.

In 2021 Jean Arnault, son of LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault, took charge of the watch division and repositioned it firmly in serious watchmaking. The completely redesigned Tambour of 2023, with a slim integrated steel bracelet and the in-house LFT023 micro-rotor calibre, was well received by collectors. Louis Vuitton also launched the Louis Vuitton Watch Prize for Independent Creatives and partnered with independents, notably with Rexhep Rexhepi of Akrivia on the LVRR-01 chiming chronograph in 2024. It also relaunched the Escale and introduced the Tambour Taiko.

The maison's watches are made in Geneva, while its headquarters remain in Paris.

name: Luminox
tagline: Always-visible tritium tool watches made for the Navy SEALs
summary: Luminox was founded in California in 1989 by Barry Cohen and became famous for its always-glowing tritium tube illumination and its Navy SEAL watches. Wholly owned by Switzerland's Mondaine Group since 2016, it sells rugged, affordable sea, land and air tool watches in over 30 countries.
history:
Luminox was founded in 1989 by Barry Cohen in the United States with a simple proposition: a watch that could be read in total darkness without first being charged by light. Instead of conventional luminous paint, Luminox used small sealed glass tubes containing tritium gas, whose beta decay makes a phosphor coating glow continuously for many years. The brand called this 'Luminox Light Technology'.

In the early 1990s Luminox developed a watch for the US Navy SEALs, and the Navy SEAL series, particularly the carbon-reinforced 3000 and 3500 families, became the brand's signature. It went on to make branded pieces for units including the US Coast Guard and US Air Force, and partnered with Lockheed Martin on pilot's watches inspired by aircraft such as the F-117 Nighthawk, SR-71 Blackbird, F-16 and F-22. Later partnerships included Bear Grylls survival watches.

Swiss watch maker Mondaine, with which Luminox had long worked on production, acquired a 50% stake in 2006 and became the sole owner in 2016, moving the brand's base to Switzerland and making its watches Swiss made. Today Luminox organises its range into sea, air, land and space collections, including the Navy SEAL, Pacific Diver, Leatherback Sea Turtle, Atacama Field and P-38 Lightning lines, with most pieces powered by Swiss quartz and some by automatic movements, and it supports the Navy SEAL Foundation.

name: Marathon
tagline: Canadian family firm supplying Swiss-made issue watches to the US military
summary: Marathon is a fourth-generation family company, designed in Canada and manufactured in La Chaux-de-Fonds, that has supplied military watches since the Second World War. Its tritium-lit Search and Rescue divers and Navigators are official issue for the US armed forces and other governments.
history:
Marathon's roots go back to 1904, when the Wein family founded Weinstrum Watch in La Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland. In 1939 Morris Wein established the Marathon Watch Company, and from 1941 it supplied watches to the Allied forces during the Second World War. The family settled in Canada, where the company is based, while its watches continue to be made in Switzerland.

Marathon became a key supplier of military timepieces. It builds watches to the US military standard MIL-PRF-46374G and to Canadian government specifications for search-and-rescue work, and has been a leading supplier of issue watches to the US armed forces. Its designs, such as the plastic-cased Navigator pilot's watch and the steel Search and Rescue (SAR) divers, are illuminated with tritium gas tubes so they glow continuously without charging.

While its watches are issued to soldiers, sailors and aircrew, Marathon also sells them to civilians, and military-watch enthusiasts value them for their authenticity and toughness. The line-up includes the 41 mm GSAR automatic diver, the 46 mm JSAR and JDD, the CSAR automatic chronograph, the Navigator and General Purpose field watches. The business remains owned and run by the Wein family, now in its fourth generation.

name: Masahiro Kikuno
tagline: Hand-made Japanese temporal-hour watches and tourbillons, built without CNC
summary: Masahiro Kikuno is a Japanese independent watchmaker and AHCI member known for reinterpreting traditional Japanese timekeeping, above all the wadokei temporal-hour watch, whose hour markers move with the seasons. For years he made almost every part by hand without CNC machines.
history:
Masahiro Kikuno was born in 1983 in Hokkaido. He studied at the Hiko Mizuno College of Jewelry in Tokyo, completing its WOSTEP-linked watchmaking course between 2005 and 2008, and began building complicated watches entirely by hand, using manual lathes and files rather than computer-controlled machines.

His early works, a tourbillon and a perpetual calendar tourbillon, caught the attention of the Académie Horlogère des Créateurs Indépendants (AHCI); he became a candidate in 2011 and a full member in 2013. In 2011 he also unveiled the Wadokei, a wristwatch rendering of the Japanese temporal-hour system, in which daytime and night-time are each divided into six units whose length changes through the year. Its hand-painted indices shift automatically, spreading out in summer daytime and contracting in winter.

Later pieces include Orizuru (2013), Mokume (2014) with a mokume-gane pattern, several unique 'Wadokei Revision' pieces, and Sakubou (2017), a moon phase in a kuro-shibuichi and white gold case accurate to one day in 122 years and made at only four pieces a year. In 2025 he presented Complication 'inherit', a minute repeater, chronograph and tourbillon inspired by George Daniels, and his first watch made with CNC assistance.

name: Maurice Lacroix
tagline: Swiss watches from the Jura, home of the Aikon
summary: Maurice Lacroix is a Swiss brand created in 1975 by the trading company Desco von Schulthess and majority-owned by DKSH since 2011. Its integrated-bracelet Aikon is one of the best-selling watches in its price range, alongside the complicated Masterpiece line.
history:
Maurice Lacroix was launched in 1975 by Desco von Schulthess, a Zurich-based trading company that had been distributing watches and components and decided to create its own brand. The name was borrowed from a respected former company executive. Production was based in the Jura village of Saignelégier, where the company had taken over a watch assembly workshop, and the first watches were quartz and simple mechanical designs sold mainly in Europe.

The brand grew steadily through the 1980s and 1990s with accessible dress and sports watches. In 1990 it introduced the Calypso, a sports watch with an integrated bracelet and a bezel with six 'claws', which would later inspire the Aikon. The Masterpiece line, launched in the early 1990s, became the platform for more ambitious mechanical watches and complications.

In 2006 Maurice Lacroix presented its first in-house movement, the ML106 chronograph calibre, and began building a manufacture in the Jura, later adding eye-catching complications such as the Roue Carrée with square and cloverleaf-shaped wheels and a mysterious seconds display. In 2011 the Swiss market-expansion group DKSH, which had grown out of Desco von Schulthess, acquired a majority stake. DKSH has repeatedly explored a sale of the brand.

The Aikon, launched in 2016, transformed the company's fortunes. Its integrated bracelet and claw bezel offered a sport-luxury look at a fraction of the price of more famous designs, and the line expanded to automatics, chronographs, skeletons, ultra-thin models and the Aikon #tide made from recycled ocean plastic. Today the company is headquartered in Zurich with production in the Jura.

name: MB&F
tagline: Maximilian Büsser & Friends: kinetic sculptures that happen to tell time
summary: MB&F is a Geneva-based 'horological concept laboratory' founded by Maximilian Büsser in 2005, creating Horological Machines inspired by sci-fi, animals and machines alongside the more classical Legacy Machines. It collaborates with independent watchmakers and designers, and Chanel took a 25% stake in 2024.
history:
Maximilian Büsser spent seven years at Jaeger-LeCoultre and then ran Harry Winston's watch division, where he created the Opus series of collaborations with independent watchmakers. In 2005 he left to found MB&F - Maximilian Büsser & Friends - an 'artistic and micro-engineering laboratory' that would design watches with a rotating cast of freelance talents.

The first piece, Horological Machine N°1 (2007), with its figure-eight case and four barrels, set the tone. It was followed by the HM2, the dome-eyed HM3 and its 'Frog' version, the jet-inspired HM4 Thunderbolt, the Space Pirate HM6 and the jellyfish-like HM7 Aquapod. In 2011 the Legacy Machine N°1 introduced a more traditional round line with a flying balance suspended above the dial, a homage to 19th-century watchmaking; the LM Perpetual, developed with Stephen McDonnell, won a GPHG prize.

MB&F opened the M.A.D. Gallery in Geneva in 2011 for mechanical art and later the lower-priced M.A.D. Editions (M.A.D.1 in 2021). The company reported sales of about CHF 45 million in 2023 from 419 MB&F Machines and roughly 3,500 M.A.D. Editions watches.

In August 2024 Chanel acquired a 25% stake, with Büsser keeping 60% and partner Serge Kriknoff 15%. The brand marked its 20th anniversary in 2025 with the LM101 EVO and limited Legacy Machine editions.

name: Memorigin
tagline: Hong Kong's tourbillon-only brand, mixing Chinese culture and pop-culture tie-ins
summary: Memorigin is a Hong Kong brand founded in 2011 that makes only tourbillon watches, at prices far below Swiss equivalents. It combines Chinese artistic motifs with a long list of licensed collaborations, from Star Wars and Marvel to Bruce Lee and Kamen Rider.
history:
Memorigin (Chinese name 萬希泉, 'a fountain of hopes for the masses') was founded in Hong Kong in 2011 by William Shum, who started the business after completing a master's degree at Cornell University. Drawing on his family's appreciation of Chinese woodcarving, he set out to create Hong Kong's first tourbillon watch brand, making the complication accessible and designing pieces as heirlooms to be passed from father to son.

Memorigin's watches all feature tourbillons, many of them flying tourbillons in openworked dials, with cultural themes such as dragons, the Chinese zodiac and traditional instruments. The brand became widely known through licensed collaborations with Warner Bros. (Batman), Disney (Marvel's Avengers and Star Wars), the Bruce Lee Foundation (2018), Kamen Rider and, in 2026, Stephen Chow's Kung Fu Soccer, plus athletes including Michael Owen and LaMelo Ball.

Its current collections are grouped into Cultural, Timeless, Glamorous and Seamless series, and the brand also offers bespoke tourbillon commissions. Movement materials are sourced from Europe, and the brand says pieces undergo international testing before release. Designs range from classical pieces such as the Eternal Blue, with a silver clous de Paris dial, blue Roman numerals and an 80-hour reserve, to openworked cushion-shaped and luminous carbon-fibre models.

name: Michael Kors
tagline: Jet-set glamour on the wrist: the defining gold-tone fashion watch of the 2010s
summary: Michael Kors is the New York fashion label whose oversized, gold-tone chronographs and pavé-set ladies' watches became a global bestseller after Fossil Group began producing them under licence in 2004. The brand is owned by Capri Holdings, and Fossil's watch and jewellery licence has been extended through 2027.
history:
American designer Michael Kors (born Karl Anderson Jr.) launched his womenswear label in New York in 1981, selling to department stores such as Bergdorf Goodman. The business went through bankruptcy in 1993 before relaunching with lower-priced lines, while Kors also served as creative director of the French house Céline from 1997 to 2004 and later became a household name as a judge on Project Runway.

In April 2004 Michael Kors signed an exclusive watch licence with Fossil, the Texas-based fashion-watch giant. Fossil's design and distribution machine paired perfectly with Kors's jet-set aesthetic of oversized cases, gold-tone steel, chronograph sub-dials and crystal-set bezels. Collections such as Runway, Lexington, Parker and Darci became ubiquitous in department stores and airports worldwide, and by the early 2010s Michael Kors was one of the bestselling watch brands in markets such as the UK and US. Fossil added the fashion jewellery licence in 2010, and the pair renewed their agreement for ten years in 2014.

Michael Kors Holdings went public in 2011, bought Jimmy Choo in 2017 and Versace in 2018, and renamed itself Capri Holdings. As the fashion-watch category shrank in the late 2010s, Fossil also produced Michael Kors Access smartwatches. A proposed takeover of Capri by Tapestry was blocked in 2024, and in 2025 Capri sold Versace. In February 2025 Fossil and Michael Kors extended their licensing partnership through 2027, continuing a relationship of more than twenty years.

name: Mido
tagline: 'I measure': Swiss chronometers inspired by architecture
summary: Mido is a Swatch Group brand founded in Biel in 1918, known for robust automatic watches, many COSC-certified, inspired by architecture. Its Ocean Star divers, Multifort and Commander lines offer strong value.
history:
Georges G. Schaeren founded Mido in Biel/Bienne in 1918, choosing a name from the Spanish 'Yo mido', meaning 'I measure'. In the 1920s Mido became known for colourful, shaped Art Deco watches and for novelty designs such as watches shaped like car radiator grilles for brands including Bugatti and Buick.

The company focused on durability. In 1934 it launched the Multifort, a self-winding watch that was also antimagnetic, shock-resistant and water-resistant, qualities then rarely combined. Mido also developed the Aquadura crown-sealing system, which uses natural cork to seal the winding stem against water. The Ocean Star arrived in 1944 as a water-resistant sports watch and later became Mido's diving line, and in 1959 Mido launched the Commander, with a monobloc case, which was produced continuously for decades.

Like many Swiss firms, Mido was hit by the quartz crisis. It joined ASUAG's General Watch Co. in 1971 and became part of the Swatch Group through the 1983 merger of ASUAG and SSIH. Within the group it was positioned as a mechanical-watch specialist at accessible prices, with a particular following in Latin America and Asia.

Since the 2000s Mido has built its identity around architecture, drawing inspiration from landmarks such as the Golden Gate Bridge, the Colosseum and the Sydney Opera House for its Multifort, Baroncelli, Commander and Ocean Star designs. It became one of the largest producers of COSC-certified chronometers and uses Swatch Group movements such as the Caliber 80 with an 80-hour power reserve and silicon balance spring. Mido is headquartered in Le Locle.

name: Minase
tagline: Case-in-case construction and Sallaz polish from a village in snowy Akita
summary: Minase is a small Japanese luxury brand created by precision-tool and watch-case maker Kyowa in the mountains of Akita. It is known for its patented 'case in case' architecture, where the dial and movement float inside a sapphire-windowed outer shell, and for mirror-sharp Sallaz (Zaratsu) polishing.
history:
Minase's parent company, Kyowa Co., Ltd., was founded in 1963 as a maker of precision cutting drills in Akita Prefecture. From the 1960s it expanded into manufacturing watch cases for both mass-market and high-end watch brands, and by 1996 it had become a full watch manufacturer capable of design, development and production.

In 2005 Kyowa launched its own brand, named after the village of Minase where its workshop sits, a remote, snowy area the company likes to compare with Switzerland's Vallée de Joux. The first watches formed the Master Craft series. In 2011 it completed the HiZ series, which codified the brand's three signatures: Sallaz hand-polishing, the modular 'case in case' construction inspired by Japanese three-dimensional puzzles, and the MORE (Minase Original Rebuild Equation) concept, meant to make every part replaceable so a watch can last a century.

Collections such as the Divido, the architectural 7 Windows and the square Horizon use Swiss ETA 2892A2-based movements finished in-house, while the Mastercraft line features traditional Japanese crafts such as urushi lacquer. Minase makes fewer than 500 watches a year. Delivery typically takes around three months because of the limited, hand-finished production.

name: MING
tagline: Design-first watches from photographer Ming Thein's collector-founded brand
summary: MING was founded in 2017 by photographer and designer Ming Thein with a group of watch-enthusiast friends. Known for layered sapphire dials, inventive lume and quick-change straps at accessible prices, its 37.09 Bluefin won the Sports Watch Prize at the 2024 GPHG.
history:
Ming Thein, a Malaysian photographer, designer and watch collector, launched MING in 2017 together with a small group of fellow collectors. The idea was a design-first brand that would use high-quality Swiss-made components and movements while pushing aesthetics through unusual materials, layered and textured sapphire dials and distinctive luminous treatments.

The first model, the 17.01, sold out quickly and set the template: tightly controlled limited editions, often sold in online drops, with prices well below traditional Swiss independents. Later lines included chronographs, a hand-wound 'monopusher' range, and more complex pieces made with partners such as Schwarz Etienne and J.N. Shapiro. The brand operates as Horologer MING, a Swiss watchmaker, with a globally distributed team.

MING's 37-series dive and sports watches brought the brand to a wider public: the 37.09 Bluefin, a 600m diver with lume embedded in its sapphire, won the Sports Watch Prize at the 2024 Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Genève. Recent releases include the 37.11 Odyssey GMT and the 57.05 Comet worldtimer. The brand has built an unusually engaged online community, and its limited editions typically sell out quickly, with deliveries planned in batches. Its watches pair Swiss-made Sellita-based or partner movements with in-house design.

name: Mondaine
tagline: The Swiss railway clock, shrunk down for the wrist
summary: Mondaine is a family-owned Swiss watch company founded in 1951 by Erwin Bernheim, best known for its Official Swiss Railways watches based on Hans Hilfiker's iconic SBB station clock. The Mondaine Group also owns Luminox.
history:
Mondaine was established in 1951 by Swiss businessman Erwin Bernheim after he took over the Neuchâtel Watch company, originally founded in 1928. For its first decades the company produced affordable watches for other brands and private labels, benefiting from the rise of quartz technology.

The turning point came in 1986, when Mondaine obtained the commercial licence from the Swiss Federal Railways (SBB) to use the design of the Swiss railway clock. Created in 1944 by SBB engineer Hans Hilfiker, the clock face with its bold black batons and red 'lollipop' seconds hand is a design icon that appears in museums worldwide. Mondaine's Official Swiss Railways watches translated the design to the wrist and became the brand's signature. The station clocks famously sweep the seconds hand round in 58 seconds and pause at 12 for about two seconds while awaiting a central signal; in 2013 Mondaine launched the stop2go, whose movement recreates that stop at 12.

In 2012 Apple used the railway clock design in iOS 6, leading to a licensing agreement between SBB and Apple. Mondaine has broadened its line-up with the evo2, the Simply Elegant, the Helvetica range inspired by the typeface, the automatic 'Original' and the sustainable 'essence' line using bio-sourced materials. The group became sole owner of Luminox in 2016 and also holds watch licences such as Pierre Cardin. It remains owned by the Bernheim family.

name: Montblanc
tagline: The pen house whose watches draw on Minerva's Swiss heritage
summary: Montblanc, the German writing-instrument and leather-goods maison owned by Richemont, has made watches since 1997 in Le Locle and, since 2006, at the historic Minerva manufacture in Villeret. Its 1858 line draws on Minerva's mountaineering and military chronographs.
history:
Montblanc was founded in Germany in 1906 as the Simplo Filler Pen Company by stationer Claus-Johannes Voss, banker Alfred Nehemias and engineer August Eberstein. It adopted the Montblanc name, after Europe's highest peak, for its pens around 1910, added the white snowcap emblem in 1913 and in 1924 launched the Meisterstück fountain pen that became its icon. The company is based in Hamburg.

In 1977 Alfred Dunhill Ltd acquired Montblanc, and in 1993 it became part of the Vendôme group, now Richemont. Diversifying beyond pens, Montblanc entered watchmaking in 1997 with Montblanc Montre SA in Le Locle, producing well-finished watches at accessible luxury prices.

The decisive step came in 2006, when Richemont acquired Minerva, a Villeret manufacture founded in 1858 and famed for its chronograph movements. Montblanc created the Institut Minerva de Recherche en Haute Horlogerie there to preserve traditional craft, and in 2008 launched the in-house Nicolas Rieussec monopusher chronograph, named after the inventor credited with an early chronograph. Villeret went on to produce high complications such as the ExoTourbillon and Metamorphosis.

Today Montblanc's watch catalogue centres on the 1858 collection, inspired by Minerva's vintage mountaineering and military watches, including the Geosphere world-timer and the Iced Sea divers with dials textured like glacier ice; the Star Legacy and Heritage dress lines; and the high-end Minerva pieces. Montblanc remains one of the few luxury houses to span pens, leather goods and serious watchmaking.

name: Moritz Grossmann
tagline: A 19th-century Glashütte master's name revived for exquisite hand-finished watches
summary: Moritz Grossmann is a small Glashütte manufacture founded in 2008 by watchmaker Christine Hutter, reviving the name of 19th-century horologist Carl Moritz Grossmann. It produces only a few hundred highly finished watches a year, noted for hand-annealed brown-violet hands and traditional Saxon movement architecture.
history:
Carl Moritz Grossmann (1826–1885) was one of the founding figures of Glashütte watchmaking. Born in Dresden, he trained in Switzerland, England and France before opening his own workshop in Glashütte in 1854 at the encouragement of his friend Ferdinand Adolph Lange. He won prizes for his writing on escapements, was elected to the Saxon parliament and initiated the German School of Watchmaking in Glashütte in 1878. After his sudden death in 1885 his business was wound up.

More than a century later, Christine Hutter, a trained watchmaker who had worked for Wempe, Maurice Lacroix, Glashütte Original and A. Lange & Söhne, acquired the rights to the dormant name and founded Grossmann Uhren GmbH on 11 November 2008, at the height of the financial crisis.

The first watch, the Benu, launched in 2010, followed by a purpose-built manufacture in Glashütte completed in 2013. The brand quickly earned critical acclaim for movements with untreated German silver plates, pillar construction and a manually operated stop-seconds mechanism, and for signature hand-crafted hands annealed to a brown-violet colour.

Moritz Grossmann has since expanded with the Tefnut, Atum and Hamatic lines and several tourbillons, including the Benu Tourbillon, notable for using a human hair in its stop-seconds brake. Production remains tiny, at roughly 200 watches a year, making it one of the most exclusive Glashütte houses.
knownFor: Hand-annealed brown-violet hands and traditionally finished Glashütte movements

2013: Benu Tourbillon stop-seconds mechanism using a fine brush of human hair on the balance rim
2019: Hamatic pendulum automatic winding, a revival of an early hammer-winding principle

name: Movado
tagline: 'Always in motion': home of the minimalist Museum dial
summary: Movado is a Swiss-founded brand now owned by the US-based Movado Group, famous for the minimalist Museum dial with a single dot at 12 o'clock. It sells mainly quartz fashion-luxury watches such as the Museum Classic and Bold.
history:
Movado's roots go back to 1881, when 19-year-old Achille Ditesheim opened a watchmaking workshop in La Chaux-de-Fonds. His brothers Léopold and Isidore joined him, and in 1892 the firm became L.A. & I. Ditesheim, one of the area's first modern watch factories. Around 1905 it adopted the name Movado, Esperanto for 'always in motion'.

Movado was an innovative Swiss maker in the first half of the 20th century. In 1912 it introduced the Polyplan, a curved rectangular watch whose movement was built on three levels to fit the curve of the wrist, and in the 1920s and 30s it made the Ermeto, a purse watch wound by opening and closing its sliding case. Movado chronographs and calendar watches were widely admired.

In 1947 American designer Nathan George Horwitt created a dial with no numerals, only a single dot at 12 o'clock representing the sun at noon. Movado adopted it, and in 1960 the Museum of Modern Art in New York added Horwitt's design to its permanent collection, giving the Museum Watch its name. In 1969 Movado joined Zenith and Mondia in a holding company, and the Datron automatic chronograph used the El Primero movement.

In 1983 the North American Watch Corporation, founded by Cuban-born entrepreneur Gedalio Grinberg, bought Movado; the parent company later took the name Movado Group and is headquartered in Paramus, New Jersey, led by the founder's son Efraim Grinberg. Movado Group also owns Ebel, Olivia Burton and MVMT and holds licences for fashion brands. Today the Movado brand focuses on quartz Museum Classic and Bold watches sold in department stores and its own outlets.

knownFor: The Museum dial with a single dot at 12
innovations: 1912: Polyplan, curved watch with a movement on three levels
1947: Museum dial by Nathan George Horwitt, later in MoMA's collection
