name: Sinn
tagline: Frankfurt's engineering-led tool watches, tested for pilots, divers and astronauts
summary: Sinn Spezialuhren is a Frankfurt-based maker of instrument watches famous for proprietary technologies such as Tegiment hardening, Ar-Dehumidifying Technology and submarine-steel cases. Its pilot, diving and mission-timer watches are prized for robustness and value.
history:
Helmut Sinn, a former pilot and flight instructor, founded Sinn Spezialuhren in Frankfurt am Main in 1961. The company initially specialised in pilot's chronographs and cockpit clocks, selling directly to customers to keep prices down. Its watches earned credibility with professional aviators and, in 1985, German astronaut Reinhard Furrer wore a Sinn 140 S on the Spacelab D1 mission, making it the first automatic chronograph used in space.

In 1994 Helmut Sinn sold the business to engineer Lothar Schmidt, who had previously worked at IWC. Schmidt transformed Sinn into a technology-driven company, introducing innovations like the lubricant-free DIAPAL escapement, oil-filled HYDRO technology, Ar-Dehumidifying Technology to keep dials fog-free, and Tegiment surface hardening for scratch-resistant cases and bezels. The U1, launched in 2005, was the first watch made from German submarine steel.

Sinn continues to produce mission timers for German police special units (the EZM series) and has its watches independently tested and certified, including to the DIN 8330 pilot watch standard and by DNV for dive watches. Helmut Sinn died in 2018 at the age of 101. The company remains independent and family-run by the Schmidt family, with its own case manufacture, SUG, in Glashütte.

name: Skagen
tagline: Ultra-thin Danish minimalism on a steel mesh bracelet
summary: Skagen is a Danish-inspired minimalist watch brand founded in 1989 by Henrik and Charlotte Jorst and named after Denmark's northernmost town. Famous for slim cases, clean stick-marker dials and Milanese mesh bracelets, it has been owned by Fossil Group since 2012.
history:
Skagen was founded in 1989 by Henrik and Charlotte Jorst, a Danish couple who had moved to the United States in 1986. Frustrated by the lack of simple, elegant watches in the US market, they began importing and designing slim, understated timepieces inspired by Scandinavian design. The brand was named after Skagen, Denmark's northernmost town, and its logo symbolises the meeting of the Skagerrak and Kattegat seas off its coast.

The Jorsts first showed their designs at a New York corporate gift fair in 1991 and began selling under their own brand in 1992, with about US$800,000 in first-year sales. Department stores including Bloomingdale's picked up the line in the mid-1990s, and ultra-thin steel watches on fine Milanese mesh bracelets became Skagen's signature. Sales approached US$30 million by 1998 and around US$70 million by 2005, as Skagen opened offices in Denmark and Hong Kong and expanded into jewellery. In 2010 its model 233 steel watch and Swiss Movement 585 series won Red Dot design awards.

In 2012 Fossil Group acquired Skagen Designs for roughly US$237 million, bringing it alongside Fossil's own brand as a house-owned label rather than a licence. Under Fossil, Skagen extended into hybrid and touchscreen smartwatches with the Falster and Jorn lines, while core analogue collections such as Signatur, Grenen, Ancher and Holst continued the brand's clean, Danish-inspired look. Skagen remains part of Fossil Group, which restructured its debt in 2025, and continues to use the Nordic coastline as its design muse.

name: Speake-Marin
tagline: English-founded Geneva independent known for the Piccadilly case and heart-shaped hands
summary: Speake-Marin was founded in 2002 by English watchmaker Peter Speake-Marin and is now run from Geneva under CEO Christelle Rosnoblet. It is recognised by its stepped Piccadilly case, heart-shaped 'topping tool' hands, and in-house micro-rotor calibres, with the Ripples integrated sports watch as its modern hit.
history:
Peter Speake-Marin trained in England and cut his teeth restoring antique watches at a firm in London's Piccadilly, then moved to Switzerland, where he worked at complication specialist Renaud et Papi. In 2002 he launched his own brand in Bursins, Vaud, with the Piccadilly, a watch with a distinctive stepped case and hands whose heart-shaped tips were inspired by a watchmaker's topping tool.

The brand developed its in-house SM2 calibre around 2009 for the Marin 1, and later produced tourbillons, minute repeaters and the Renaissance minute-repeater tourbillon, while Speake-Marin himself consulted for houses such as Harry Winston, MB&F and Maîtres du Temps. In 2017 the founder left the company that bore his name; Christelle Rosnoblet, an administrator since 2012, became CEO, and the headquarters moved to Geneva in 2019.

Under the new leadership the brand broadened its range with the Ripples integrated-bracelet sports watch, the Openworked collection with sandblasted skeletonised movements, and the Piccadilly-cased Resilience with grand feu enamel dials, powered by the in-house SMA03 micro-rotor calibre. The atelier says thirteen manufacture movements have been developed over its history. Its heart-shaped hands and stepped case remain the brand's most recognisable signatures.

name: Spinnaker
tagline: Affordable automatic divers named after the pioneers of underwater exploration
summary: Spinnaker is an affordable dive-watch brand whose collections, such as Fleuss, Bradner, Piccard and Spence, are named after pioneers of diving and ocean exploration. It offers Japanese automatic divers with sapphire crystals at a few hundred dollars and is known for a steady stream of colourful limited editions and pop-culture collaborations.
history:
Spinnaker positions itself as a tribute to 'a life beneath, beyond and beside the sea', drawing on the golden age of diving and the daring spirit of early underwater pioneers. Each core collection is named after a figure from diving history: the Fleuss honours Henry Fleuss, whose 19th-century closed-circuit rebreather was a milestone in underwater breathing apparatus; the Bradner references Hugh Bradner, the physicist credited with inventing the modern wetsuit; and the Piccard nods to the Piccard family of deep-sea and stratospheric explorers. Other lines include the Spence, Hull, Croft, Cahill, Dumas, Challenger and Tesei.

The brand's formula is to put vintage-inspired dive-watch design, 316L steel cases, sapphire crystals, Swiss Super-LumiNova and Japanese Miyota or Seiko automatic movements into watches typically priced between about US$300 and US$600. Signature pieces include the Bradner, with its vintage proportions and bi-directional bezel; the Fleuss, a cushion-cased diver later reworked in a slimmer 40mm size; and the Spence 300, engineered to be only 11.5mm thick while offering 300m of water resistance.

Spinnaker is part of the Dartmouth Brands portfolio of affordable watch brands. In recent years it has become known for frequent limited editions and licensed collaborations with properties such as SpongeBob SquarePants, Popeye and Peanuts' Snoopy, as well as ocean-conservation partnerships with organisations including 4ocean and the Dolphin Project. It sells direct online worldwide and through retailers, with a two-year international warranty.

name: Squale
tagline: Professional dive watches and case maker to the industry since 1959
summary: Squale (French for 'shark') is a Swiss dive-watch brand founded by Charles von Büren in Neuchâtel, whose cases were once supplied to other famous brands. Owned by the Italian Maggi family since the 1980s and headquartered in Ticino, it is best known for the 50 Atmos 1521 with its crown at 4 o'clock.
history:
Charles and Hélène von Büren established a watchmaking business in Neuchâtel around 1948, specialising in dive watches, and in 1959 registered the Squale trademark along with an early patent for the production of diving watch cases. Squale's case expertise made it a supplier to other brands, and its robust divers found favour with professionals. In 1965 Italian freediver Enzo Maiorca set a world record at 67 metres wearing a Squale Master.

The 1970s were Squale's heyday. The 50 Atmos model reference 1521, with its crown at 4 o'clock and distinctive orange minute hand, became the brand's icon, and Squale became official supplier to the Italian Navy and the Folgore paratroopers brigade. Italy became its most important market, where the Maggi family acted as distributor.

As Charles von Büren prepared for retirement, he sold the brand in 1982 to the Maggi family, who had worked closely with the company. The quartz era was difficult, but in 2005 the Maggis relaunched Squale and restarted production of its classic references, including the 1521, the Squalematic and the 1545. The modern range has broadened with the vintage-sized Sub-39 and Sub-37, the Super-Squale, the T-183 and numerous collaborations. In 2020 Squale moved its headquarters from Milan to Chiasso in Switzerland's Ticino canton, and it sponsors freediver Vincenzo Ferri. Squale remains a favourite among enthusiasts seeking professional-grade Swiss divers at approachable prices.

name: Stowa
tagline: Original wartime Flieger maker turned direct-to-consumer Bauhaus and pilot specialist
summary: Stowa, founded by Walter Storz in 1927, was one of the five original makers of the German B-Uhr pilot's watch. Revived by Jörg Schauer in 1996, it sells classic Flieger, Antea and Marine watches directly online at honest prices.
history:
Walter Storz founded Stowa (from STOrz WAlter) in 1927 in Hornberg in the Black Forest and moved the business to Pforzheim, Germany's watchmaking and jewellery centre, in 1935. In the 1930s Stowa produced the Antea, a clean Bauhaus-influenced design, and during the Second World War it was one of five companies contracted to build the large Beobachtungsuhr (B-Uhr) observation watches for Luftwaffe navigators, alongside A. Lange & Söhne, Laco, Wempe and IWC.

The Pforzheim factory was destroyed in an air raid in February 1945. Storz rebuilt, and in the post-war decades Stowa made a wide range of watches including the Seatime divers of the 1960s. Walter Storz's son Werner took over, but like much of the German industry the company struggled through the quartz era.

In 1996 Jörg Schauer, a Pforzheim-area watchmaker known for his own robust watches, acquired Stowa. He rebuilt the brand around faithful reinterpretations of its historic designs and became one of the first watch companies to sell primarily online direct to customers, keeping prices low. Stowa is now based in Engelsbrand near Pforzheim, where it assembles watches with Swiss movements and offers the Flieger, Antea, Marine, Partitio and Seatime lines.

name: Studio Underd0g
tagline: Watermelons, pizza and mechanical chronographs: British watchmaking with a sense of humour
summary: Studio Underd0g is a British microbrand founded by designer Richard Benc in 2020 and launched on Kickstarter in 2021. Famous for playful fruit- and dessert-themed dials on affordable mechanical chronographs, it has grown into one of the most recognisable independent brands, collaborating with H. Moser & Cie. and opening its own assembly facility, the D0ghouse.
history:
Designer Richard Benc developed Studio Underd0g during the 2020 COVID-19 lockdown, aiming to 'inject a bit of silliness' into an industry he saw as overly serious. The brand launched on Kickstarter in March 2021 with the 01Series, a 38.5mm manual-wind chronograph using the Seagull ST19 movement with 1940s-style pushers and dials in playful colourways such as Watermel0n, Desert Sky and Go0fy Panda, priced from about £325. The campaign reached its target within an hour.

The brand's zero-for-O naming, food-inspired dials and cheeky marketing built a devoted following. The 02Series of October 2023, a 37.5mm time-only watch with Studio Underd0g's first Swiss movement and a signature multi-layer sapphire dial, generated more than £1.8 million in sales in a nine-hour window. Collaborations followed with Time+Tide on pizza-themed watches, with Christopher Ward and Massena LAB, and, most surprisingly, with H. Moser & Cie. in 2024, pairing a Moser perpetual calendar with the first Underd0g monopusher chronograph in a US$64,900 'Passion Fruit' set. The monopusher 03Series became the brand's premium line, and a 2024 exclusive deal with Seagull underpinned a third-generation 01Series.

In December 2025 Studio Underd0g acquired its long-time British assembly workshop, renaming it Underd0g Manufacture and lifting capacity to more than 14,000 watches a year. In May 2026 it opened the D0ghouse in Maidenhead, a working facility where visitors can assemble their own watch, marking a shift from a virtual start-up to a British manufacturer with its own watchmakers.

name: Swatch
tagline: The plastic 'second watch' that saved Swiss watchmaking
summary: Swatch launched in 1983 as a low-cost, 51-part plastic quartz watch that revived the Swiss industry after the quartz crisis and became a global pop-culture phenomenon. The flagship brand of the Swatch Group, it scored another sensation in 2022 with the Omega x Swatch MoonSwatch.
history:
By the early 1980s the Swiss watch industry had been devastated by cheap Japanese and Hong Kong quartz watches. At ETA, part of the struggling ASUAG group, managing director Ernst Thomke tasked engineers Elmar Mock and Jacques Müller with creating a radically cheap Swiss watch. Their design used just 51 parts, a plastic case into which the movement was directly built, and ultrasonically welded construction that made it impossible to repair but cheap to mass-produce. The name was a contraction of 'second watch'.

The first twelve Swatch models were launched on 1 March 1983 in Zurich at around 50 Swiss francs. Backed by bold marketing and a fashion-driven approach of new seasonal collections, Swatch became an instant hit, and Nicolas G. Hayek, who engineered the merger of ASUAG and SSIH into SMH (renamed the Swatch Group in 1998), made it the engine of the Swiss recovery. Artist collaborations with Keith Haring, Kiki Picasso and others, the Pop Swatch, Chrono, Scuba, Irony metal watches and the ultra-thin Skin kept the brand in the spotlight, and Swatch collecting became a craze.

In 2013 the brand launched the Sistem51, the first mechanical movement with fully automated assembly, again using just 51 parts. In 2020 Swatch introduced bio-sourced plastics, then bioceramic. The March 2022 Omega x Swatch MoonSwatch, a bioceramic take on the Speedmaster, caused queues around the world, and in 2023 the Blancpain x Swatch Scuba Fifty Fathoms followed. Swatch remains headquartered in Biel/Bienne, with Nick Hayek Jr. leading the group.

name: Swiss Military Hanowa
tagline: Officially licensed 'Swiss Military' watches at accessible prices
summary: Swiss Military Hanowa is the watch brand of Hanowa AG, founded in 1963 in Biel by Hans Noll. Launched in 1990 and an official licensee of the Swiss Confederation, it sells sporty, military-inspired Swiss-made watches at entry-level prices worldwide.
history:
Hanowa was founded in 1963 in Biel/Bienne by Hans Noll and his wife Elisabeth Wirz, two years after Noll had taken over the sales management of a watch factory in the town. The company name was formed from the first letters of the founder's name, HAns NOll, and 'WAtch'. Hanowa built a business producing affordable Swiss watches for international distribution, and survived the quartz era by embracing quartz movements and value pricing.

In 1990 the company launched a second brand, Swiss Military Hanowa, drawing on the values associated with the Swiss armed forces: robustness, endurance and reliability. The brand's watches carry the Swiss cross, and since 2015 Hanowa has been an official licensee of the Swiss Confederation, allowing it to market products under the 'Swiss Military' name. The company later moved its headquarters from Biel to Möhlin in the canton of Aargau.

Swiss Military Hanowa's catalogue is large and varied, from simple quartz watches such as the Flagship Heritage to chronographs, ceramic-bezel sports pieces like the Sidewinder, aviation-themed Avia models and automatic divers including the Maître Plongeur. Positioned well below mainstream Swiss mid-range brands, it sells through department stores, military exchanges and online retailers across Europe, the Middle East and Asia, and it marked its 60th anniversary in 2023.

name: TAG Heuer
tagline: Avant-garde Swiss chronographs with deep roots in motor racing
summary: TAG Heuer is LVMH's high-volume sports-luxury brand, built on Heuer's pioneering stopwatches and chronographs. The Carrera and square Monaco are motor-racing icons, backed by long partnerships in Formula 1 and motorsport.
history:
Edouard Heuer opened a watchmaking workshop in Saint-Imier in 1860 and moved to Biel in 1867. In 1887 he patented the oscillating pinion, a clutch system still used in many mechanical chronographs. The company built its reputation on precision timing: the 1916 Mikrograph measured 1/100th of a second, and Heuer stopwatches timed the 1920, 1924 and 1928 Olympic Games.

Under Jack Heuer, great-grandson of the founder, the brand became synonymous with motor racing. The Carrera, named after the Carrera Panamericana road race, arrived in 1963, followed by the Autavia and, in 1969, the square, waterproof Monaco, one of the first automatic chronographs thanks to the Calibre 11 developed with Breitling, Hamilton-Büren and Dubois Dépraz. Steve McQueen wore a Monaco in the 1971 film Le Mans, and Heuer timed Ferrari's F1 team in the 1970s.

The quartz crisis left Heuer struggling, and in 1985 it was acquired by Techniques d'Avant Garde (TAG), a Luxembourg-based holding of the Ojjeh family, becoming TAG Heuer. The 1980s and 90s brought accessible sports watches such as the Formula 1 and a long partnership with McLaren. LVMH bought the company in 1999.

In the 2010s TAG Heuer launched in-house chronograph movements, notably the Heuer 01 and Heuer 02, and in 2015 the Connected smartwatch. Since 2020 it has refocused on its heritage, with the glassbox Carrera and the TH20-00 movement, and returned as official timekeeper of Formula 1 in 2025. It is headquartered in La Chaux-de-Fonds.

name: Technos
tagline: A Swiss name that became Brazil's watch: Latin America's biggest watchmaker
summary: Technos began in 1900 as a Swiss watchmaker in Welschenrohr, Solothurn, but its brand rights passed to Brazil, where it is now the flagship of Grupo Technos, the largest watch company in Latin America. Assembled in Manaus, its watches, led by the iconic Skydiver diver, are among the most familiar in Brazil.
history:
Technos traces its roots to 1900, when Melchior Gunzinger founded a watch company in Welschenrohr in the Swiss canton of Solothurn. His son Joseph took over in 1920, renaming the business Gunzinger Bros Ltd and registering the Technos trademark in 1924. The company exported widely, and in the 1950s Technos watches arrived in Brazil, where an exclusive distributor, Importadora Centauro, founded in 1956, built the brand into a household name. Technos celebrates 1958 as the year of its arrival in Brazil.

In Switzerland the firm moved to Biel/Bienne in 1977 and changed hands several times during the quartz-crisis era, passing to General Watch Co. in 1970 and to the Japanese importer Heiwado in 1982. Meanwhile the Brazilian business opened an assembly plant in the Manaus free-trade zone in 1982. In the 1990s the Brazilian company acquired the Technos rights for South America, and in 2002 the remaining worldwide rights, making Technos a fully Brazilian brand. The Skydiver, a dive watch first introduced in the 1960s, became its icon, and the 1986 Skydiver Anadigi, combining analogue hands with a digital display, became a Brazilian classic.

Grupo Technos went public in 2011 and built a multi-brand portfolio including Mormaii, Euro, Condor, Mariner, Allora, Touch and Dumont, plus licensed and distributed brands such as Fossil and Michael Kors. It launched e-commerce and its own stores in the 2010s and connected watches from 2015. Today the group, headquartered in Rio de Janeiro with production in Manaus, describes itself as the largest watch company in Latin America, producing around a million watches a year, and in 2026 celebrated 40 years of the Skydiver Anadigi.

name: Timex
tagline: It takes a licking and keeps on ticking: America's everyman watch since 1854
summary: Timex traces its roots to the Waterbury Clock Company, founded in Connecticut in 1854, and became the watch that put a timepiece on nearly every American wrist. Today Timex Group, still based in Connecticut, sells everything from $60 Weekenders and Ironman digitals to Marlin reissues and Giorgio Galli-designed automatics.
history:
Timex's story begins in 1854 in Waterbury, Connecticut, the 'Brass City', where the Waterbury Clock Company was founded as an offshoot of brass maker Benedict & Burnham. Its mass-production know-how made cheap, reliable timepieces possible, including the famous one-dollar Ingersoll 'Yankee' pocket watch of the 1890s, and Waterbury was also making wristwatches for soldiers by the First World War.

The company was nearly bankrupt in the Depression before Norwegian shipping magnate Thomas Olsen and engineer Joakim Lehmkuhl took control, reorganising it as the U.S. Time Corporation. In 1950 it launched the Timex brand: cheap, sturdy pin-lever watches sold in drugstores and promoted with TV 'torture tests' hosted by John Cameron Swayze, with the slogan 'It takes a licking and keeps on ticking.' By the 1960s about one in every two watches sold in the US was a Timex.

Timex survived the quartz and digital upheavals by moving into electronics, releasing the Ironman Triathlon sports watch in 1986, the Indiglo electroluminescent backlight in 1992 and the Data Link computer-linked watch with Microsoft in 1994. Now Timex Group B.V., still privately controlled by the Olsen family and headquartered in Middlebury, Connecticut, has recently won over enthusiasts with vintage reissues such as the Q Timex and Marlin, the Giorgio Galli S1 automatic and titanium Expedition and Marlin models.

name: Tissot
tagline: Swiss watches for everyone, from Le Locle since 1853
summary: Tissot is the Swatch Group's high-volume, accessible Swiss brand, selling millions of watches a year. It is known for innovations such as the first mass-produced dual-time pocket watch and the T-Touch, and for the hugely popular PRX.
history:
Charles-Félicien Tissot and his son Charles-Émile founded Tissot in Le Locle in 1853, assembling watches from parts made by local craftsmen. That same year they produced what the company describes as the first mass-produced pocket watch showing two time zones. Charles-Émile travelled to Russia and the Americas to sell the watches, and Russia became a major market; Tissot supplied watches to the Russian Imperial court.

In 1930 Tissot introduced one of the first antimagnetic wristwatches and in the same year merged with Omega to form SSIH, the Société Suisse pour l'Industrie Horlogère. Tissot became SSIH's more affordable brand. It experimented widely: the Navigator world-time watch of 1953, the Sideral of 1971 with a fibreglass case, and the Astrolon or IDEA 2001 of 1971, the first mechanical watch with a movement made largely of plastic. The quartz crisis led to the 1983 merger of SSIH and ASUAG that created the Swatch Group.

In the 1980s Tissot released unconventional materials watches such as the RockWatch in Alpine granite, WoodWatch and PearlWatch. In 1999 came the T-Touch, a tactile-screen analogue watch with altimeter, compass and barometer, which evolved into the solar T-Touch Connect.

Tissot's volume rests on sponsorships including MotoGP, cycling and basketball and on the Powermatic 80 movement, introduced in 2013, which gave an 80-hour power reserve at mass-market prices. The 2021 PRX, based on a 1978 integrated-bracelet design, became a global hit and one of the best-selling Swiss watches of the decade. Tissot remains headquartered in Le Locle.

name: Titan
tagline: India's watch giant, from mass-market quartz to ultra-thin Edge mechanicals
summary: Titan is India's largest watchmaker and one of the world's biggest by volume, a Tata Group company that sells about 15 million watches a year across brands including Titan, Sonata and Fastrack. Its Edge line is known for ultra-thin design, and it has recently built in-house mechanical and tourbillon movements.
history:
Titan was founded on 26 July 1984 by Xerxes Desai as Titan Watches Limited, a joint venture between the Tata Group and the Tamil Nadu Industrial Development Corporation (TIDCO). A factory for quartz analogue watches was built in Hosur, Tamil Nadu, inaugurated by J.R.D. Tata, and the Titan brand launched in 1987, transforming an Indian market until then dominated by the state-owned HMT.

Titan grew quickly with design-led quartz watches and added brands for every segment: Sonata for value, Fastrack for youth (spun off as an independent brand in 2005), Raga for women and Nebula in solid gold. In 2002 it launched the Edge, a quartz watch that was among the thinnest in the world. It diversified into jewellery with Tanishq in 1994 and eyewear, and jewellery now makes up most of Titan Company's revenue. In 2011 Titan bought the Swiss brand Favre-Leuba.

Titan runs several manufacturing sites making cases, quartz and mechanical movements. It developed a 12-line 4 Hz mechanical calibre in 2015, India's first tourbillon movement in 2024 for the limited Jalsa Tourbillon, and in 2026 the Edge UltraSlim Mechanical with a 2.2 mm hand-wound calibre.

name: Tommy Hilfiger
tagline: Classic American cool in red, white and blue, on the wrist since 2001
summary: Tommy Hilfiger is the preppy American lifestyle brand founded in 1985 and owned by PVH Corp. since 2010. Its watches, launched in 2001 and designed, made and distributed under licence by Movado Group, are affordable quartz and automatic pieces with sporty, nautical and racing styling and the brand's red-white-and-blue accents.
history:
Designer Tommy Hilfiger launched his eponymous label in New York in 1985 with backing from Indian textile magnate Mohan Murjani, famously announcing himself with a Times Square billboard that placed his name alongside America's great designers. The brand's preppy, all-American style, flag logo and red, white and blue palette made it one of the defining fashion labels of the late 1980s and 1990s, embraced by hip-hop artists as well as the country-club set.

Tommy Hilfiger expanded rapidly into accessories through licensing. In 2001 Movado Group launched Tommy Hilfiger watches under an exclusive licence, and the line became one of Movado's most important licensed businesses, selling through department stores, Tommy Hilfiger stores and online worldwide. The watches are typically quartz multifunction and chronograph designs in steel, ion-plated or silicone-strapped cases, often with navy dials, red accents and nautical or motorsport details, plus a women's range of mesh-bracelet and crystal-set pieces.

The company itself changed hands several times: it was taken private by Apax Partners in 2006 and bought by PVH Corp., owner of Calvin Klein, for about US$3 billion in 2010, with its global headquarters now in Amsterdam. Movado's Tommy Hilfiger watch licence has been repeatedly extended and currently runs through 31 December 2029. Recent additions include vintage racing-inspired chronographs and the TH85, a 40mm Japanese automatic with a coin-edge rotating bezel, 100m water resistance and exhibition caseback, signalling a push toward more serious watch specifications.

name: Traser
tagline: Swiss tritium-lit tactical watches born from a US Army contract
summary: Traser is the watch brand of mb-microtec, the Bern-area specialist in self-powered tritium light sources (trigalight). Created in 1989 to build a watch robust enough for the US Army, it makes affordable Swiss-made tactical, outdoor and dive watches readable in total darkness.
history:
Traser is the watch brand of mb-microtec ag, a company based in Niederwangen near Bern that specialises in gaseous tritium light sources, tiny sealed glass capsules whose inner phosphor coating glows continuously thanks to the beta decay of tritium gas. The company markets this technology as 'trigalight', and it is used in instruments, gun sights and signage as well as in watches.

The traser watch brand was established in 1989 to meet a specific military requirement: a watch tough enough for the US Army that could be read at night without any external light or charging. The resulting P6500 Type 6 was issued to US forces and became one of the first self-illuminating military watches, establishing traser's reputation among soldiers, law enforcement and outdoor professionals. For a time traser also produced watches for other brands using its light sources.

Over the following decades traser built a broad range of Swiss-made watches organised into tactical, outdoor and diver collections, all built around trigalight tubes on the hands and indices, which remain visible for up to 20 years. Popular models include the P67 Officer Pro, P65 Tactical Mission, P68 Pathfinder with solar and automatic variants, the lightweight P99 Tactical Carbon and professional divers with helium valves and ceramic bezels rated to 500 metres. traser remains part of mb-microtec, positioning itself as a practical, affordable Swiss alternative for users who need guaranteed night-time legibility.

name: Tudor
tagline: Rolex's sister brand, reborn as the go-to modern tool watch
summary: Founded by Hans Wilsdorf to offer Rolex-grade reliability at a lower price, Tudor has become one of the fastest-growing Swiss brands on the strength of the vintage-inspired Black Bay and titanium Pelagos. It now makes its own movements through its sister company Kenissi.
history:
Tudor traces its origins to 1926, when the Geneva firm Veuve de Philippe Hüther registered the name 'The Tudor' on behalf of Hans Wilsdorf, the founder of Rolex. Wilsdorf took over the brand in 1936 and in 1946 created Montres Tudor SA, explaining that he wanted a watch retailers could sell at a more modest price while keeping the dependability of Rolex. Early Tudors used bought-in movements but Rolex Oyster cases, crowns and bracelets.

The Oyster Prince of 1952 was tested by the British North Greenland Expedition, and the Tudor Submariner of 1954 went on to serve with navies including the French Marine Nationale and the US Navy. In the 1970s Tudor introduced the snowflake hands on its divers and launched the Oysterdate chronographs later nicknamed 'Monte Carlo'. As the brand drifted, it withdrew from the United States in the mid-1990s.

A reinvention began in the late 2000s. The Heritage Chrono of 2010 and especially the Black Bay of 2012, which revived vintage Submariner cues such as the big crown and snowflake hands, turned Tudor into a collector favourite. The Pelagos titanium diver followed the same year and Tudor returned to the US market in 2013. In 2015 it introduced its first manufacture calibre, the MT5621, and in 2016 set up Kenissi to produce movements for itself and other brands such as Breitling, Chanel and Norqain.

The Black Bay Fifty-Eight of 2018, sized at 39mm, became a modern classic, and in 2023 the Black Bay received METAS Master Chronometer certification. Tudor now sits alongside Rolex under the Hans Wilsdorf Foundation, with independent design and its own headquarters in Geneva, offering Swiss-made tool watches mainly between roughly $3,000 and $7,000.

name: Tutima
tagline: Glashütte pilot-chronograph pioneer that returned home after six decades in the West
summary: Tutima traces its roots to UROFA and UFAG, founded in Glashütte in 1927, whose 1941 Flieger chronograph became a German aviation icon. After decades in Ganderkesee near Bremen, the family-owned brand returned to Glashütte in 2011 and now makes in-house calibres including a minute repeater.
history:
In 1927, amid economic crisis in Glashütte, two companies were founded under the chairmanship of Dr. Ernst Kurtz: UROFA (Uhren-Rohwerke-Fabrik Glashütte AG), which made movements, and UFAG (Uhrenfabrik Glashütte AG), which made finished watches. Their best-quality watches carried the name Tutima, from the Latin 'tutus' for safe or secure. In 1941 the company produced the Tutima Flieger chronograph with calibre 59, a robust flyback chronograph issued to German pilots and now a highly collectible piece.

At the end of the Second World War, Ernst Kurtz left Glashütte for West Germany, and the Tutima name continued in Lower Saxony. The brand was later carried on by Dieter Delecate, and Tutima became based in Ganderkesee near Bremen. In 1984 Tutima supplied the Military Chronograph (NATO Chronograph) to the German Air Force, cementing its reputation for tool watches.

In 2011 Tutima returned to Glashütte, opening a new manufacture and presenting the Hommage minute repeater, followed by the in-house manual-wind calibre 617 in the Patria line. The brand remains owned by the Delecate family and offers pilot's watches, the M2 professional line, the Saxon One sport chronographs and the Patria dress watches.

name: Ulysse Nardin
tagline: Le Locle's marine-chronometer maker turned pioneer of silicon and the Freak
summary: Founded in Le Locle in 1846, Ulysse Nardin built its fame on marine chronometers used by dozens of navies. Revived in the 1980s with astronomical watches and the radical Freak, it pioneered silicon components and is now independent alongside Girard-Perregaux in the Sowind Group.
history:
Ulysse Nardin founded his company in Le Locle in 1846, specialising in precision pocket watches and, above all, marine chronometers. His son Paul-David Nardin expanded the business, and the firm's chronometers won thousands of awards at observatory competitions and international exhibitions. At one point Ulysse Nardin marine chronometers equipped around 50 of the world's navies, and the anchor became the brand's emblem.

The quartz crisis nearly finished the company, and by 1983 it was on the verge of disappearing when Swiss entrepreneur Rolf Schnyder bought it. Schnyder partnered with the watchmaker and scholar Ludwig Oechslin, who designed the 'Trilogy of Time': the Astrolabium Galileo Galilei of 1985, the Planetarium Copernicus of 1988 and the Tellurium Johannes Kepler of 1992. Oechslin's 1996 GMT± Perpetual introduced a perpetual calendar adjustable forwards and backwards with the crown.

In 2001 Ulysse Nardin launched the Freak, a watch without dial, hands or crown in which the entire movement rotates to show the time. It used silicon for escapement components, a material the company then developed through its affiliate Sigatec, making it a pioneer of silicon technology now used across the industry. The brand also launched the Maxi Marine and Diver collections, rooted in its nautical heritage.

After Schnyder's death in 2011, the French group Kering acquired Ulysse Nardin in 2014 and later placed it alongside Girard-Perregaux in the Sowind Group. In 2022 Kering sold both brands to their management under Patrick Pruniaux. Today the brand's collections are the Freak, Diver, Marine and the angular Blast, positioning it as a technically daring independent.

name: Undone
tagline: Hong Kong's custom-made watches: design your own for a few hundred dollars
summary: Undone is a Hong Kong brand that lets customers customise affordable mechanical and mecha-quartz watches online, from dials and hands to cases and straps. It is known for vintage-inspired chronographs, the Basecamp field watch and a long list of pop-culture collaborations.
history:
Undone was founded in Hong Kong in 2014 by Michael Young, who had previously restored vintage Rolex watches and believed that true luxury meant a product made for its owner. The brand launched with 'accessible bespoke' watches: customers choose case, dial, hands, crown and strap in an online configurator, and the watch is assembled to order.

Unlike many microbrands, Undone keeps most operations in-house, including design, R&D, component manufacture and assembly, outsourcing only crystals and movements, typically Japanese Seiko/TMI NH35A automatics and mecha-quartz chronograph movements. Early hits included the Urban vintage chronographs, inspired by 1960s and 70s racing chronographs, the Aqua diver and the Basecamp tool watch with California dial options.

The brand has built a strong following through collaborations with Hello Kitty, Sanrio, Ghost in the Shell, hololive, POPEYE, the Manta Trust and the Atlassian Williams F1 team. Its range now includes the Aquadeep titanium diver, Terra, ultra-thin 4.9 mm Slim and enamel automatics. Early Basecamp models came on Cordura NATO straps, and buyers can add initials to the dial or caseback for a small fee. Watches typically sell for about $265 to $1,150.

name: Unimatic
tagline: Milanese 'design by removal' tool watches in black and matte steel
summary: Unimatic is a Milan-based microbrand founded in 2015 by industrial designers Giovanni Moro and Simone Nunziato. Its brutally minimal, 300m-rated tool watches, typically black-dialled with sandblasted or brushed steel and numbered casebacks, made it a cult favourite and a frequent collaborator with Hodinkee, Massena Lab and fashion houses.
history:
Unimatic was founded in Milan in 2015 by Giovanni Moro and Simone Nunziato, two industrial designers who wanted to apply a philosophy of 'design by removal' to the tool watch: every element had to serve a function, and anything decorative was stripped away. Their first watch, the Modello Uno, was a limited edition diver of 300 pieces with a stark black dial, pale-green lume and a matte steel case, inspired by mid-century Italian military and professional diving watches.

The brand quickly found an audience among collectors and fashion insiders alike. In 2016 Unimatic collaborated with the Paris concept store Colette and introduced the Modello Due, a 38mm time-only field-diver. The Modello Tre chrono-diver followed in 2018, and a steady run of limited editions and co-branded projects, including with Hodinkee and Massena Lab, turned new Unimatic releases into fast sell-outs. Nearly every model shares the same DNA: 300m water resistance, double-domed sapphire, a numbered screw-down caseback engraved with a 'Rosa dei Venti' compass rose, and Japanese Seiko-made movements.

In 2021 Unimatic set up its own assembly line near Milan, bringing assembly, testing and quality control in-house, and launched a permanent Classic line of individually numbered watches alongside the more technical Toolwatch series with GMT variants. In 2023 it partnered with Massena Lab on the 36mm Modello Cinque. Today Unimatic remains independent, designing and assembling its watches in Italy while continuing to release small, tightly edited limited editions.

name: Union Glashütte
tagline: Johannes Dürrstein's 1893 Glashütte name, revived by the Swatch Group
summary: Union Glashütte was founded in 1893 by Johannes Dürrstein to make fine yet affordable watches. Revived in the 1990s and part of the Swatch Group since 2000, it offers Glashütte-made mechanical watches at a lower price point than its sister brand Glashütte Original.
history:
Johannes Dürrstein, whose family firm Dürrstein & Co. already operated in Glashütte, founded the Uhrenfabrik Union in 1893 with the aim of producing high-quality watches that remained affordable. Union became known for precise pocket watches, including complicated pieces, and exported widely before the First World War.

The upheavals of the 20th century, including the world wars and the post-1945 nationalisation of Glashütte's watch industry into the state-owned GUB combine, brought the Union name to a halt for decades.

After German reunification the name was revived in the 1990s alongside the privatised Glashütte Original, and in 2000 both brands became part of the Swatch Group. Union Glashütte was positioned as the group's more accessible Glashütte brand, using Swatch Group-based automatic and manual calibres finished and assembled in Glashütte, many now fitted with silicon balance springs and long power reserves.

Unlike Glashütte Original, which builds complex manufacture calibres, Union Glashütte concentrates on reliable, well-finished everyday watches at more accessible prices.

Today the collection includes the sporty Belisar, the 1960s-inspired Noramis, the Averin and Seris, and the 1893 Johannes Dürrstein Edition, whose enamel-look dials, blued hands and railway-track chapter rings recall historic Glashütte pocket watches.

name: Universal Genève
tagline: The Polerouter and Compax maker, reborn under Breitling in 2026
summary: Universal Genève, founded in 1894, was one of the great Swiss chronograph and micro-rotor makers, creator of the Tri-Compax and the Gérald Genta-designed Polerouter. After decades of dormancy it was acquired by Breitling in 2023 and relaunched in April 2026 with a new in-house micro-rotor movement.
history:
Universal was founded in 1894 in Le Locle by Numa-Emile Descombes and Ulysse Georges Perret, and moved to Geneva in 1919, later adopting the name Universal Genève. The firm became a chronograph specialist: in 1917 it made one of the first wristwatch chronographs, in 1936 the Compur, and in 1944 the celebrated Tri-Compax, combining chronograph, triple calendar and moonphase for its 50th anniversary.

In 1954 the young Gérald Genta designed the Polerouter to commemorate Scandinavian Airlines' first commercial flights over the North Pole. From 1955 it was powered by the micro-rotor Microtor calibre, one of the first micro-rotor automatic movements, and the brand later produced the ultra-thin Golden Shadow. The 1960s Compax chronographs gained a cult following, including the 'Nina Rindt' Compax worn by the wife of racing driver Jochen Rindt.

The quartz crisis devastated the company. It changed hands several times, going to Hong Kong's Stelux group in 1977 and later to Hong Kong-based Hong Kong Boom Group in 1989, and output dwindled until the brand went effectively dormant in the 2000s. In late 2023 Breitling, controlled by Partners Group, acquired Universal Genève. After more than two years of development it relaunched on 8 April 2026 as 'Le Couturier de la Montre', with a new Polerouter powered by the UG-110 micro-rotor calibre, a Compax with the micro-rotor chronograph UG-200, the reversible Cabriolet and the Disco Mini, and a return to Geneva's Rue du Rhône.

name: Urwerk
tagline: Satellite hours and wandering time from Geneva's sci-fi watchmakers
summary: Urwerk was founded in Geneva in 1997 by watchmaker Felix Baumgartner and designer Martin Frei. Its watches replace hands with rotating 'satellite' hour cubes and cones that travel across a minute arc, in angular titanium and steel cases inspired by spacecraft.
history:
Felix Baumgartner, the son of a clock restorer, and his brother Thomas teamed up with art-school-trained designer Martin Frei in the mid-1990s. Launched at Baselworld 1997 with the UR-101 and UR-102, their company took its name from the Mesopotamian city of Ur, where early timekeeping began, combined with the German 'Werk' for movement.

The founders reinvented the 17th-century 'wandering hours' display: numerals mounted on rotating satellites sweep along a scale to indicate the minutes. Later pieces added turbine-regulated automatic winding (UR-202), linear displays inspired by an old Patek Philippe prototype (UR-CC1 King Cobra), the Zeit Device pocket watch (UR-1001) and the EMC, whose movement lets owners monitor and adjust its own rate. The UR-210 added a retrograde winding-efficiency indicator; the UR-100V (2019) became the core line; and the UR-150 Scorpion (2023) introduced a retrograde satellite.

Urwerk remains fully independent and led by its founders, producing around 200 watches a year. It also collaborated with MB&F on the C1 clock and with pop-culture projects, and in 2024 revisited its origins with the UR-102 Reloaded set. Its designs, often compared to spacecraft and sci-fi props, made Urwerk one of the defining names of avant-garde independent watchmaking.

name: Vacheron Constantin
tagline: The oldest watch manufacture in continuous operation, Geneva since 1755
summary: Founded in Geneva in 1755, Vacheron Constantin claims more than 270 years of uninterrupted production, making it the oldest continuously operating watch manufacture in the world. Part of Richemont since 1996, it is the third member of the 'Holy Trinity' and is renowned for grand complications, métiers d'art and the Overseas sports watch.
history:
Vacheron Constantin began in 1755 when 24-year-old Jean-Marc Vacheron, a master watchmaker in Geneva, took on his first apprentice, a contract that survives as the brand's birth certificate. His descendants expanded the business, and in 1819 Jacques-Barthélemy Vacheron went into partnership with the merchant François Constantin, who travelled Europe selling the firm's watches under the motto 'do better if possible, and that is always possible'.

In 1839 the company hired Georges-Auguste Leschot, whose pantograph and machine tools allowed standardised, interchangeable movement parts, an industrial breakthrough for Swiss watchmaking. The Maltese cross, derived from a component of the going barrel, was registered as the brand's emblem in 1880. Vacheron Constantin became a supplier to royalty and the wealthy, producing ornate pocket watches for King Fuad I of Egypt and the American collector James Ward Packard.

The twentieth century brought turbulence. The Depression and the quartz crisis weakened the company, which passed through the hands of the Ketterer family and, in the 1990s, Sheikh Ahmed Zaki Yamani, before being acquired by the Vendôme group, now Richemont, in 1996. Its 1977 ref. 222, an integrated-bracelet steel sports watch, paved the way for the Overseas, launched in 1996.

Under Richemont the manufacture moved to a modern headquarters in Plan-les-Ouates (2004) and returned to extreme complication. The Ref. 57260 pocket watch of 2015 featured 57 complications, the Les Cabinotiers Solaria of 2024 set a record for a wristwatch, and for its 270th anniversary in 2025 the house unveiled the Berkley Grand Complication with 63 complications. Its bespoke Les Cabinotiers department continues to create one-of-a-kind pieces for private clients.

name: Van Cleef & Arpels
tagline: Place Vendôme poetry: watches that tell time as stories
summary: Van Cleef & Arpels is a Paris high-jewellery maison founded in 1896 and owned by Richemont. Its Poetic Complications, such as the Lady Arpels Pont des Amoureux and Midnight Planétarium, use mechanical animations, enamel and gems to turn time-telling into narrative art.
history:
Van Cleef & Arpels grew out of a love story: in 1895 Alfred Van Cleef, son of a stone-cutter, married Estelle Arpels, daughter of a precious-stone dealer. The following year Alfred and Estelle's brother Charles Arpels founded the business, and in 1906 they opened a boutique at 22 Place Vendôme in Paris, where the maison remains today. Estelle's brothers Julien and Louis later joined the firm.

The house became famous for inventive jewellery. In 1933 it patented the Mystery Set, a technique in which gemstones are set without visible prongs. Around 1935 it created the Cadenas watch, a discreet bracelet watch shaped like a padlock that became a favourite of the Duchess of Windsor, and in the 1930s and 40s it produced jewellery watches and minaudières. The Alhambra four-leaf clover motif, launched in 1968, became its best-known jewellery design, and the house expanded to New York in 1939.

Family control gave way in 1999 when the Vendôme group, now Richemont, took a majority stake, completing its acquisition by 2003. Under chairman Nicolas Bos the maison developed a distinctive watchmaking identity, with workshops in Geneva. The Poetic Complications, starting with the Lady Arpels Pont des Amoureux in 2010, use retrograde and animated mechanisms to tell stories: two lovers meeting on a Paris bridge, planets orbiting the sun in the Midnight Planétarium of 2014, and flowers opening in the Lady Arpels Heures Florales.

Today Van Cleef & Arpels is one of Richemont's most profitable jewellery maisons, and its watches, many produced in small series with enamel and gem-setting, are regularly awarded at the Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Genève.

name: Venezianico
tagline: Venetian art and architecture translated into accessible mechanical watches
summary: Venezianico is an Italian independent brand founded in late 2017 by brothers Alberto and Alessandro Morelli, based near Venice in San Donà di Piave. Its collections, named after Venetian landmarks, blend value-driven automatic watches with ambitious craft pieces, and in 2025 it unveiled the V5000, its first proprietary Italian-made movement.
history:
Brothers Alberto and Alessandro Morelli founded Venezianico in late 2017 while studying at Venice's Ca' Foscari University, combining a passion for watchmaking and design with their deep attachment to the city. The brand's logo was inspired by a detail they noticed while walking through St Mark's Square: the golden Renaissance cross atop the ancient Clock Tower, a symbol of the passage of time in Venice. Each collection takes its name and cues from Venetian history, architecture and the lagoon.

The Redentore, named after Andrea Palladio's Basilica del Redentore, is the brand's elegant everyday line in 36mm and 40mm, while the Nereide, named after the sea nymphs of myth, is a sporty 200m diver with a sunray dial, crystal-insert bezel and integrated 'Canova' bracelet. The Arsenale, named after the historic Venetian shipyards, is an integrated-bracelet sports watch with knurled bezel and exotic dials such as mother-of-pearl and meteorite, and the Bucintoro evokes the ceremonial galley of the Doges. Venezianico built a large following by offering Japanese automatic movements, sapphire crystals and striking dials at approachable prices, alongside a steady stream of limited editions and collaborations with retailers across Asia.

In 2025 Venezianico introduced the V5000, its first proprietary mechanical calibre, designed with and manufactured in Italy by OISA, a hand-wound 3.5Hz movement with 60 hours of power reserve. It debuted in the limited Redentore Utopia and powers the Grade 5 titanium Redentore Levius, whose Zefiro guilloché dial is hand-engraved on an 1850 rose engine. The company is headquartered in the Palazzo Baradel atelier in San Donà di Piave and aims to become Italy's reference name in watchmaking.

name: Victorinox
tagline: The Swiss Army Knife maker's tough, accessible Swiss watches
summary: Victorinox, founded in 1884 by Karl Elsener and famous for the Swiss Army Knife, entered watches in 1989 under the 'Swiss Army' name. Its watches, led by the ultra-tough I.N.O.X., offer Swiss-made quality at accessible prices and are sold worldwide.
history:
Victorinox began in 1884 when Karl Elsener opened a cutlery workshop in Ibach, in the canton of Schwyz. In 1891 the company began supplying knives to the Swiss Army, and the multi-tool 'Officer's Knife' that followed became the world-famous Swiss Army Knife. The company name, adopted in 1921, combines the name of Elsener's mother Victoria with 'inox', the term for stainless steel.

Victorinox entered the watch business in 1989 in the United States, where watches were sold under the 'Swiss Army' brand through the distributor Swiss Army Brands. The watches, often styled after field and military pieces with a Swiss cross logo, became popular affordable Swiss-made timepieces through the 1990s. In 2001 Victorinox established Victorinox Swiss Army Watch AG and took full control of the watch business in 2002. In 2005 it acquired its long-time rival Wenger, which also had a watch line.

Victorinox watches emphasise durability and value. The I.N.O.X., launched in 2014, was put through more than 100 extreme tests, including being run over by a tank and dropped from height, and became the flagship of the range, later extended in titanium, carbon and mechanical versions. Other collections include the FieldForce, Journey 1884, Alliance and Dive Pro. The company remains controlled by Elsener family foundations and is led by Carl Elsener Jr., with around 90% of its production exported to more than 100 countries.

name: Vortic
tagline: Antique American pocket-watch movements reborn as Colorado-built wristwatches
summary: Vortic Watch Company, founded in 2013 in Fort Collins, Colorado, turns restored antique American pocket-watch movements into one-of-a-kind wristwatches. It is also known for winning a landmark trademark case brought by Swatch Group's Hamilton.
history:
Vortic was founded in 2013 by R.T. Custer and Tyler Wolfe, who met as students and wanted to build watches in the United States. Their idea was to rescue movements from antique American pocket watches made by companies such as Elgin, Waltham, Illinois and Hamilton, restore them and fit them into new wristwatch cases. A Kickstarter campaign in 2014 raised about $41,000 and launched the business in Fort Collins.

In 2015 Hamilton, owned by Swatch Group, sued Vortic and Custer personally, alleging counterfeiting and trademark infringement because some restored movements bore the Hamilton name. After a five-year fight, a US federal judge ruled in Vortic's favour on all counts in September 2020, affirming the right to restore and resell antique watches with their original markings. The case became a notable precedent for upcycling.

Vortic makes a few hundred watches a year, each unique, in series named after the cities of the original makers, plus an annual Military Edition built around US Army Air Corps pocket watches, and it offers conversions of customers' heirloom watches. It also launched the sister brand Colorado Watch Company. In June 2025 Custer suffered a major stroke; his wife Lindsay Roselle has run the company as interim CEO during his recovery.

name: Vostok
tagline: Chistopol's Soviet military watchmaker behind the Komandirskie and Amphibia
summary: Vostok is made by the Chistopol Watch Factory in Tatarstan, established in 1942 when a Moscow watch plant was evacuated during the Second World War. Its Komandirskie military watches and ingeniously sealed Amphibia divers are among the cheapest in-house mechanical watches in the world.
history:
In 1941–42, as German forces approached Moscow, the Second Moscow Watch Factory was evacuated to the small Volga town of Chistopol in Tatarstan. The relocated plant began producing watches and military instruments for the Red Army, and after the war it stayed in Chistopol, becoming the Chistopol Watch Factory, which adopted the Vostok ('East') brand name in the 1960s.

Vostok became a major supplier to the Soviet Ministry of Defence. In 1965 it introduced the Komandirskie ('commander's') watch for officers, and in 1967 the Amphibia, a dive watch rated to 200 m that uses a clever sealing design in which water pressure pushes the crystal and caseback more tightly against their gaskets. Its sturdy, simple in-house movements, including the 2409 manual and 2415/2416 automatics, earned a reputation for reliability.

After the collapse of the Soviet Union the factory was privatised and faced repeated financial difficulties, but it continued making its own movements and cases. Vostok watches became a cult favourite among Western enthusiasts thanks to their low prices, endless dial variants and ease of modification. In 2017 the factory marked the 50th anniversary of the Amphibia with a 1967-style reissue, and it continues to produce Amphibia, Komandirskie and special editions today.

name: Vulcain
tagline: The Cricket, the mechanical alarm watch of American presidents
summary: Vulcain is a Swiss watchmaker founded in 1858 in La Chaux-de-Fonds and best known for the Cricket, launched in 1947 as one of the first practical mechanical alarm wristwatches. Worn by several US presidents, it has been relaunched since 2021 under Guillaume Laidet's leadership.
history:
Vulcain traces its origins to 1858, when Maurice Ditisheim began making watches in La Chaux-de-Fonds; the Vulcain name was registered in 1894 by the Ditisheim family firm. The company made precision pocket watches and chronographs and exhibited at world's fairs, earning medals for complicated pieces.

Its defining moment came in 1947 with the Cricket, one of the first mechanical alarm wristwatches loud enough to be genuinely useful, thanks to a double membrane and resonance chamber in the caseback. The alarm was likened to a cricket's chirp. In 1953 President Harry Truman received a Cricket, and the watch became associated with the White House, worn or owned by Presidents Eisenhower, Nixon and Lyndon Johnson; the company later branded it 'the watch of presidents'. Vulcain also built the Cricket Nautical of 1961, a dive watch with an alarm designed to warn divers of decompression stops.

The quartz crisis hit Vulcain hard and ownership changed several times, including a period under Swiss watch groups in the 1970s and 1980s. The brand was revived in 2002 and moved to Le Locle, where it continued producing its in-house alarm calibres in small quantities, but it struggled commercially. Around 2021 revival specialist Guillaume Laidet, known for Nivada Grenchen, began working with the Luxembourg-based owners, expanding the watchmaking team and dealer network and relaunching the Cricket Classique, Cricket Tradition and President lines alongside Skindiver and 1970s-style chronographs.

name: Waltham
tagline: America's first watch factory, inventor of mass production, reborn in Switzerland
summary: The Waltham Watch Company, founded in 1850 in Massachusetts, pioneered the 'American System' of making watches with interchangeable machine-made parts and produced around 40 million timepieces before its US factory closed in 1957. The brand lives on through its Swiss offshoot, now based in Mendrisio, which makes modern mechanical watches such as the Field & Marine Dual Time.
history:
Waltham began in 1850 when Aaron Lufkin Dennison, with Edward Howard and David Davis, set out to make watches by machine rather than by hand. After starting near Boston, the company moved in 1854 to Waltham, Massachusetts, on the Charles River. There it perfected what became known as the American System of Watch Manufacturing, using precision machinery to make interchangeable parts. The approach shocked Swiss makers when Waltham's watches beat them at the 1876 Philadelphia Centennial Exhibition.

Waltham became one of the largest watchmakers in the world. Its pocket watches, from the affordable William Ellery, the model Abraham Lincoln owned, to the railroad-grade Vanguard and Crescent Street, set the standard for American railways. It made wristwatches for soldiers in the First World War, aircraft clocks and, during the Second World War, military watches such as the A-11 and A-17 alongside Elgin and Bulova.

After the war, cheap imports and management problems pushed Waltham into bankruptcy in 1949, and US watch production ended in 1957. A Swiss subsidiary, Waltham International SA, created in 1954, kept the trademark outside North America. Italian-American businessman Antonio DiBenedetto took majority control in 2011, and the Swiss-made brand, now headquartered in Mendrisio, relaunched with pilot's watches such as the Aeronaval line and, more recently, the Field & Marine Dual Time based on a 1918 waterproof design. The original factory buildings are preserved as a historic district, and the company's archives are held at Harvard Business School.

name: Weiss Watch Company
tagline: A one-watchmaker revival of American field-watch manufacturing, now in Nashville
summary: Weiss is a small independent brand founded in 2013 by watchmaker Cameron Weiss, who hand-assembles field watches with a high proportion of American-made parts. Originally based in Los Angeles, the company moved to Nashville, Tennessee in 2020.
history:
Cameron Weiss trained as a watchmaker in the United States and Switzerland, earning WOSTEP certification, before founding Weiss Watch Company in Los Angeles in 2013 with his wife Whitney. His goal was to bring back small-scale American watchmaking, and his first Standard Issue Field Watches paired simple military-inspired dials with an increasing share of parts machined in the US.

The brand grew a loyal following as one of the few American companies making cases, dials and movement parts domestically rather than just assembling imported kits. Its watches were sold directly to customers and assembled, regulated and tested by hand in small batches.

In 2020 Weiss and his family moved the company to Nashville, citing the city's creative community and the local manufacturing base that serves the aerospace and automotive industries. They bought a building in the Wedgewood-Houston neighbourhood, and in 2024 opened a Nashville studio and boutique where collectors can see the workshop. The current lineup is built around 38 mm and 42 mm automatic Standard Issue Field Watches with matching date wheels, plus limited titanium and textured-dial editions. Weiss watches are sold mainly direct to customers, which lets the company keep production small and personal.

name: Withings
tagline: French health-tech firm whose hybrid watches hide medical sensors behind real hands
summary: Withings, founded in 2008 near Paris, makes connected health devices and is best known in watches for hybrid smartwatches that look like classic analog watches. Its Activité and ScanWatch lines add step counting, heart-rhythm and blood-oxygen sensing behind physical hands.
history:
Éric Carreel, Cédric Hutchings and Fred Potter founded Withings in June 2008 in Issy-les-Moulineaux, just outside Paris. Its first hit was a Wi-Fi bathroom scale, followed by connected blood-pressure monitors, thermometers and sleep trackers.

In 2014 Withings launched the Activité, a Swiss-made analog watch with a hidden activity tracker and a sub-dial showing progress toward a step goal; it was described as the first smartwatch to look like a traditional wristwatch. Nokia bought the company in 2016 and rebranded its products under the Nokia name, but in 2018 co-founder Éric Carreel bought it back and restored the Withings brand.

Independent again, Withings launched the ScanWatch in 2020, a hybrid watch with a small digital screen and sensors for ECG and blood-oxygen readings aimed at detecting atrial fibrillation and signs of sleep apnoea. It has since added the ScanWatch 2 with temperature sensing (2023), the cheaper ScanWatch Light (2024) and the dive-style ScanWatch Nova, alongside devices such as ECG-equipped smart scales and a home urine analyser. Several Withings devices have received medical clearances, reflecting the company's focus on health data rather than apps and notifications.

name: Yema
tagline: French tool-watch maker behind the Superman diver and the first French watch in space
summary: Yema was founded in Besançon in 1948 and became France's leading watch exporter, known for the 1963 Superman dive watch and the Rallygraf and Navygraf lines. Now based in Morteau, it has revived its heritage models and developed its own CMM micro-rotor and automatic calibres.
history:
Henry-Louis Belmont founded Yema in Besançon in 1948. The brand grew rapidly in the 1950s and 1960s with robust sports watches, becoming one of France's largest watch exporters. Its best-known model, the Superman dive watch of 1963, featured a patented bezel-lock system secured by the crown guard, and was adopted by divers and French military users. Yema also produced the Rallygraf chronograph for motorsport, the Navygraf diver and the Yachtingraf regatta timers.

In 1982 French astronaut Jean-Loup Chrétien wore a Yema Spationaute during the Soviet-French Soyuz T-6 mission, making it the first French watch in space. The same year the company was acquired by Matra, and in 1988 it was sold to Japan's Hattori Seiko group.

In 2009 Yema was bought by Montres Ambre, a family watch group based in Morteau on the French-Swiss border, which moved the brand there. Over the following decade Yema relaunched its heritage icons through successful crowdfunding campaigns and, from 2021, introduced its own movements developed under the Manufacture Morteau banner: the CMM.20 micro-rotor calibre, followed by the CMM.10 automatic, the CMM.29 slim micro-rotor and even a tourbillon. Today Yema offers everything from affordable meca-quartz Rallygrafs to chronometer-precision Supermans, with official partnerships including the French Navy.

name: Zenith
tagline: Home of the El Primero, the high-beat automatic chronograph
summary: Zenith is an LVMH-owned manufacture in Le Locle whose El Primero, unveiled in 1969, was among the first automatic chronograph movements and beats at 36,000 vph. Its Chronomaster and Defy collections carry that high-frequency heritage.
history:
Georges Favre-Jacot founded his watchmaking business in Le Locle in 1865, aged 22, and was among the first to gather the many crafts of watchmaking under one roof in a true manufacture. His pocket-watch calibre named Zenith, launched at the end of the 19th century, was so successful that the company adopted the name in 1911. Zenith became a prolific winner of observatory chronometry prizes and supplied pilots' watches and instruments.

On 10 January 1969 Zenith announced the El Primero, an integrated automatic chronograph movement beating at 36,000 vibrations per hour and able to measure tenths of a second. It was one of the first automatic chronograph calibres, launched in the same year as the Calibre 11 of Heuer and Breitling and Seiko's 6139.

The quartz crisis nearly ended the story. In the 1970s Zenith was owned by the American Zenith Radio Corporation, which ordered mechanical production to be stopped. Workshop head Charles Vermot secretly hid the El Primero tools, plans and cams in an attic, allowing production to restart in the 1980s. From 1988 a modified El Primero powered the Rolex Cosmograph Daytona until 2000.

LVMH bought Zenith in 1999. After a flamboyant period under Thierry Nataf, Jean-Claude Biver and then Julien Tornare refocused the brand on its heritage, and in 2017 Zenith launched the Defy El Primero 21, measuring 1/100th of a second, and the Defy Lab with a silicon monolithic oscillator. Today the Chronomaster Sport, Chronomaster Original, Defy Skyline and Pilot lines are made in the historic Le Locle manufacture.

name: Zodiac
tagline: Sea Wolf dive watches since 1953, now under Fossil
summary: Zodiac was founded in Le Locle in 1882 by Ariste Calame and is best known for the 1953 Sea Wolf, one of the first purpose-built dive watches, and the colourful Super Sea Wolf. Owned by Fossil Group since 2001, it has faced uncertainty after Fossil's 2025 restructuring, though Fossil named it one of its core brands.
history:
Zodiac was established in 1882 in Le Locle by Ariste Calame; the Zodiac name was registered in 1908, and Calame's son Louis Ariste Calame took over in 1895 after attending watchmaking school. In 1930 the company introduced the Autographic, a self-winding watch with power-reserve indicator, unbreakable crystal and radium dial.

In 1953 Zodiac launched the Sea Wolf, one of the first purpose-built dive watches for the consumer market, appearing in the same year as the Blancpain Fifty Fathoms and Rolex Submariner. The 1960 Aerospace GMT extended the design to air travel, and in the late 1960s the Astrographic displayed time with 'floating' hands on transparent discs. The early-1970s Super Sea Wolf, with a larger case rated for greater depths, was supplied to the US Navy SEALs and other military users, and its bright dials and bezels made it a 1970s icon.

The quartz crisis brought Zodiac to its knees and it changed hands several times before Fossil acquired it in 2001 for about $4.7 million. Fossil used Zodiac as its Swiss-made mechanical brand, with watches powered by movements from Fossil's STP subsidiary, and relaunched the Sea Wolf and Super Sea Wolf in 2015 with vintage-inspired designs, followed by colourful limited editions, the Olympos and the Aerospace GMT. In October 2025 Fossil Group filed for Chapter 15 protection as part of a restructuring, and heavy discounting followed, but Fossil identified Zodiac, alongside Skagen and Relic, as a core brand it intends to keep.
